Under matched evaluator, comparison protocol, group size, prompt schedule, and query budget, \ours{} requires no additional evaluator queries beyond the observed comparisons within each rollout group and improves over Pairwise-GRPO across controlled comparisons, transfer settings, and blind human evaluations.

title: When Protection Overrides Consequences: Understanding Protection Mode in Large Language Model Decision-Making
summary: Frontier language models excel at complex tasks yet may prioritize protection over larger physical consequences in simple, urgent decisions. GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, moves a girl playing in shallow water before retrieving a submerged camera. We call this Protection Mode and study it with ProtectionBench: 285 prompts, 34 physical families, and nine models. At lowest effort, at least one of four responses prioritizes the subject on 34.74% of Sol prompts and over 83% of MiniMax M3 and Qwen3.5-27B prompts; none of four independent human raters does so. Controls show that choices usually track physical risk. We elicit both risks before requesting an action. Some models assess risk incorrectly; others state the correct ordering but still choose the subject. Qwen3.5-27B with thinking shows 100% correct risk ordering but 57.81% subject choice among eligible conversations on eight selected scenes. Attention audits find no stable reduction in attention to relevant facts; removing the stated risk direction reduces object-first choice in dots3-note-prev but not detectably in Qwen3.5-27B. Adding a general "people or animals before property" rule increases subject choice by 19-38 percentage points, whereas factual reminders favor the object by 0.7-5.2 points. Removing naturally generated versions of that rule lowers subject choice by 10-15 points. We also examine whether post-training introduces this pattern. Base models already show Protection Mode; post-training changes justifications more than choices.

title: Where Should the Gaussians Go? Reusable Label-Aware Allocation for Budget-Constrained Gaussian Splatting of Cinematic CT
summary: Anatomical labels help 3D Gaussian splatting preserve vessels in cinematic renderings of CT, but the representation is still found by optimising each patient's scene, where densification decides where Gaussians go, while real-time displays cap their number. We address one part of this process: deciding where a fixed budget of B Gaussians should be placed. We propose a reusable, labelaware allocation front end that maps a patient's CT, labels and transfer function to a density over 2mm cells and draws exactly B positions from it without per-patient optimisation; the other Gaussian attributes are still fitted per patient. The front end is learned once from per-patient optimised scenes and implemented as a population-trained neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF). With identical attribute fitting on 20 held-out patients at 10K-100K Gaussians, both raise vessel-masked PSNR over uniform allocation by 4.5-7.1dB and over pruning a dense voxel-aligned model by 1.6-3.3dB. The neural prior does not differ significantly from per-patient optimised allocation at any budget, and VACF is within 0.6dB of it on vessels; on 19 external patients the neural prior again matches it on vessels and VACF is within 0.7dB. As an initialisation for position optimisation, VACF allocation beats per-patient densification on vessels at 10K Gaussians and, at 25K, reaches a higher vessel PSNR after 118s of optimisation than densification after 248s. Under altered rendering presets, VACF transfers to new colours and lighting but not to a label-free transfer function, whereas the neural prior shows the opposite pattern.

title: Where to Start, How to Move: Analyzing Curricula under GRPO for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) provides no reward-relative learning signal when all rollouts receive identical rewards. In long-horizon tasks that require multiple interactions, rewards are given only upon successful task completion, making all-fail groups common early in training and limiting opportunities to practice later steps. Guide Assisted GRPO replays a successful reference prefix before the learner continues. We study how initial positions, handoff units, and movement rules affect unassisted task completion. Across three model sizes on BFCL, starting near completion is more effective under a fixed turn-level threshold rule. Finer handoffs alone do not consistently help, but outcome-informed tool-call selection outperforms GRPO on trained and untrained task categories. Guided starts also improve AppWorld success on both evaluation splits. These findings highlight where learning starts and how starting positions move as key curriculum choices.

title: Which Knowledge Should LLMs Trust? Uncovering a Generalizable Steering Direction Across Knowledge Conflicts
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently encounter conflicts between internal parametric knowledge and external contextual knowledge, yet the mechanisms governing this selection remain unclear. We show that the choice between context and parametric knowledge is linearly represented and can be controlled along a single direction in the model's residual stream. We first demonstrate that this direction generalizes across factual-conflict settings, including context formats, knowledge categories, and datasets, while consistently shifting behavior between parametric and contextual answers. We then transfer a direction learned from simple factual conflicts to three more complex task families: RAG, memory, and rule following, where models must acquire information from retrieved documents, interaction histories, or explicit rules. Across four model families and multiple transfer settings, steering consistently improves the use of prompt-provided information over the unsteered model. These results suggest that the direction captures a transferable preference for external knowledge rather than a mechanism specific to factual conflicts.

title: Who Should We Listen to More? Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition for Pluralistic Alignment
summary: Pluralistic alignment needs to accommodate diverse preferences under limited human feedback. Using AI simulators to label preference comparisons reduces annotation costs, but variation in simulation accuracy across individuals can leave some people's preferences poorly represented in training. We study how to allocate human feedback across people to construct training data for pluralistic alignment, and how this allocation affects the trained policy. To make this allocation explicit and controllable, we define a social welfare objective over individual supervision utilities that measure label quality. Each query's marginal welfare gain depends on its expected supervision improvement, the recipient's current utility, and application-designated priority. Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition (WAPA) uses auxiliary reference models to estimate query gains and individual utilities, then selects queries by estimated marginal welfare gain while updating recipient utilities. We prove exact optimality of the acquisition algorithm for the estimated welfare objective under a fixed query budget and model predictions. Experiments on six Roleplay collections and four OpinionQA regions demonstrate improved supervision and controllable allocation tradeoffs. Policy training on four Roleplay collections improves preference prediction for both seen and unseen individuals. When prioritizing a designated group and poorly represented individuals, acquiring human labels for 20% of comparisons recovers 75-86% of the average predictive utility gap between policies trained entirely on AI-generated labels and entirely on ground-truth labels.

title: Who's Behind the Text? Robust Model Authorship Attribution
summary: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate text, their misuse has become a growing societal problem, with implications for academic misconduct, model distillation, and cyberattacks. For these reasons, Model Authorship Attribution (MAA), which identifies the source model of a given text, is important for promoting the responsible use of LLMs and improving AI safety. In practice, attribution systems must remain reliable beyond the distributions observed during training. They may encounter texts from unseen domains and writing settings, as well as generations from future versions of model families that were not available when the system was trained. However, existing MAA methods often exhibit substantial performance degradation under such distribution shifts. To address this challenge, we propose Authorship Tracing via Likelihood-based Attribution of Sources (ATLAS), which formulates MAA through source-conditioned text modeling rather than direct source prediction. ATLAS learns how text from each source family is generated and attributes a given text by comparing its likelihood under each learned source condition. We aggregate this likelihood evidence at the token level with clipping so that no single token dominates the decision. We further introduce MAABench, a broad MAA benchmark for evaluating practical OOD settings such as domain and version. Our experiments show that ATLAS consistently outperforms existing baselines across MAABench and OpenTuringBench. In particular, when both the generation domain and the model version change on MAABench, ATLAS achieves 74.27% accuracy, 9.00pp higher than the strongest baseline. Beyond MAA, ATLAS can also help identify distillation source models by measuring which source model a target LLM most closely resembles. Our extended experiments show that ATLAS recovers the known teacher of every distilled model we evaluate.

title: Whose Data, Whose Benchmark? A User-Centric Framework for Auditing Evaluation Resources
summary: Benchmarks shape how model capabilities are measured and interpreted, yet their scores can obscure whose conventions, contexts, and judgments define successful performance. We introduce a user-centric audit framework that distinguishes users who contribute benchmark content from those whose needs evaluation results are intended to represent. The framework operationalizes seven dimensions across benchmark content, metadata, documentation, and scoring procedures. Across 16 resources, we find that American-centered conventions account for 62.4-94.4% of matched signals in 11 text benchmarks, while geographic visibility in five image-text resources is concentrated and strongly associated with national GDP share (mean Pearson r = 0.780; Spearman p = 0.778). Documentation reveals a systematic source-target gap: all 16 resources operationalize source-user context, but none operationalize target-user context. Paired scoring experiments further show that meaning-preserving answer variants reduce DROP exact-match accuracy from 100.0% to 33.3%, while TruthfulQA exhibits metric-dependent reductions in reference similarity. Our framework and documentation checklist make user assumptions auditable, clarifying what benchmark scores represent and where evaluation claims are supported.

title: Whose turn is it? Context-guided model routing for stateful agents
summary: Model routing can reduce the cost of LLM applications by assigning simpler requests to cheaper models without sacrificing the quality of the response. However, most routers treat requests as independent. Stateful agents do not operate under this assumption: a user turn may require multiple model and tool calls, its difficulty depends on the state produced by earlier turns, and changing models can sacrifice reuse of the conversational prompt cache. We study zero-shot, cost-aware routing at the user-turn boundary, systematically varying the routing rule, access to session history, candidate models that differ in size, reasoning effort, or model provider, and prompt-cache behavior. We evaluate on multi-turn versions of SheetCopilot and SpreadsheetBench 2, where persistent workbooks and cross-turn dependencies make isolated routing decisions especially brittle. At a matched offloading rate, giving the router session history improves task pass rate over the same router without history, with gains for every model pair; history-aware routing remains within one point of always using the expensive model. We also found that cost depends on execution dynamics rather than token prices alone: the cheaper model's per-task cost advantage narrows from 6.8x to 3.2x on longer sessions. A closed form cache analysis further shows that downward switches (expensive to cheap) recover their cache cost within two LLM calls, whereas upward switches do not break even under the evaluated conditions. Together, these results show that agent routing is a sequential decision problem: effective policies must account for what happened earlier in the session and for the asymmetric cost of switching models.

title: Why Do Agent Teams Fail Across Boundaries? A Failure Taxonomy for Agent-to-Agent Systems with Private States
summary: Agents are increasingly interacting with other agents that act for different principals (people or organizations on whose behalf they work), such as a buyer's personal agent negotiating with an enterprise's seller agent. In such agent-to-agent (A2A) scenarios, each agent has its own environment and holds information and authority that the other cannot see. Moreover, the interests of each agent may be aligned (cooperative), partly aligned (mixed-motive), or opposed (competitive). Existing multi-agent system failure studies assume one orchestrator, shared workspace, or single principal. We ask how A2A systems fail when these assumptions are removed. We study more than 2,500 recorded runs of A2A systems built from different agent harnesses and models, spanning 488 scenarios across eight families (legal, CRM, security, commerce, etc.). From these traces, we derive $A^2$-Failures, a taxonomy of 20 A2A failure modes in four categories: (i) discovery and delegation, (ii) grounding and record consistency, (iii) verification, and (iv) conduct and fidelity. Three findings hold across every harness, model, and scenario studied: (1) discovery and interaction are driven by the phrasing of the task rather than the availability of peer agents; (2) no agent verifies a peer's factual claim on its own initiative, so an A2A system inherits the reliability of its least reliable participant unless the protocol or mechanism performs the check; and (3) the aggregate outcome score credits the agent completing the task while staying blind to the coordination, verification, and conduct failures beneath it, so A2A systems must be evaluated per agent, against each agent's own principal. We release the run logs behind the taxonomy at https://huggingface.co/datasets/a2a-salesforce/a2-failures.

title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
summary: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

title: Why don't Graph Transformers attend to the same token?
summary: In large language models (LLMs), attention concentrates heavily on the first token. This 'attention sink' is believed to protect deep models against over-mixing. Even though graph transformers face a related pressure, we find that a SoTA graph transformer, GRIT, rarely forms sinks on molecules, and that it sinks less when trained on larger graphs, the opposite of the trend in LLMs. In principle, a graph can prevent sinks: we prove and show empirically that its symmetry and locality limit the attention any node can receive. On molecules, however, with distinguishable atoms and global attention, neither limit prevents sinks; what stops them lies in the model. We find that the attention scoring function is the main cause. Replacing GRIT's gated logit with a dot product raises its sink rate from 0.09 to 0.68 on identical graphs. In Graph Transformers using dot-product attention, removing the sink gives about the same error as removing a random node, while GRIT's most-attended nodes matter to its predictions. Attention sinks are therefore a property of dot-product attention rather than of Transformers. In our experiments, they form when dot-product scoring has a distinguishable node to concentrate on.

title: WinARDet: Compressed Window Auto-Regression for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Grounding
summary: MLLM-based detectors formulate vision-language grounding as autoregressive coordinate generation, yet in dense scenes, they often collapse into a box repetition loop, repeatedly emitting identical boxes until the decoding budget is exhausted. We trace this failure to historical-answer attention takeover: Under full-history autoregression, repeated coordinate tokens in the growing answer history attract disproportionate attention, crowding out the attention sinks needed to attend to new visual evidence. % To break this loop, in this paper, we propose \textbf{Compressed Window Auto-Regression} (WinAR). This new mechanism partitions a long answer sequence into consecutive generation windows and restricts full token-level autoregression to the current window only while compressing each previous window into a fixed set of latent tokens that condition subsequent decoding. This design reduces the repeated exposure to raw historical coordinates that triggers the attention takeover, yet preserves cross-window dependencies essential for coherent multi-object generation. On RSDense, which contains 200-2,000 objects per image, our model WinARDet improves RexOmni F1-score (IoU=0.5) from 32.16 to 39.36 over the baseline, while reducing the redundancy rate from 35.48% to 13.00%. WinARDet also generalizes across decoding strategies and output formats, including parallel box decoding and polygon generation, providing a practical paradigm for long-horizon vision-language grounding across scene densities.

title: Write Once, Plan Many: Building Reusable Visual Planning Systems from One Scene
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can reason about visual planning tasks, but querying them for every instance incurs repeated inference cost and latency. Generating reusable planning programs offers an alternative, but constructing reliable planning systems for new problem domains without extensive supervision remains challenging. We present a training-free framework that constructs reusable perception and planning programs from a domain specification and a single practice scene without a paired solution. The central challenge is obtaining useful feedback from the limited input. Our framework addresses it by leveraging VLM's ability to provide a renderer and a dynamic model based on its scene understanding. Rendering detected states enables comparison with the practice scene, while checking simulated action outcomes against the domain specification helps expose errors in rule implementation. Together, these checks guide refinement of the grounding program and planner without requiring solution labels. After refinement and component selection, the programs are frozen and solve new instances without further VLM calls. The same framework constructs systems across domains without manual pipeline redesign. Across fifteen domain variants spanning 2D and 3D scenes with discrete and continuous state, our systems achieve 99.3% average planning success, compared with 80.9% for the strongest domain-level program-generation baseline and 90.7% for the strongest instance-level baseline. Cost analyses show a favorable success-cost trade-off, and ablations confirm the contributions of the executable domain model, execution feedback, and component selection.

title: XferAgent: Cross-Agent Experience Transfer for Self-Improving LLM Agents
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can reuse experience from prior task executions to improve performance on subsequent tasks. Although existing methods enable cross-agent experience sharing, differences in agents' execution histories and task requirements make shared experiences difficult to reuse effectively. We propose XferAgent, a framework for cross-agent experience transfer that organizes reusable experience in local and shared experience graphs. XferAgent reconciles compatible contributions from heterogeneous agents while avoiding unreliable merges. For each new task, it selects shared experiences and integrates them with the target agent's local experience to support task execution. Experiments across diverse task domains show improvements over representative memory-based methods and effective experience transfer between heterogeneous agent frameworks. Cumulative task success also increases over successive task passes as agents update and reuse their experiences.

title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
summary: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads. Yet, model families offer only a few fixed sizes (e.g., S, B, L), forcing users to commit to a model based on hardware and latency constraints. This rigidity is often suboptimal under varying query loads. We introduce a retraining-free method that elastifies pre-trained transformers into a single model that adapts on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. Our key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: unlike prior work, which optimizes a single importance weight per MLP block or attention head, we rank every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, on a common scale, by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets, all at once. Across 27 vision and text transformer encoders ranging from 22M to 8B parameters, our method yields smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity and outperforms one-shot baselines under deep pruning. For example, pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, without the need for weight correction or retraining. At 60% sparsity, a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 model achieves up to $1.80\times$ higher throughput and $1.26\times$ lower single-query latency on an A100 GPU. Elastic models are produced in minutes, with construction time scaling sub-linearly with parameter count.

title: ixi-sLM: On-Device sLM for AI Call Agent Service
summary: Running an AI call agent on-device makes it private, network-independent, and free of per-query cloud cost, but shipping one as a real-world service imposes constraints a cloud deployment never faces: ~1GiB memory budget, in-call latency and thermal limits, static-integer NPU execution, Korean STT input far from sLM pretraining, and cloud-level quality expectations. We bring ixi-sLM, a 1.2B Korean sLM, to mobile NPUs through ON-DEVICE MODELING: domain-adaptive modeling trims the vocabulary by call frequency to shrink the embedding and LM head that take nearly half the model under INT4 transformer weights and refits the tokenizer to call speech (18% fewer tokens on call traffic), while task-aware quantization calibrates on real calls and assigns per-module mixed precision by activation sensitivity. A single domain-adapted model runs ixi-O's two production services, AI Call Summary and AI Call Answering, at 94% of a state-of-the-art cloud LLM's task-weighted quality; our on-device modeling carries that quality onto the NPU with only a marginal drop in overall score, in an 803MiB model (28% of FP16) at 23% of the CPU's per-call energy. The same recipe deploys across Qualcomm and Apple NPUs and serves several million ixi-O subscribers in production.

title: xLightGCN: Explainable Graph Neural Network Based Recommendation Systems with Most Influential Peers
summary: Recommendation systems, systems that predict a user's preference for items in order to curate that user's feed, are a ubiquitous and central feature in online social networks. While they are a central piece of our modern digital infrastructure, many modern approaches are opaque black boxes, making them difficult to audit, understand, and assess the trustworthiness of. In this paper we present an exact, graph-based approach for generating explanations for decisions made by recommendation systems. We argue that in the risk-sensitive sociotechnical context of user-facing AI such as recommendation systems, explainability is a key pillar for establishing the trustworthiness of models and validating their effectiveness. We propose a technique built on LightGCN like architectures, an influential and popular class of recommendation models. We describe our approach and argue that it provides an appropriate assurance mechanism for these AI systems leading to specific advantages, including interpretable explanations and a theoretically guaranteed measure of explanation fidelity. We conclude by discussing limitations and directions for future research.

title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
summary: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.
summary_zh: 机器人如何自主收集学习灵巧操作所需的接触丰富经验？我们提出DSP：从监督玩耍中获取灵巧性（Dexterity from supervised play），该框架中，机器人通过行为克隆从数分钟的人类玩耍中学习玩耍策略，随后自主部署该策略以收集数小时的交互数据来训练世界模型。在推理阶段，同一玩耍策略通过提出候选动作序列供学习到的世界模型评估，从而引导模型预测控制（MPC）。为加速推理，我们还引入了一种方法，通过学习到的世界模型内的自对弈来蒸馏出闭环、目标条件的策略。我们在欠驱动推物和多指手的任意到任意手中姿态重定向任务上，于仿真和真实世界中评估了这一框架。在真实世界实验中，我们的方法在成功率上比事后行为克隆高出69.6%，并且以少490倍的交互数据达到了与强化学习相当的成功率。这些结果表明，监督玩耍能够自主收集交互数据、引导基于模型的规划，并实现无需任何任务特定演示或仿真到现实迁移的策略学习。
tldr: DSP introduces a framework where a robot learns a play policy from brief human play, uses it to collect data for training a world model, and then employs the same policy to guide model-predictive control for dexterous manipulation, achieving strong real-world performance without task-specific demos or sim-to-real transfer.
tldr_zh: DSP提出了一种框架，机器人从短暂的人类玩耍行为中学习玩耍策略，并利用该策略自主收集数据以训练世界模型，然后在推理时用该策略指导模型预测控制，实现灵巧操作，无需任务特定演示或仿真到现实的迁移。

title: Whole-Body Dexterity
summary: Current humanoid dexterous manipulation remains largely confined to end-effectors and simple grasps, falling short of humans' ability to engage the entire body by bracing and sliding bulky objects against the arms and torso. We introduce Whole-Body Dexterity (WBD), a general framework that uses the robot's body and appendages as contact surfaces to grasp and manipulate objects. Our sim-to-real pipeline first generates a dataset of feasible whole-body grasps, then trains reinforcement-learning experts on a general any-to-any repositioning objective by sampling initial and goal grasps from the dataset, and distills these experts into a single policy that uses proprioception and object geometry. We show that the distilled policy transfers zero-shot to a real Unitree G1, where it repositions a basketball and a cardboard box to regions around the torso and completes a long-horizon task that stows a box under one arm, carries it from a shelf to a table, and places it. The controller operates interactively, steered by coarse motion references from a human teleoperator. Across real-world whole-body manipulation tasks, the distilled controller completes 90% of trials, compared with 18% for direct retargeting and 4% for a generalist whole-body controller.
summary_zh: 当前的人形机器人灵巧操作仍主要局限于末端执行器和简单抓取，未能达到人类通过手臂和躯干支撑并滑动笨重物体、从而调动全身参与操作的能力。我们提出了全身灵巧性（WBD）框架，这是一种通用方法，利用机器人的身体和附肢作为接触表面来抓取和操作物体。我们的仿真到现实（sim-to-real）流程首先生成一组可行的全身抓取数据集，然后基于该数据集中的初始抓取和目标抓取进行采样，针对通用的任意到任意重新定位目标训练强化学习专家，并将这些专家策略蒸馏为单一策略，该策略仅依赖本体感觉和物体几何信息。我们展示了该蒸馏策略能够零样本迁移到真实的Unitree G1机器人上，使其能够将篮球和纸箱重新定位到躯干周围区域，并完成一项长时程任务：将箱子夹在腋下，从货架搬运到桌子上并放置好。该控制器可交互运行，由人类远程操作员提供粗略的运动参考进行引导。在真实世界的全身操作任务中，蒸馏控制器完成了90%的试验，而直接重定向方法仅为18%，通用全身控制器为4%。
tldr: This paper introduces Whole-Body Dexterity (WBD), a framework for humanoid robots to use their entire body for manipulation, employing sim-to-real training with reinforcement learning and distillation. The resulting policy transfers zero-shot to a real Unitree G1 robot, achieving high success rates in whole-body tasks like repositioning a basketball and stowing a box.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了全身灵巧性（WBD）框架，使类人机器人能够利用全身进行操控，通过强化学习和蒸馏进行仿真到现实的迁移。所得策略零样本迁移到真实的Unitree G1机器人上，在全身任务中取得了高成功率。

title: FastVLA: Task-Conditioned and Temporally Adaptive Visual Token Compression for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. Token compression via attention is a natural solution but is challenging for VLA control because (1) decision-critical tokens are determined by the task, not generic visual saliency, and (2) the token budget varies substantially across steps, so static metrics and budgets waste computation or discard control-critical tokens. We introduce FastVLA, a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework. At each step, FastVLA scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from the importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration. We evaluate FastVLA on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER, and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot. In simulation, it reduces LLM-backbone FLOPs by 35-59\% and action latency by 9-32\% (a 1.09$\times$-1.46$\times$ speedup) while maintaining task success, achieving a comparable or better efficiency-performance trade-off than existing plug-and-play token compression/pruning/reuse baselines. On the real robot, it cuts end-to-end latency by 20\% (1.25$\times$ speedup) at comparable success. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型为通用机器人操作提供了一种有前景的范式，但其闭环部署常受限于推理效率：在每一步中，高分辨率且通常为多视角的图像被编码为数百个视觉令牌，这些令牌主导了Transformer的计算量与延迟。通过注意力机制进行令牌压缩是一种自然的解决方案，但对VLA控制而言颇具挑战，原因在于：（1）决策关键令牌由任务决定，而非通用视觉显著性；（2）令牌预算在步骤间差异显著，因此静态指标与固定预算要么浪费计算资源，要么丢弃控制关键令牌。我们提出了FastVLA，一种无需训练、任务感知且时间自适应的视觉令牌压缩框架。在每一步中，FastVLA通过任务到视觉的注意力对令牌重要性进行评分，并基于重要性分布的均匀性自适应设定压缩率，该均匀性通过带有在线滑动窗口校准的逆辛普森指标来衡量。我们在LIBERO和SIMPLER基准上对OpenVLA、OpenVLA-OFT及CogACT进行了评估，并在实体Franka Research 3机器人上进行了验证。在仿真中，该方法将LLM主干网络的FLOPs降低35%-59%，动作延迟减少9%-32%（加速1.09倍至1.46倍），同时保持任务成功率，与现有即插即用的令牌压缩/剪枝/复用基线相比，实现了相当或更优的效率-性能权衡。在实体机器人上，该方法在成功率相当的情况下，端到端延迟降低20%（加速1.25倍）。代码已开源：https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA。
tldr: FastVLA is a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, which scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adjusts compression rates based on importance-distribution uniformity to reduce FLOPs and latency while maintaining task success in simulation and on a real robot.
tldr_zh: FastVLA 是一个无需训练、任务感知且时间自适应的视觉标记压缩框架，用于视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型，通过任务到视觉的注意力对标记重要性评分，并基于重要性分布均匀性调整压缩率，从而在仿真和真实机器人上保持任务成功率的同时减少 FLOPs 和延迟。

title: VeriVLA: Adaptive Test-Time Verification for Flow-Based VLAs with Latent World Models
summary: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.
summary_zh: 基于流的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略本质上是随机的：不同的噪声种子可以从相同的观测中产生质量各异的动作片段。然而，在测试时，该策略通常只提交单一采样结果，而不对其质量进行显式估计。在精细操作中，执行次优动作可能会不可逆地破坏任务进展并导致失败。为利用策略的随机性，我们引入了一种免训练的“双轴触发”机制，该机制使用两个初始样本来度量片段内的时序变化和样本间的方差，从而检测关键状态。一旦触发，基于JEPA的潜在世界模型将通过对候选动作片段进行排序，预测以动作为条件的未来潜在状态及相应的任务进展变化。通过在潜在空间中运行，验证器避免了像素重建，实现了高效且更精确的排序。在三个真实世界任务（即插笔、移液和放苹果）中，我们的方法将平均完成分数从50.8%提升至65.5%，同时在单块RTX 4090上，每次触发决策仅增加326毫秒的采样与验证时间。仿真实验中也观察到一致的增益：在RoboTwin 2.0的标准设置下，平均成功率从66.4%提升至73.6%；在其随机设置下，从62.8%提升至69.6%；在LIBERO上，从96.9%提升至97.6%。
tldr: VeriVLA is a training-free, test-time verification method for flow-based VLA policies that uses a two-axis trigger and a JEPA-based latent world model to rank candidate action chunks, improving success rates on real-world and simulated manipulation tasks.
tldr_zh: VeriVLA 是一种针对基于流的 VLA 策略的免训练测试时验证方法，利用双轴触发器和基于 JEPA 的潜在世界模型对候选动作块进行排序，从而在真实世界和模拟操作任务中提高成功率。

title: What Should Robot Policies Learn to Predict? Rethinking Supervision Targets in Vision-Language-Action Learning
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are typically trained with action prediction as the primary supervision signal, since robots ultimately execute actions. Auxiliary objectives such as latent-action (LA) and future-vision (FV) prediction are often added to improve policy learning, yet they compete with action prediction for the same training budget. We ask whether, under a fixed budget, allocating a substantial share of training samples to such objectives, rather than to further action prediction, can improve policy learning. We build a unified VLA framework that couples a two-stream multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) with a sample-level router, which assigns each training sample to either action prediction or an auxiliary objective and thus makes supervision allocation explicit. Within this framework, we instantiate three LA targets based on LAPA and its DINO-feature variants, and three FV targets based on DINOv3, V-JEPA 2, and Wan2.2 representations. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, and four real-robot tasks, suitable LA and FV supervision outperforms action-only training under the same budget, even when action prediction receives no more than half of the training samples. FV generally outperforms LA, although the strongest LA target remains competitive on CALVIN. Diagnostic analyses suggest that DINO-based LA targets emphasize relative motion, whereas FV targets emphasize absolute position and task identity. We therefore argue that what robot policies learn to predict, and how training is allocated among these targets, should be treated as explicit design choices rather than defaulting to action-dominant training.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略通常以动作预测作为主要监督信号进行训练，因为机器人最终需要执行动作。为了改进策略学习，常常会加入潜在动作（LA）和未来视觉（FV）预测等辅助目标，但这些目标与动作预测争夺相同的训练预算。我们探究在固定预算下，将大量训练样本分配给此类目标而非继续用于动作预测，是否能够改进策略学习。为此，我们构建了一个统一的VLA框架，将双流多模态扩散Transformer（MMDiT）与样本级路由器相结合，后者将每个训练样本分配给动作预测或辅助目标，从而使监督分配变得明确。在该框架内，我们基于LAPA及其DINO特征变体实例化了三种LA目标，并基于DINOv3、V-JEPA 2和Wan2.2表示实例化了三种FV目标。在LIBERO、CALVIN以及四项真实机器人任务中，在相同预算下，合适的LA和FV监督优于仅进行动作预测的训练，即使动作预测获得的训练样本不超过一半。FV总体上优于LA，尽管最强的LA目标在CALVIN上仍具有竞争力。诊断分析表明，基于DINO的LA目标强调相对运动，而FV目标强调绝对位置和任务身份。因此，我们认为，机器人策略学习预测什么内容，以及训练在这些目标之间的分配方式，应被视为明确的设计选择，而非默认采用以动作为主的训练方式。
tldr: This paper systematically studies supervision target allocation in VLA training by introducing a unified framework with a router that assigns samples to action prediction or auxiliary objectives, showing that allocating a substantial share to latent-action or future-vision prediction can outperform action-only training under the same budget, with future-vision generally being stronger.
tldr_zh: 本文通过在VLA训练中引入一个统一的框架和路由器，将训练样本分配给动作预测或辅助目标，系统研究了监督目标分配问题，发现在相同预算下，将大量样本分配给潜在动作或未来视觉预测可优于纯动作训练，且未来视觉通常更强。

title: Cross-Embodiment Causal Transfer from Human Videos to Robot Manipulation
summary: Scaling robot manipulation models requires large amounts of interaction data, yet collecting diverse real-robot experience remains costly. Human manipulation videos, in contrast, provide abundant and diverse task experience that could potentially benefit robot learning. However, differences in morphology, action spaces, and control mechanisms make human motions unsuitable as direct supervision for robot actions, raising a scientific question: what knowledge in human videos should be transferred across embodiments to robot manipulation? To address this question, we analyze subtask transfer through the lens of causal beams, focusing on which contextual conditions and interaction dependencies should be retained to support local task effects. Based on this perspective, we propose Causal-Beam-Guided Subtask Transfer (CBST). CBST learns manipulation-related representations from human videos and grounds them in task-level semantic variables using robot demonstrations. Within a predefined manipulation model, causal-beam constraints guide contextual information selection by requiring retained assignments to sustain local mechanism outputs while preserving nontrivial responsiveness to retained inputs. The selected semantic information conditions a world-action model, allowing the robot to generate actions from its own observations without requiring human-robot motion correspondence. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show improvements in task success over the corresponding world-action model baselines.
summary_zh: 扩展机器人操控模型需要大量的交互数据，然而收集多样化的真实机器人经验成本高昂。相比之下，人类操作视频提供了丰富多样的任务经验，有望为机器人学习带来助益。然而，形态、动作空间和控制机制上的差异使得人类动作无法直接作为机器人动作的监督信号，这就引发了一个科学问题：在人类视频中，哪些知识应当跨实体迁移到机器人操控中？为回答这一问题，我们从因果束的视角分析子任务迁移，重点考察哪些情境条件和交互依赖应被保留，以支持局部任务效应。基于这一视角，我们提出了因果束引导的子任务迁移方法（CBST）。CBST从人类视频中学习与操控相关的表征，并利用机器人演示将其锚定到任务级语义变量上。在预定义的操控模型内，因果束约束通过要求保留的赋值持续维持局部机制输出，同时保留对保留输入的非平凡响应，从而引导情境信息的选择。所选定的语义信息对世界-动作模型进行条件约束，使机器人能够基于自身观测生成动作，而无需人机关节映射。在机器人操控基准上的实验表明，相较于相应的世界-动作模型基线，任务成功率有所提升。
tldr: This paper proposes Causal-Beam-Guided Subtask Transfer (CBST), a method that extracts manipulation-related semantic representations from human videos and uses them to condition a world-action model for robot manipulation, improving task success on robot benchmarks without requiring human-robot motion correspondence.
tldr_zh: 本文提出因果束引导的子任务迁移方法(CBST)，从人类视频中提取与操作相关的语义表征，并将其用于条件化世界动作模型，使机器人无需人类-机器人运动对应即可生成动作，从而在机器人操作基准上提升任务成功率。

title: Fast-VLA: You Only Think Once for Robot Manipulation
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies commonly place a multi-billion-parameter model inside the feedback loop, repeatedly recomputing task context whenever they predict a new action chunk. Yet task understanding changes far more slowly than the robot state. We introduce Fast-VLA, which invokes a frozen 4B VLM once per episode to contextualize the instruction and initial views as fixed, multi-layer key-value task memory. During execution, a lightweight online actor fuses learned time- and arm-indexed queries with current visual and proprioceptive feedback to form action queries. These queries retrieve task context from the fixed memory and predict action chunks without re-running the foundation model. Fast-VLA achieves 92.46% and 92.40% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean and Randomized, and 95.95% and 79.11% on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus evaluation. Against three continually conditioned baselines on the same hardware, it reduces RoboTwin amortized policy inference time by 10.9-17.1x and requires 1.22 GiB of post-prefill online resident memory. Task-memory swaps further show that the actor relies on episode-matched task memory. These results show that task context can be established once while closed-loop control remains responsive throughout execution. Project page: https://garfield-kh.github.io/FastVLA
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略通常将数十亿参数的模型置于反馈回路中，每当预测新的动作片段时都会反复重新计算任务上下文。然而，任务理解的变化速度远慢于机器人状态的变化。我们引入了Fast-VLA，它在每个回合中仅调用一次冻结的4B VLM，将指令和初始视图作为固定的多层键值任务记忆进行情境化。在执行过程中，一个轻量级的在线动作网络将学习到的时间索引和手臂索引查询与当前的视觉和本体感觉反馈融合，形成动作查询。这些查询从固定记忆中检索任务上下文，并在不重新运行基础模型的情况下预测动作片段。Fast-VLA在RoboTwin 2.0 Clean和Randomized上分别取得了92.46%和92.40%的成功率，在LIBERO和LIBERO-Plus评估中分别取得了95.95%和79.11%的成功率。与三个在同一硬件上持续条件化的基线相比，它将RoboTwin的摊销策略推理时间减少了10.9至17.1倍，并且预填充后的在线驻留内存仅需1.22 GiB。任务记忆交换进一步表明，动作网络依赖于与回合匹配的任务记忆。这些结果表明，任务上下文可以一次性建立，而闭环控制在整个执行过程中始终保持响应。项目页面：https://garfield-kh.github.io/FastVLA
tldr: Fast-VLA proposes a VLA policy architecture that runs a frozen 4B VLM only once per episode to create fixed key-value task memory, while a lightweight actor uses this memory for closed-loop action chunk prediction, dramatically reducing inference time and memory use without sacrificing task success.
tldr_zh: Fast-VLA 提出一种 VLA 策略架构，在每个 episode 中仅运行一次冻结的 4B VLM 来创建固定的键值任务记忆，轻量级 actor 利用该记忆进行闭环动作块预测，大幅降低推理时间和内存占用而不牺牲任务成功率。

title: LTM: Latent Transition Based In-Context Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering interactions that are no longer visible. We introduce Latent Transition Memory (LTM), which stores history as compact latent transitions between consecutive observations. Instantiated on $π_{0.5}$ as LTM-$π$, our method uses a frozen latent action encoder, a lightweight adapter, and causal KV caching for incremental inference without memory-specific semantic annotations or external reasoning-model calls. With DreamDojo transitions, LTM-$π$ achieves 58.54% success on RoboMME and 80.5% on LIBERO-Mem, performing best among baselines without external reasoning models or memory-specific annotations. Ablations support the contribution of transition content beyond temporal cues and the efficiency of delayed memory admission. Scaling RoboMME demonstrations tenfold improves success from 57.67% to 87.50%, while a Cup Swap diagnostic highlights the role of process supervision in temporal composition. Under a 200-token memory budget, success remains 84.00%, versus 87.50% without compression. Finally, real-robot counting success improves from 11.25% to 82.50%. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and efficiency of latent transition memory, highlighting its capacity for complex temporal information, bounded-context operation, and real-world robotic control.
summary_zh: 机器人操作通常需要记住那些不再可见的交互信息。我们引入了潜在转移记忆（Latent Transition Memory, LTM），该方法将历史信息以连续观测之间的紧凑潜在转移形式进行存储。在$π_{0.5}$上实例化为LTM-$π$后，我们的方法使用冻结的潜在动作编码器、轻量级适配器以及因果KV缓存来实现增量推理，且无需特定于记忆的语义标注或外部推理模型的调用。在DreamDojo转移任务中，LTM-$π$在RoboMME上取得了58.54%的成功率，在LIBERO-Mem上取得了80.5%的成功率，在无外部推理模型或特定于记忆标注的基线中表现最佳。消融实验支持了转移内容超越时间线索的贡献以及延迟记忆准入的高效性。将RoboMME演示数据扩大十倍后，成功率从57.67%提升至87.50%，而Cup Swap诊断实验则凸显了过程监督在时间组合中的作用。在200个令牌的记忆预算下，成功率保持在84.00%，相比之下，无压缩时成功率为87.50%。最后，真实机器人计数成功率从11.25%提升至82.50%。综上，这些结果证明了潜在转移记忆的有效性、可扩展性和高效性，突出了其在复杂时间信息处理、有限上下文操作以及现实世界机器人控制方面的能力。
tldr: LTM introduces a latent transition memory mechanism that compresses interaction history into compact latent transitions for vision-language-action models, improving robotic manipulation success on benchmarks and real robots without external reasoning models or memory-specific annotations.
tldr_zh: LTM 提出了一种潜在转换记忆机制，将交互历史压缩为紧凑的潜在转换，用于视觉-语言-动作模型，在不依赖外部推理模型或记忆特定标注的情况下，提升机器人操作在基准测试和真实机器人上的成功率。

title: Causal Analysis of Robot Foundation Models Enables Efficiency Gains
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are a promising approach to general purpose robot manipulation. While the internal computation of vision-language models, which compose the backbone of VLAs, has been studied extensively, less is known about how their perceptual and semantic representations are transformed into action in VLA models. We study this question mechanistically in three frontier VLA models ($π_{0.5}$, MolmoAct2, and MolmoBot) by analyzing the causal pathways through which the input image and the instruction shape actions. Across the three models, activation patching shows that causally relevant information influences the action expert (AE) through a narrow band of mid-to-late cross-attention layers, which we term the action-conditioning interface. The content of this information changes with token and layer within the model. Early-to-mid layer representations of the target noun token determine which object is selected, whereas mid-to-late layers carry the spatial information in text tokens that redirects the movement when patched. Where spatial information is stored in prompt tokens various based on the architecture. In MolmoAct2 the model forms task-conditioned representations at the text positions that follow the instruction, whereas $π_{0.5}$ additionally stores this information at image token positions. We show that these findings can be translated directly into improving model efficiency. We find that restricting MolmoBot's action expert conditioning to only 3 out of 36 layers reduces inference FLOPs by up to $33\%$ while maintaining comparable task success with the default model across 3,000 evaluation episodes ($46.7\%$ vs. $46.9\%$), and the same principle carries over to real-robot deployment of $π_{0.5}$.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型是通用机器人操作的一种前景广阔的方法。尽管构成VLA骨干的视觉-语言模型的内部计算已被广泛研究，但关于其感知和语义表示如何在VLA模型中转化为动作，目前知之甚少。我们通过分析输入图像和指令塑造动作的因果路径，在三个前沿VLA模型（π₀.₅、MolmoAct2和MolmoBot）上从机制层面研究了这一问题。在三个模型中，激活替换表明，因果相关信息通过一条狭窄的中后期交叉注意力层带影响动作专家（AE），我们将其称为动作条件化接口。这些信息的内容随模型中的token和层而变化。目标名词token的早中期层表示决定选择哪个物体，而中期到后期层则携带文本token中的空间信息，在替换时重定向运动。空间信息存储在提示token中的位置因架构而异。在MolmoAct2中，模型在指令之后的文本位置形成任务条件化表示，而π₀.₅还额外将此类信息存储在图像token位置。我们表明，这些发现可直接转化为模型效率的提升。我们发现，将MolmoBot的动作专家条件化限制在36层中的仅3层，可使推理FLOPs降低高达33%，同时在3，000个评估回合中保持与默认模型相当的任务成功率（46.7%对46.9%），且同一原则可推广至π₀.₅的真实机器人部署。
tldr: This paper mechanistically analyzes VLA models to identify a narrow action-conditioning interface in mid-to-late cross-attention layers and demonstrates that restricting action expert conditioning to only a few layers can reduce inference FLOPs by up to 33% without sacrificing task success, both in simulation and on real robots.
tldr_zh: 本文对视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型进行机制分析，发现动作条件化信息集中在中间至后期交叉注意力层的狭窄接口中，并证明将该条件化限制在少数几层可减少高达33%的推理计算量，而不损失任务成功率，在仿真和真实机器人上均得到验证。

title: VLA-$Δ$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer semantic knowledge acquired through vision-language pretraining to robot control, achieving strong performance across various benchmarks. However, most VLAs directly map observations to demonstrated actions without explicit supervision of intermediate physical state changes, making them prone to overfitting observation-action correspondences. Some methods introduce intermediate reasoning or future-state prediction in language, visual, or latent spaces to guide action generation, but do not explicitly supervise the physical state transition itself. We therefore propose VLA-$Δ$, a general framework that uses physical changes between current and future states as explicit learning targets. To support this objective, we construct a large-scale pretraining dataset and derive physical state-transition annotations covering task-relevant semantics and visual motion changes, providing more direct supervision for continuous action generation. During inference, the model generates actions directly from current observations without additional inference overhead. VLA-$Δ$ achieves performance competitive with the state of the art on LIBERO and RoboTwin, and outperforms $π_{0.5}$ in real-robot experiments. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-OmniAI/VLA-Delta
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型将通过视觉-语言预训练获得的语义知识迁移至机器人控制，在多项基准测试上展现出强劲性能。然而，大多数VLA模型直接将观测映射到示范动作，缺乏对中间物理状态变化的显式监督，因而容易过拟合观测-动作对应关系。部分方法引入中间推理或在语言、视觉及潜在空间中进行未来状态预测以引导动作生成，但并未显式监督物理状态转移本身。为此，我们提出VLA-$Δ$，一种以当前与未来状态之间的物理变化作为显式学习目标的通用框架。为支撑该目标，我们构建了一个大规模预训练数据集，并推导出涵盖任务相关语义与视觉运动变化的物理状态转换标注，从而为连续动作生成提供更直接的监督。在推理阶段，模型仅基于当前观测直接生成动作，无需额外推理开销。VLA-$Δ$在LIBERO和RoboTwin上取得了与现有最先进方法相当的性能，并在真实机器人实验中优于$π_{0.5}$。我们的代码已公开于https://github.com/ZJU-OmniAI/VLA-Delta。
tldr: This paper proposes VLA-Δ, a framework that explicitly supervises physical state transitions (changes between current and future states) in vision-language-action models to improve robot control, achieving competitive performance on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-robot experiments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出VLA-Δ框架，通过在视觉-语言-动作模型中显式监督物理状态转移（当前与未来状态之间的变化）来改善机器人控制，在LIBERO、RoboTwin及真实机器人实验中取得了有竞争力的性能。

title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
summary: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.
summary_zh: 个性化对于通用机器人进入家庭环境并实现真正的实用性至关重要。尽管通用机器人操作已被广泛研究，但个性化机器人操作（PeRM）缺乏一个受控基准来区分任务完成与偏好满足。我们提出了LIBERO-PeRM，一个用于具身智能体偏好学习的基准。LIBERO-PeRM研究五个问题：1）策略如何在零样本设置下遵循偏好；2）策略如何从演示中学习单一偏好；3）随着演示数量增加，策略获取偏好的效率如何；4）学习到的偏好在布局和任务间的泛化能力如何；以及5）策略如何组合偏好在冲突情境下表现。我们提出了一种受控的公式化方法，并在仿真中建立了可观测偏好的分类体系，涵盖运动、技能和用户画像选择。该公式化方法仅限于语言可表达的偏好，这些偏好可以在不改变任务目标的情况下在LIBERO中实例化，能够自动评估，并可在任务间复用。基于LIBERO，我们的程序化流水线生成了包含偏好和不包含偏好的配对演示。我们构建了五个任务套件（共312个任务），包含高质量演示、丰富的元数据和偏好满意度指标。实验表明，当前的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略在零样本个性化方面存在困难，而监督微调（SFT）使偏好变得可学习。混合训练在无偏好保持方面优于顺序适应，并且与仅偏好训练相比，在上下文提示下提升了性能，但可能削弱运动偏好的学习；偏好泛化、分解和冲突处理仍然具有挑战性。代码、数据集和演示可在项目网站获取：https://libero-perm.github.io/。
tldr: LIBERO-PeRM introduces a benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation in simulation, with 312 tasks and paired preference/no-preference demonstrations, revealing that current VLA models struggle with zero-shot personalization but can learn preferences via SFT, while generalization and conflict handling remain challenging.
tldr_zh: LIBERO-PeRM 提出了一个用于个性化机器人操作模拟的基准测试，包含312个任务和成对的偏好/非偏好演示，揭示了当前VLA模型在零样本个性化方面表现不佳，但可以通过SFT学习偏好，而偏好泛化和冲突处理仍具挑战。

title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
summary: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.
summary_zh: 现实世界中通用机器人策略的后训练面临两大挑战：部分可观测性使得动作选择具有歧义性，而离线后训练方法则延迟了部署经验所带来的反馈。我们提出了“价值即记忆”（Value as Memory, VaM）框架，通过价值缓存与在线真实世界强化学习来应对这些挑战。价值缓存基于最近的价值预测来调节动作，将其作为任务进展记忆；在线更新则通过结合离线示范、离策略干预和在线策略采样，实现样本高效的策略改进，从而支持及时的策略优化。由此，VaM 能够从离线强化学习预热阶段过渡到在线自主学习阶段，并利用稀疏奖励进行训练。在涉及可变形物体和富含接触操作的长时程任务中，VaM 在引入价值缓存后的平均绝对成功率达到 \(29.4\%\) 的提升，而在匹配的离线训练基础上，在线自主学习带来了 \(32.8\%\) 的成功率增益。所评估的在线调度在相同的梯度步数预算下执行的策略迭代次数为原来的 \(8\) 倍，同时通过数据采集与训练的并行处理，每梯度步的记录时间降低了超过 \(2\) 倍。
tldr: Value as Memory (VaM) enhances generalist robot policies by caching value predictions as task-progress memory and using online real-world RL, yielding significant success-rate gains across long-horizon manipulation tasks.
tldr_zh: 记忆价值 (VaM) 通过缓存价值预测作为任务进度记忆，并利用在线真实世界强化学习，显著提升了长时程操作任务的成功率。

title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
summary: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.
summary_zh: 预测世界如何响应一个动作，所需的信息远不止可见内容：机器人必须考虑那些既无法直接观测又未被明确指定的环境因素，从摩擦力和质量等物理属性，到人类定义的环境规则。我们提出T2-Z，一种用于环境潜在变量测试时优化的方法，该方法通过可学习的环境潜在变量增强机器人世界模型，以调节世界预测。这一紧凑的潜在变量无需任何关于存在哪些环境因素或其取值的监督，即可捕捉潜在的环境变化。在训练过程中，T2-Z交替进行两个阶段：世界模型优化阶段，固定潜在变量，学习跨环境的通用动作条件动力学；环境潜在变量优化阶段，冻结世界模型，优化调节性潜在变量，使潜在结构纯粹通过世界预测自然涌现。在测试时，世界模型保持冻结，新初始化的环境潜在变量通过一次或多次测试时交互进行优化，使模型适应此前未见过的环境配置。在7个模拟环境和4个真实机器人任务中，T2-Z将物体预测误差指标从15.20降至7.00，并将动作成功率从33.73%提升至72.96%。其涌现的潜在变量在不同视觉场景中捕捉了单个及复合因素的结构化表征。消融实验进一步表明，T2-Z仅凭单条测试时交互轨迹即可高效推断环境潜在变量。
tldr: T2-Z introduces a test-time optimization method for environment latents in robotic world models, enabling adaptation to unseen environmental configurations from minimal interactions and improving prediction and control on simulated and real robot tasks.
tldr_zh: T2-Z提出了一种测试时优化环境潜变量的方法，用于机器人世界模型，通过少量交互适应未见过的环境配置，并在仿真和真实机器人任务中提升预测与控制性能。

title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
summary: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/
summary_zh: 我们提出了P³-WAM，一个面向以自我为中心灵巧操作任务的统一世界动作模型，通过三种互补模式学习三维感知、动作条件预测和目标导向规划：感知模式，从视频中重建关节手部运动和相机轨迹；预测模式，在给定动作下生成未来视觉画面；规划模式，在以初始图像、语言指令和可选视觉目标为条件下，联合生成动作轨迹及其预期视觉结果。我们的模型通过混合变换器架构，将紧凑、结构化的三维动作表示整合到预训练的视频扩散变换器中，该架构共享基础权重、具备模态特定适应能力和双向视觉-动作注意力机制。随机化的模态可见性使得视频和三维动作在三种模式中既可作为条件上下文，也可作为预测目标。实验表明，统一训练相比单模态训练提升了全部三种能力，包括在视觉语言模型评估下的规划质量增益。通过统一训练，我们的模型在四个数据集上的三维手部重建和动作条件视频预测任务中超越了专门的基线模型，同时在生成目标导向操作视频时，相比视频生成基线具有更强的指令遵循度和动作进展性。项目页面：https://p3-wam.pages.dev/
tldr: This paper introduces P3-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that jointly learns 3D perception, action-conditioned video prediction, and goal-directed planning via a mixture-of-transformers architecture, showing benefits of unified training across all tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了P3-WAM，一个用于第一人称灵巧操作统一世界动作模型，通过混合Transformer架构联合学习3D感知、动作条件视频预测和目标导向规划，并展示统一训练对所有任务的益处。

title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
summary: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.
summary_zh: 生成式仿真能够自动化机器人环境构建，但物理上有效的环境未必有助于训练。挑战在于识别能够针对策略失败点进行改进的环境，以及能够帮助策略克服这些失败点的监督信号。我们提出了CoDA框架，在该框架中，仿真数据引擎与动作策略通过共享的异构记忆共同演化，该记忆涵盖环境构建、策略失败和学习进展。该记忆将视觉-语言评判器验证得到的诊断结果编译为生成程序，用于重现困难场景，同时生成训练程序以帮助策略克服这些困难。我们进一步提出Text2potential方法，将诊断结果转化为动作块价值学习的分阶段潜能，为策略更新提供密集监督，同时在标准塑形假设下保持任务最优策略。测得的学习进展进一步指导后续生成与程序优化。在四个操作任务族中，CoDA将监督微调后的分布外成功率从5.3%提升至27.6%，在相同生成预算下，比最强闭环基线高出9.5个百分点。在LIBERO-Pro上，经过15轮生成与训练，位置扰动下的成功率从25%提升至84%，指令扰动下的成功率从1%提升至76%。
tldr: CoDA co-evolves a generative simulation data engine with an action policy using a shared memory of diagnoses and learning progress, improving out-of-distribution manipulation success significantly.
tldr_zh: CoDA 通过共享记忆中的诊断和学习进展，协同演化生成式仿真数据引擎与动作策略，显著提高了分布外操作成功率。

title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
summary: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/
summary_zh: 近期三维世界模型越来越多地采用几何基础模型（GFMs）的特征作为预测性世界状态，这得益于其丰富的几何先验。然而，这些特征的视角依赖性使得场景动态与相机引起的变换相互纠缠，导致由此产生的状态演化更难以预测。我们提出了GeoState，一种用于预测性三维世界建模的视角解耦几何表示，它将场景状态的演化与相机相关的观测分离开来。具体而言，场景分词器将多视角GFM特征聚合为视角解耦的场景状态，几何解码器通过相机光线查询该状态。随后，自回归世界模型预测未来的场景状态，而相机运动则单独建模。因此，预测的状态既可以在预测的相机参数下解码，也可以在外部指定的相机参数下解码，同时在整个生成过程中保持单一从上下文推导出的尺度，而无需逐帧进行尺度对齐。实验表明，GeoState在Waymo数据集上优于以往的三维世界模型，支持几何一致的跨视角查询，并能零样本泛化到KITTI和nuScenes数据集。项目主页：https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/
tldr: GeoState introduces a view-decoupled geometry representation for 3D world modeling, separating scene-state evolution from camera motion to enable accurate prediction and cross-view decoding, demonstrated on driving datasets.
tldr_zh: GeoState 提出了一种视图解耦的几何表示用于3D世界建模，将场景状态演化与相机运动分离，从而实现准确预测和跨视角解码，并在驾驶数据集上得到验证。

title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Generalist robot policies benefit from large-scale visual pretraining but often struggle with contact-rich dexterous manipulation, where force, compliance, and incipient slip are hard to observe from images. We present Spark-0, a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) model that uses touch in two complementary ways. During pretraining, image-space contact maps derived from tactile gloves, together with features from a frozen 3D geometry teacher, supervise the visual tokens; these objectives are removed at inference. In parallel, a tactile pathway encodes regional force histories and 3D taxel states to condition the action expert. A single checkpoint therefore supports both vision-only and tactile-conditioned deployment. To scale this supervision, we build HumanTouch, a 1,000-hour dataset of full-hand tactile human manipulation, and pretrain Spark-0 on it together with egocentric video, robot data, and simulation. We also release SparkArena, which pairs vision-only simulated tasks with tactile-conditioned real-robot tasks on one dexterous embodiment. Spark-0 achieves the highest mean success rate on both SparkArena tracks and ranks first on all eight aggregate metrics of the Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark. Compared with vision-only pretraining on the same data and compute with touch discarded, retaining the touch of 1,000 hours of HumanTouch raises vision-only success on Ego Humanoid from 52.5% to 71.7%, and success on SparkArena-Real, where touch is also used at deployment, from 44.0% to 52.0%, indicating that touch serves not only as a policy input but also as scalable supervision for dexterous visuomotor pretraining. The Website is available at: https://xsparkai.com/Spark-0.
summary_zh: 通用机器人心智策略受益于大规模视觉预训练，但在接触丰富的灵巧操作任务中往往表现不佳，因为此类任务中的力、柔顺性及初始滑移难以从图像中观测。我们提出Spark-0，一种空间对齐的视觉-触觉-语言-动作（VTLA）模型，以两种互补方式利用触觉信息。在预训练阶段，由触觉手套生成的图像空间接触图，连同冻结的三维几何教师模型提取的特征，共同监督视觉令牌；这些目标在推理阶段被移除。与此同时，触觉通路编码区域力历史与三维触觉单元状态，以调制动作专家模块。因此，单一检查点同时支持纯视觉与触觉条件化部署。为扩展此类监督，我们构建了HumanTouch——一个包含1000小时全手触觉人类操作数据的数据集，并在此数据集上连同第一人称视频、机器人数据及仿真数据预训练Spark-0。我们还发布了SparkArena，该平台在同一灵巧实体上同时提供纯视觉仿真任务与触觉条件化的真实机器人任务。Spark-0在SparkArena两条任务轨道上均取得最高平均成功率，并在Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark的全部八项综合指标中排名第一。与在相同数据和计算资源下舍弃触觉的纯视觉预训练相比，保留1000小时HumanTouch触觉信息使Ego Humanoid上的纯视觉成功率从52.5%提升至71.7%，并使部署阶段同样使用触觉的SparkArena-Real成功率从44.0%提升至52.0%，这表明触觉不仅是策略输入，更是可扩展的灵巧视觉运动预训练监督信号。网站地址：https://xsparkai.com/Spark-0。
tldr: Spark-0 introduces a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action model that uses 1,000 hours of tactile human manipulation data to supervise visual pretraining, improving dexterous manipulation performance in both vision-only and tactile-conditioned settings.
tldr_zh: Spark-0 提出了一种空间对齐的视觉-触觉-语言-动作模型，利用 1000 小时的触觉人工操作数据进行预训练，提升了灵巧操作在纯视觉和触觉条件下的性能。

title: Mem4Act: Learning Effective Latent Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
summary: Long-horizon robotic manipulation fundamentally requires memory: agents must retain task-relevant information from past observations and interactions and use it to guide future actions. Existing approaches typically preserve raw historical observations, compressed visual tokens, or language summaries, but these representations either expose the action policy to increasingly long histories or risk discarding task-relevant temporal, semantic, and perceptual information. We introduce Mem4Act, a framework for learning effective latent memory as a fixed-size representation explicitly optimized for long-horizon robotic control. Mem4Act addresses three coupled challenges: how to efficiently cover long histories, what information memory should retain, and how to ensure the policy actually relies on memory. To this end, it organizes history via multi-granularity temporal aggregation, preserves complementary semantic and perceptual information through question-answering supervision and key-frame DINO feature reconstruction, and employs memory-first two-stage training to encourage greater use of memory by the action policy. The resulting memory captures both high-level task state and fine-grained perceptual evidence while providing a bounded interface to the action policy. Across RoboMME, RMBench, and four real-world manipulation tasks, Mem4Act achieves state-of-the-art performance on memory-dependent control, with success rates of 49.88%, 61.0%, and 81.5%, respectively. Extensive ablations further demonstrate the importance of temporal aggregation, complementary memory supervision, and memory-first training.
summary_zh: 长程机器人操作从根本上需要记忆能力：智能体必须从过去的观察和交互中保留任务相关信息，并利用这些信息来指导未来的行动。现有方法通常保留原始的历史观察、压缩后的视觉标记或语言摘要，但这些表示要么使行动策略暴露于不断增长的历史信息中，要么存在丢失任务相关的时间、语义和感知信息的风险。我们提出Mem4Act，一个学习有效潜在记忆的框架，将记忆表示为针对长程机器人控制明确优化的固定大小表征。Mem4Act解决了三个相互耦合的挑战：如何高效覆盖长历史、记忆应保留哪些信息，以及如何确保策略真正依赖记忆。为此，它通过多粒度时间聚合来组织历史信息，通过问答监督和关键帧DINO特征重建来保留互补的语义与感知信息，并采用记忆优先的两阶段训练来促进行动策略更多地利用记忆。由此产生的记忆同时捕捉高层任务状态和细粒度感知证据，同时为行动策略提供有界接口。在RoboMME、RMBench以及四项真实世界操作任务中，Mem4Act在依赖记忆的控制任务上取得了最先进的性能，成功率分别为49.88%、61.0%和81.5%。广泛的消融实验进一步证明了时间聚合、互补记忆监督和记忆优先训练的重要性。
tldr: Mem4Act introduces a fixed-size latent memory for long-horizon robotic manipulation, using multi-granularity temporal aggregation and complementary semantic-perceptual supervision to enable policies to effectively retain and rely on task-relevant history.
tldr_zh: Mem4Act提出了一种固定大小的潜在记忆框架，用于长时程机器人操作，通过多粒度时间聚合和语义-感知互补监督，使策略能够有效保留并依赖任务相关历史信息。

title: MOSS: Mode-Oriented Source Shaping for Robot Flow Matching Policies
summary: In robotic manipulation, the same observation often admits multiple feasible actions. Generative policies such as diffusion and flow matching naturally capture such multimodal behaviors, yet which mode is executed is left to random sampling and cannot be actively controlled. We propose Mode-Oriented Source Shaping (MOSS), which turns mode selection into an explicit choice of where generation starts. We first reveal, both empirically and theoretically, that deterministic flow transport induces mode-dependent structure in the source space. Under ideal deterministic ODE transport, distinct behavioral modes have distinct source-space preimages, while practical approximation errors can blur their boundaries due to imbalanced data, limited model capacity, and few inference steps. Motivated by this source-space structure, MOSS constructs semantically aligned mode-specific Gaussian sources that encode mode identity in the initial noise. A modality-strength estimator predicts the local degree of multimodality, which adaptively controls the geometry of the mode-specific sources. It contracts them toward a shared Gaussian where behaviors are similar and separates them near behavioral branching points. During deployment, the desired behavior is selected at inference simply by sampling from the corresponding component. Across 6 simulated and 3 real-world manipulation tasks, MOSS steers to the target mode up to 100% of the time with high task success, recovers minority modes at over 90% guidance rate under a 10:90 imbalance dataset, and surpasses mode-conditioned flow policy by 43.3 points of guidance rate on real robots.
summary_zh: 在机器人操作领域，相同的观测往往对应多种可行的动作。扩散模型和流匹配等生成式策略自然能够捕捉此类多模态行为，然而具体执行哪一种模态则依赖于随机采样，无法进行主动控制。为此，我们提出了模态导向源空间塑形方法（MOSS），将模态选择转化为对生成起始位置的显式决策。我们首先通过实证和理论两个层面揭示，确定性流传输会在源空间中诱发与模态相关的结构。在理想的确定性常微分方程传输下，不同的行为模态对应源空间中不同的原像区域，而实际中的近似误差——源于数据不平衡、模型容量有限以及推理步数较少——可能会模糊这些区域的边界。受这一源空间结构启发，MOSS构建了语义对齐的模态特异性高斯源，将模态身份信息编码于初始噪声之中。此外，我们设计了一个模态强度估计器，用于预测局部的多模态程度，并自适应地调控模态特异性源的几何形状：在行为相似的区域将其收缩至共享高斯分布，而在行为分叉点附近则将其分离。在部署阶段，只需从相应分量中采样，即可在推理时选择期望的行为模态。在6个仿真任务和3个真实机器人操作任务中，MOSS能够以高达100%的概率精准引导至目标模态，同时保持较高的任务成功率；在10:90不平衡数据集下，对少数模态的引导率超过90%；在真实机器人上，相较于模态条件流策略，引导率提升了43.3个百分点。
tldr: MOSS introduces a mode-oriented source shaping method for robot flow matching policies, enabling explicit mode selection during inference by structuring the initial noise distribution according to behavioral modes and adapting source geometry based on predicted multimodality, achieving high guidance rates on simulated and real manipulation tasks.
tldr_zh: MOSS提出了一种面向模式的源整形方法，用于机器人流匹配策略，通过在推理时根据行为模式结构化初始噪声分布，并根据预测的多模态性调整源几何形状，实现显式模式选择，在模拟和真实操作任务中实现了高引导率。

title: REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs
summary: We introduce REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size. REKI consists of a vision-language model (VLM) followed by a flow-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision-language data. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert's cache. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots, and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer. REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: https://github.com/kyutai-labs/reki.
summary_zh: 我们推出REKI，一个仅基于公开数据预训练的24亿参数视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA），在性能与模型规模之间开创了新的帕累托前沿：在LIBERO-Plus、RoboTwin Clean2Rand和RoboCasa365基准上，仅逊于规模约为其两倍的模型。REKI由一个视觉-语言模型（VLM）后接一个流匹配动作专家组成，并在精心混合的公开机器人、第一人称人类以及视觉-语言数据上完成预训练。此外，我们为其赋予了一种记忆机制，使策略能够以极低的成本访问近期状态：动作专家中的少量寄存器令牌汇总每一帧的VLM输出，并持久保存在专家的缓存中。这种记忆机制提升了在仿真环境和真实机器人上的成功率，并将姿态间的振荡频率降低了约四倍。REKI采用简洁的模型设计与训练范式，并在训练与推理效率上进行了优化。我们发布了涵盖数据整理、训练、推理与评估、部署以及全部预训练和微调模型权重的完整代码：https://github.com/kyutai-labs/reki。
tldr: REKI introduces a 2.4B VLA pretrained on public data with a memory mechanism using register tokens, achieving a strong performance-to-size trade-off on multiple benchmarks and real robots.
tldr_zh: REKI 提出了一个仅使用公共数据预训练的 2.4B 视觉-语言-动作模型，通过寄存器令牌实现记忆机制，在多个基准和真实机器人上取得了优异的性能-规模平衡。

title: Inertially Significant Humanoid Teleoperation via Whole Body Model Predictive Control and Online Parameter Estimation
summary: The effective deployment of humanoid robots in practical tasks of interest will require a capability of sensing and adapting to variations in inertial parameters, as occurs during heavy tool use or when carrying significant payload. Such payloads constitute a significant proportion of the combined payload-robot system, the effects of which cannot be ignored by delegating to feedback control. This paper showcases a general solution to this problem by integrating a whole body model predictive controller (WB-MPC) with an extended Kalman filter (EKF) for online estimation of fully physically consistent time-varying inertial parameters. These estimates are fed through to the WB-MPC's full rigid body dynamics model, resulting in more accurate feedforward torques for task demands under external load. Additionally, a virtual reality (VR) interface is provided that enables an operator to provide task-specific references without regard to payload while delegating dynamic balance to the WB-MPC. The framework is validated with simulation and hardware experiments on a humanoid system.
summary_zh: 在人类oid机器人的实际任务部署中，有效运作要求具备感知并适应惯性参数变化的能力，这在重工具使用或携带显著负载时尤为关键。此类负载在负载-机器人组合系统中占据显著比例，其影响不能仅通过反馈控制来忽略。本文提出了一项通用解决方案，通过整合全身模型预测控制器（WB-MPC）与扩展卡尔曼滤波器（EKF），实现在线估计完全物理一致且时变的惯性参数。这些估计值被输入至WB-MPC的完整刚体动力学模型中，从而在外部负载下为任务需求生成更精确的前馈力矩。此外，本文还提供了一种虚拟现实（VR）接口，使操作员能够在无需考虑负载的情况下指定任务参考，同时将动态平衡交由WB-MPC处理。该框架通过仿真及在人形系统上的硬件实验得到了验证。
tldr: This paper presents a whole-body model predictive control (WB-MPC) framework integrated with an extended Kalman filter (EKF) for online estimation of inertial parameters, enabling humanoid robots to handle significant payloads. A VR interface allows task-level teleoperation while the controller maintains dynamic balance, validated in simulation and hardware.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了将全身模型预测控制（WB-MPC）与扩展卡尔曼滤波（EKF）相结合，用于在线估计惯性参数的框架，使仿人机器人能够处理重大有效载荷。虚拟现实界面允许操作员在任务层面进行遥操作，同时控制器保持动态平衡，并在仿真和硬件上得到验证。

title: Compliant GMT: Making General Motion Tracking Compliant via Residual Reference Adaptation
summary: We propose Compliant GMT (C-GMT), a modular framework for full-body compliant responses in general motion tracking. As humanoid robots move into real world deployment, they not only need to perform any motion but also respond safely and robustly to interaction forces. Existing general motion tracking policies can imitate diverse motions but are trained to be stiff, leading to unexpected and unsafe behaviors under disturbance. Prior work in compliant humanoid control trades off compliance and generality. There exist examples of full-body compliant responses, but these are heavily curated to single-reference policies. On the other hand, general motion trackers (GMT) are trained to rigidly imitate massive motion capture datasets. Our key insight is to leverage the generality of pretrained GMTs for motion tracking while introducing compliance from a residual adapter that conditions on a history of proprioception. This enables our approach, C-GMT, to achieve both general motion tracking and whole-body compliant responses. Compared to state-of-the-art general motion trackers and single-motion compliant policies, C-GMT demonstrates competitive performance in both motion tracking accuracy and compliance adherence. We further demonstrate improved safety, robustness, and error tolerance in simulation and real-world G1 experiments.
summary_zh: 我们提出了Compliant GMT（C-GMT），一种用于通用运动跟踪中全身柔顺响应的模块化框架。随着人形机器人走向实际部署，它们不仅需要执行任意运动，还需对交互力做出安全且鲁棒的响应。现有的通用运动跟踪策略能够模仿多样动作，但训练后往往刚性较强，在扰动下会产生意外且不安全的行为。先前在柔顺人形控制方面的研究在柔顺性与通用性之间存在权衡。已有全身柔顺响应的实例，但这些实例高度定制于单一参考策略。另一方面，通用运动跟踪器（GMT）则被训练为刚性模仿大规模动作捕捉数据集。我们的关键见解在于，利用预训练GMT的通用性进行运动跟踪，同时通过基于本体感觉历史信息进行条件化的残差适配器引入柔顺性。这使得我们的方法C-GMT能够同时实现通用运动跟踪与全身柔顺响应。与最先进的通用运动跟踪器及单运动柔顺策略相比，C-GMT在运动跟踪精度和柔顺遵从性方面均展现出具有竞争力的性能。我们进一步在仿真及真实世界G1实验中验证了其安全性、鲁棒性及误差容忍度的提升。
tldr: This paper introduces Compliant GMT, a modular framework that adds whole-body compliant responses to general motion tracking policies on humanoid robots via a residual adapter conditioned on proprioception, improving safety and robustness in simulation and real-world experiments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了Compliant GMT，一种通过基于本体感受的残差适配器为通用运动跟踪策略添加全身柔顺响应的人形机器人模块化框架，在仿真和真实世界实验中提高了安全性和鲁棒性。

title: GRID-Planner: Graph-Structured Relational Reward Shaping for Diffusion Planning
