Enriching inputs with our visual-element annotations narrows the performance gap by 17-24%, demonstrating value beyond evaluation and motivating data enrichment for multimodal document QA. Our code is available at https://github.com/oracle-samples/veld-qa.

title: Verdict: Encode Once, Decide Many
summary: Automating organizational work means answering many small typed questions about one piece of state (does this email need a reply, how urgent is it, who owns it) with probabilities good enough to act on without a human. The open typed-decision model we compare against, like a standard cross-encoder, answers each question with a separate pass over the input. We present Verdict-MQ, an open encoder that reads a case once and answers all of its questions: given identical retained state tokens after truncation (verified on every reported case), a structured attention mask makes the state encoding independent of the questions, keeps questions from influencing each other, and makes option order irrelevant by construction. On the typed-decisions benchmark, a 395M Verdict-MQ matches the soft gold labels significantly better than the released 421M Laya specialist on all five fresh seeds (KL 0.080 vs 0.117, Brier 0.045 vs 0.061), an advantage that survives per-system temperature scaling; its higher accuracy (0.801 vs 0.767) lies past the benchmark's own saturation point, so we read that margin as closer agreement with the benchmark's labelling teacher. On RACE, BoolQ and MultiRC, against a matched fine-tuned baseline it wins on MultiRC and loses on RACE and on BoolQ, where its training is unstable; we measure zero-shot references ourselves, including a closed general system (Jev) that beats every fine-tuned encoder. A controlled comparison measures what the shared state costs: giving each question its own question-aware copy of the state gains 0.9-3.5 points on RACE and MultiRC at 1.4-2.5x the per-case latency, and nothing measurable on typed decisions, with the invariance guarantees unchanged.

title: Vertical Sliced Wasserstein Distances for Meta-Measures
summary: Many modern learning problems require comparing probability distributions whose individual observations are themselves probability measures, naturally giving rise to meta-measures in $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(Ω))$. However, optimal transport distances on this space can be prohibitively expensive to evaluate. We introduce the vertical sliced Wasserstein ($\mathrm{VSW}$) distance, a scalable metric on $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(Ω))$. Rather than slicing along the transport geometry of $\mathcal{P}(Ω)$, $\mathrm{VSW}$ projects each inner measure using continuous test functions and compares the resulting one-dimensional distributions with one-dimensional Wasserstein distance. We prove that $\mathrm{VSW}$ is a valid metric on $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(Ω))$, metrizes weak convergence, and admits dimension-independent statistical convergence guarantees. Empirically, $\mathrm{VSW}$ provides high accuracy and efficiency compared with existing distances for meta-measures. We further derive a practical particle gradient for the empirical $\mathrm{VSW}_2^2$ objective and demonstrate its use for gradient-based transport of meta-measures. $\mathrm{VSW}$ provides a simple and scalable alternative for comparing and optimizing distributions of distributions.

title: VesperMUSE: Multi-Modal Fusion Vision Transformer for Image Semantic Segmentation Under Diverse Light Conditions
summary: Semantic segmentation is critical for the reliable navigation and scene understanding of autonomous systems, yet its performance degrades severely in low-light environments due to noise, artifacts, colour distortion, and the loss of structural details. To address this challenge, this work introduces VesperMUSE, a unified multi-modal framework designed to achieve robust image semantic segmentation across diverse illumination conditions. The architecture addresses the light deficiency problem on multiple levels: proposing a novel physics-informed synthetic low-light adaptation algorithm, approaching Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) through a thermal-guided paradigm, and finally aiming to recover the intrinsic scene details for semantic segmentation through a multi-modal fusion approach. Following enhancement, the framework dynamically integrates the primary RGB features with auxiliary thermal representations and surface normal maps highlighting geometric discontinuities and material boundaries. At the core of this integration is a highly scalable, modality-agnostic self-attention mechanism that extracts both global context and fine local features from an arbitrary number of auxiliary inputs. By combining and projecting these hierarchical multi-modal representations into a unified component, the attention module allows the network to selectively attend to relevant cross-modal cues without requiring any architectural modifications when different sensor configurations are used. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that VesperMUSE successfully recovers missing visual cues, providing a flexible, state-of-the-art (SOTA) solution for machine perception in extreme and unstructured real-world environments.

title: Visual Sanad: Auditing Vision-Language Models for False Acceptance of Qur'anic Citations
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used to interpret religious, educational, and culturally sensitive visual content, yet their reliability on citation verification remains underexplored. We introduce Visual Sanad, a controlled benchmark for testing whether VLMs falsely accept incorrect Qur'anic verse attributions when the same quote-reference pair is rendered under different visual framings. The benchmark contains 2,400 rendered images built from 100 English Qur'an verses, four factual states per verse, and six visual conditions ranging from plain text to decorative and authority-framed layouts. All quote-reference pairs were source-checked and human-audited before rendering. Across 24 full model-prompt runs, we observe a sharp capability split. Proprietary API-served VLMs range from near-perfect citation verification to moderate false acceptance, whereas recent open-weight VLMs often show weak discrimination and default to VALID on most images. De-biased prompting can reduce false acceptance, but often by shifting the decision threshold toward INVALID rather than by producing strong citation discrimination. Visual Sanad therefore exposes a culturally grounded multimodal factuality failure: fluent VLMs may treat displayed religious citations as self-authenticating unless they have strong citation-verification ability.

title: VisualTrust: Video Reasoning under On-Screen Claim Framing
summary: On-screen text can describe what a video shows, or it can frame what the video is supposed to mean. Current benchmarks treat both alike, testing whether a model can read the text rather than whether it should trust it. We study claim deference, multimodal large language models' tendency to let an on-screen claim override conflicting visual evidence. We introduce VisualTrust, a counterfactual benchmark with 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes. Each case pairs a question with three versions of the same video: one with no claim, one with an accurate claim, and one with a misleading claim that alters a single grounded fact. The option the misleading claim supports is the trap answer. Across seven open-weight and four proprietary models, mean accuracy falls from 90.1% without a claim to 51.9% with a misleading claim. Among initially correct responses, 42.8% flip to the trap answer and only 0.6% become other errors. Strong no-claim accuracy does not ensure resistance. We also introduce DEAR (Decoupled Evidence Arbitration and Reading), a training-free agent for video question answering that separates evidence arbitration from reading. An independent check reports conflicting evidence, a selector weighs it without a fixed modality priority and blinds what it withholds, and the reader answers from the resulting video in a fresh context. On 500 videos across three proprietary models, DEAR raises accuracy under misleading claims from 47.2--64.0% to 81.8--85.2% and reduces trap-answer selection from 34.4--50.8% to 11.6--15.0%, while preserving no-claim accuracy.

title: Watts If? A Benchmark for Counterfactual Reasoning About the AI Data Center Buildout
summary: An AI data center is committed years before it draws a watt: a few discrete choices (grid or on-site gas, evaporative or dry cooling, which county to file in) fix its capital, water draw, and carbon path, and LLMs are now asked to help screen them with no test of whether they track what each commitment rules out. We introduce DCBench-440, with two arms reported separately: 200 generative questions over STRIPS worlds for five US deal archetypes, with search-verified gold answers and no tested shortcut above 12% on any question type, and 240 multiple-choice questions grounded in quoted site records, emission equations, and stated scenarios. Across open-weight deployments, accuracy spans 12.5-71.5% (generative) and 58.3-92.5% (multiple choice). One skill fails everywhere: asked to list every action available at a decision gate, no model exceeds 4.0% exact match. The strongest list 72-85% of the actions that would change the project's state but omit most permitted actions that change nothing; with those excused, the best exact match is still 24%. Code, data, and other materials are available upon request.

title: WaveLLM: Wavelet-Domain LLM Entropy Modeling for Lossless Image Compression
summary: Lossless image compression fundamentally relies on accurate entropy modeling, driving a recent shift toward large language model (LLM)-based methods. However, existing approaches mainly emphasize the modeling capacity of LLMs while directly serializing images into pixel or residual sequences, leaving heterogeneous signal patterns entangled within a single prediction stream. In this paper, we argue that effective entropy modeling depends not only on model capacity, but also on the predictability of the input representation. Motivated by this insight, we propose WaveLLM, a wavelet-domain LLM-based entropy model for lossless image compression. By decomposing an image into multi-level wavelet subbands, WaveLLM converts a heterogeneous prediction problem into a set of more structured and statistically homogeneous subproblems that are more amenable to autoregressive probability estimation. To bridge numerical coding symbols with the LLM's native text token space, we introduce a dedicated numerical interface featuring value embeddings and a coefficient prediction head. Furthermore, a task-adaptive prompting strategy is designed to enable a single shared model to adapt to diverse subbands within a unified framework. Built on Llama-3.2-3B with LoRA adaptation, WaveLLM achieves 2.51, 2.24, and 2.27 bpsp on Kodak, CLIC.pro, and DIV2K, respectively, outperforming the PixelCNN-based codec using the same wavelet transform by 0.43, 0.36, and 0.46 bpsp, and surpassing recent LLM-based lossless compressors on all three benchmarks.

title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation
summary: Policy-shift distillation reuses the difference between a teacher's log probabilities before and after reinforcement learning (RL) as supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, this endpoint policy shift cannot reveal whether local action preferences evolved consistently during teacher training. The same endpoint shift can result from early and late shifts that reinforce or partially cancel each other. We investigate whether agreement between early and late teacher policy shifts can guide selective transfer. We introduce Waypoint-guided On-Policy Distillation (Waypoint-OPD), which uses an intermediate teacher checkpoint from the same RL run to compare early and late shifts in relative action preferences at student-visited prefixes. We gate the endpoint shift according to the directional agreement between the early and late shifts, suppressing it when they point in opposing directions. Compared with endpoint-only transfer, our method requires only one additional frozen-teacher scoring pass. Using RL-trained Qwen3-4B teachers, we evaluate our method with Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B as student models in mathematical and code reasoning. In all six domain--student settings, Waypoint-OPD achieves the highest domain-average score among the compared distillation methods. Ablations with the Qwen3-8B student show that removing or shuffling gates reduces mathematical reasoning performance. These results support the use of directional agreement between early and late teacher policy shifts to weight the endpoint shift during student training.

title: What Does History Add? Calendar Controls and Information-Timing Audits for University Trajectory Forecasting
summary: We audit the predictive value of historical summaries in a rule-based university trajectory simulator. Seventeen ridge specifications and persistence separate current plans, past-state and past-plan summaries, and calendar-only history-length indicators. Across training, validation and two family-held-out evaluations, we reconstruct 16,750 routes and 804,000 monthly records. On the original 40-family set, six-month history lowers six-step normalized RMSE from 0.159234 to 0.151522, but its difference from a length-only control is -0.000895 (descriptive paired 95% interval [-0.001957,0.000248]). Fixed weights on 30 families unused in identified prior tasks reproduce this pattern: 0.156480 to 0.150074 versus current-state prediction, but -0.000558 [-0.001783,0.000728] versus the length control. These uncertain comparisons do not generalize to all-history summaries, which improve on their own calendar control. Exploratory decomposition finds clearer preparation-index and funds benefits, whereas fatigue dominates the six-month model's loss and has an uncertain length-controlled benefit. Moreover, 28.20% of its six-step fatigue predictions violate the simulator's [5,90] support. We document family dependence, prior exposure, strict temporal indexing, matched recursive references and independent numerical replay. The task conditions on recorded future plans; it does not evaluate real-student forecasts, causal action effects, autonomous planning or language-model memory. This is an evaluation audit, not a new memory architecture.

title: What Should We Remove? Evaluating the Reliability and Costs of RLVR Data Decontamination
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) math corpora are routinely screened for benchmark overlap, but the reliability and data-loss costs of cleaning policies remain underexamined. We audit sixteen open RLVR math corpora comprising 1,673,514 corpus-specific training items against six benchmarks containing 1,949 questions. We evaluate eight policies based on exact, lexical, and semantic matching using 594 independently and blindly dual-reviewed training-benchmark pairs. Calibration and held-out sets have disjoint benchmark questions and training-example families. A separate review of all 83 candidate matches for 80 sampled training items measures item-level false removal. At cosine threshold 0.80, 52 of 59 sampled removals (88%) were confirmed false removals; this is not a demonstrated population rate. No semantic threshold in our preregistered grid (0.80-0.98) meets the 90% conservative-precision target on calibration. The existing judge-adjudicated policy achieves 98.1% resolved precision and 98.2% candidate-frame recall on held-out corpora. It has zero confirmed false removals among six sampled removals, with one unresolved case; this does not establish zero risk. Within the evaluated candidate frame, this policy offers a more favorable precision-recall balance than the semantic-threshold alternatives tested. Recall does not measure contamination outside the candidate frame. We release reviewed labels, per-policy decisions, and coverage accounting to support evaluation of cleaning reliability and cost rather than overlap counts alone.

title: What do AI chatbots do after users decline therapeutic redirection for suicide thoughts?
summary: Safety evaluations of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots focus on therapeutic redirection, statements urging users who disclose suicide thoughts to seek help from crisis lines or other human sources. How chatbots respond when users refuse that help is unclear. This cross-sectional audit ran 2,550 scripted multi-turn conversations in September 2026. Each conversation opened with a disclosure of suicide thoughts at 3 levels of severity, answered every referral with up to 10 standardized refusals and then changed the subject. All 2,550 conversations included a referral, 2,542 (99.7%) in the first reply. However, mean persistence ranged from 0.01 to 9.94 refusals across chatbots. Newer versions of all 5 chatbots tested in 2 versions persisted less than older versions (each P < .05). Compared with passive ideation, a disclosure of intent was associated with 1.26 more refusals sustained (95% CI, 1.06-1.46) and higher odds of renewed referral after the topic change (odds ratio, 10.07; 95% CI, 7.43-13.66). Chatbots that persisted less in referral more often presented themselves as the user's support (Spearman rho = -0.80; P < .001). Of 8,818 refusal-phase replies urging outside help, only 173 (2.0%) asked about barriers to seeking it. Chatbots uniformly recommended outside help after disclosures of suicide thoughts but varied widely in persisting in those recommendations, with newer versions persisting less. Safety evaluations should test what happens after a crisis referral is refused, not only whether one is offered.

title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
summary: Corporate financial disclosures often unfold over time, with announcements, prepared remarks, and discussion spanning multiple high-frequency return intervals. Financial NLP benchmarks can therefore suffer from a within-event timing mismatch when the prediction target begins before the textual or audio input used by a model could be complete. Chronological train--test splits do not prevent this mismatch, because it occurs inside individual events rather than across samples. We introduce an Availability Contract, which requires a benchmark to state the input boundary, evidence for input availability, the outcome start, and the claims supported by that evidence. We apply this framework to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms. For each call, we hold the return endpoint fixed and compare the previous close, a documentary call-start proxy, and a completion proxy based on reconstructed audio end plus a stipulated processing allowance. At this baseline, moving from the call-start proxy to the completion proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of calls. Holding completion-clock cutpoints fixed, 28.3% change quintile. In an independent release-session analysis of a public earnings-call volatility benchmark, shifting before-market target windows forward by one trading session raises three-day mean squared error by 18.1-21.4% across four frozen prediction streams, while their point rankings remain unchanged. Together, the results show that labels and losses can depend materially on the declared outcome clock even when model rankings appear stable. The Availability Contract makes this assumption explicit and ties post-input claims to the available timing evidence.

title: When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark
summary: Muon's gains in data efficiency motivate evaluating its performance under explicit data, time, and tuning budgets. On a single A100 GPU, we compare a reference single-device Muon implementation with AdamW across 17.7M- and 33.6M-parameter causal language models and 2.70M-parameter vision transformers. A common 23-candidate development budget selects configurations evaluated with five matched seeds, full validation trajectories, optimizer-step timing, and a frozen one-shot test. Muon reduces validation-loss area under the curve by 3.25--22.44\% at equal data and lowers test loss in all 20 primary pairs. In this configuration, Muon improves time-normalized loss area} by 19.68--22.31\% on vision, while AdamW is better by 3.38--6.96\% on language. The full Muon optimizer call, including auxiliary AdamW updates, consumes 56.1--69.6\% of training time, compared with 6.1--9.1\% for the AdamW baseline. Muon also has higher expected regret under restricted access to these candidate pools. These results characterize small models with reference kernels; their wall-clock ordering does not establish a ranking for larger models or optimized implementations.

title: When Is Muon Optimal? Radial Fragility and Minimax Geometry
summary: Muon replaces a matrix gradient by an approximate polar factor and has shown strong empirical performance in neural-network training. The Isotropic Curvature Model (ICM) provides a curvature-based explanation for this update by asking when gradient orthogonalization minimizes a one-step local-loss surrogate. We investigate the stability of this explanation when the fixed input radius of the ICM is replaced by a general radial law. We introduce the Random-Radius Isotropic Curvature Model (RR-ICM) and the Polar-Factor Admissibility Set, which encodes exact scaled-polar optimality as a geometric condition on the positive polar factor of the gradient. We derive an exact characterization of this set for arbitrary radial laws and show that all nonscalar admissible responses arise from radial atoms aligned with curvature kinks. Consequently, every atomless radial law exhibits zero-capacity rigidity: exact scaled-polar optimality is possible only when the gradient is already a scaled column isometry. To connect the curvature-based framework with the established spectral geometry of Muon, we introduce the Minimax RR-ICM by replacing directional averaging with worst-case optimization over probability laws on the sphere. We prove that every nonzero global minimizer lies on the polar ray of the gradient, while its scale is determined by a one-dimensional convex problem. The corresponding admissibility geometry is a positive-semidefinite trace slab, in sharp contrast to the spherical-zonoid geometry of the RR-ICM. Together, these results expose the radial fragility of average-curvature explanations and provide a new minimax variational characterization of Muon's polar direction.

title: When Judges Agree and Are Wrong: Consistency-Accuracy Dissociation as a Blind Spot for Label-Free Evaluation
summary: Label-free evaluation methods, such as self-consistency filtering, majority-vote aggregation, and agreement-based reliability scoring, rely on an implicit assumption that consistency can serve as a proxy for correctness when ground-truth labels are unavailable or expensive to obtain. In this paper, we test this assumption directly. Using four financial QA datasets (multiple-choice and free-form), ten consistency dimensions, and two frontier model families, we measure the joint distribution of consistency and accuracy at the level of individual examples rather than in aggregate. We find that 60% of all incorrect answers fall in the high-consistency region (consistency $\geq$ 0.8), and that 77.7% of these show complete answer collapse, i.e. identical wrong answers across all perturbation variants. This high-consistency/incorrect quadrant cannot be detected by any evaluation signal that is built on agreement alone, as the model appears maximally reliable while being wrong. We show that the phenomenon is robust to the choice of consistency threshold t (it persists from t=0.50 to t=1.00), is shared across model families, and is concentrated in specific intersections of perturbation dimension and domain. We map where this quadrant occurs, analyze its stability properties, and discuss the implications for evaluation pipelines that use agreement-based signals in place of human labels.

title: When Models Misread Ink: Auditing VLMs for Arabic Calligraphy Recognition
summary: Arabic calligraphy is a high-stakes cultural visual domain for Muslim communities, yet VLM evaluations rarely test its fine-grained script traditions. We audit 12 VLMs on a cleaned 1,195-image six-way benchmark using numeric, visual-cue, and Diwani-first prompts. In this closed-set setting, the best numeric-prompt accuracy is 60.9% for closed/API models and 47.2% for open-weight models. The main failure is default-label collapse: every numeric run is dominated by a single label taking 33-63% of predictions, against an 18.8% majority-class baseline. For 8 of 12 models the default is Thuluth; GPT-4o labels 52.9% of all images as Thuluth although it is only 18.1% of the set. Prompting helps unevenly: visual cues move accuracy by more than 10 points for some models but hurt others, and foregrounding Diwani often relocates the default rather than removing it. Arabic calligraphy recognition is therefore a compact, culturally grounded stress test for VLM robustness and for measuring which visual traditions become legible to automated systems.

title: When Reasoning Is Not Enough: Proactive Inquiry for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can act unsafely when individually benign images and texts are interpreted jointly. Beyond implicit reasoning risk, where reasoning drifts toward harm, we identify intent-level risk, where cross-modal ambiguity silently commits the model to a hazardous premise that path-level optimization alone cannot correct. We propose SAFE-PRO, which uses a Risk-Conditioned Uncertainty (RCU) signal, combining predictive entropy with a learned cross-modal risk score, to decide when to ask safety-grounded clarifying questions and where to apply path optimization, under a reward that prioritizes safety and penalizes over-refusal. We also build SSUI-Dialog, a multimodal multi-turn dataset with dual-intent supervision, and theoretically analyze gradient variance and unsafe-completion risk under RCU. Across seven benchmarks and two base MLLMs, SAFE-PRO consistently improves safety over SRPO, roughly halves its over-refusal, and surpasses GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet in average single-turn safety.

title: When Reasoning Traces Conflict with Evidence: How Answer Configuration Shapes Evidence Following
summary: A reasoning trace retained at answer time plays two roles: it can raise accuracy, and it can compete with the current evidence when the two disagree. We disentangle these roles by crossing verified evidence versions with the traces generated from each and answering from the same traces and evidence under two configurations: continuation of the model's own thinking and a separate answer call. Across three model families (gpt-oss, Gemma4, Qwen3) on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, the separate call raises evidence-following over continuation by 29.9 to 60.6 points. On the same pairs, removing the trace lowers accuracy by similar amounts under both configurations. Yet continuation repeats the stale conclusion in most conflicts, and the separate call follows the current evidence far more often. Benefiting from a trace and deferring to it are therefore distinct properties. Further analyses show that the final line of a trace carries most of its value, gold evidence helps most before the trace is written, distractors weaken correction under a separate call, and renewed reasoning, unlike a verification instruction, follows the current evidence in most conflicts. Because trace deletion alone cannot reveal which source an answer follows, evaluations should report both properties together with the answer configuration.

title: When Should a Low-Light Pipeline Generate? Auditable Risk Control for Selective Generative Enhancement
summary: Generative low-light enhancers recover plausible texture but may hallucinate structure; restoration networks preserve structure but can leave regions under-enhanced, and neither advantage is spatially uniform. Therefore, we formulate selective generative enhancement as a decision problem: determine where overriding a frozen base expert is beneficial and refuse to switch when the evidence is insufficient. We propose VetoNet, an auditable regional routing framework centered on a certified veto. It first measures the complementary strengths and routing direction of a frozen restoration generative pair, then predicts the utility of regional overrides from deployment-available signals alone and admits an override only when a distribution-free harm-budget certificate says the perceptual (LPIPS) risk budget allows it. Experiments across multiple expert pairs and domains show that VetoNet adapts its routing behavior to the strength and reliability of the available evidence. When expert complementarity is sufficiently predictable, it achieves statistically significant certified gains; when the relative strengths of the experts change, it correspondingly reverses the routing direction; and when routing evidence is weak or affected by cross-domain shift, it conservatively vetoes switching.

title: When do quantum views help? Complementary classical-quantum representations in multi-view fusion
summary: Recent studies have reported promising results from quantum machine learning in drug discovery, healthcare, materials science and cybersecurity. Research includes comparisons with classical machine learning algorithms and the development of sequential hybrid pipelines. We propose that fusion can improve prediction when classical and quantum representations capture complementary predictive relationships. Our classical-quantum multi-view framework preserves the full classical input alongside simulated quantum features. Concatenation and attention combine the views; single-view comparisons, replacement and masking controls assess both views' contributions. Controlled angular-polynomial experiments distinguish targets adequately represented by a single view from those that depend on complementary angular and polynomial relationships. For these mixed targets, fusion improves prediction by combining the relevant feature sets, while matched classical representations recover the same benefit, linking the improvement to their complementary predictive content. Controlled classification tests further show that gains depend on alignment between the chosen representation and the target, and on a suitable fusion rule. Benchmark validation shows improved mean predictive performance over classical baselines on Wine, Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer, three-class Fashion-MNIST and Steel Plates Faults within the evaluated protocols. Classical replacement and masking controls remain competitive, classical baselines lead on Digits and Covertype, and outcomes with missing or corrupted views depend on the available inputs. These findings support evaluating quantum representations for their complementary predictive contribution and matching the representation and fusion strategy to the target relationships.

title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
summary:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used upstream of decision-making to clean data, detect label errors, and reconstruct missing values. Yet LLM-assisted data curation creates a new operational tradeoff: higher-fidelity models and richer prompts can be substantially more expensive, while the value of this additional fidelity depends on the downstream optimization accuracy. This raises the central question of this work: when should one pay for a better LLM, given a specific downstream task at hand?
  We study this question through stochastic optimization with mixed-fidelity first-order oracles, which can have systematic bias and state-dependent variance. We develop two cost-aware algorithmic frameworks that allow adaptive switching between stochastic oracles. With known bias, the first meta-algorithm applies a restarted, cost-aware policy that adaptively selects oracle fidelity across optimization stages. Its cumulative cost is no larger than that of the best fixed oracle in hindsight and can be substantially smaller. With unknown bias, we develop a budgeted certification scheme that uses occasional trusted-gradient evaluations to certify the optimization progress and eliminate unsuccessful oracle sources, and show an explicit tradeoff between certification cost and delayed detection of biased sources. We provide concrete realizations of these meta-algorithms by applying biased stochastic gradient extrapolation (SGE) and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise as subroutines. Synthetic and LLM-completion experiments illustrate the qualitative switching behavior predicted by the theory: the adaptive policy skips several expensive LLM oracles and substantially reduces cumulative cost relative to fixed high-fidelity alternatives while achieving comparable accuracy.

title: When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill
summary: Reusing the attention KV cache across requests is a standard way to cut prefill cost in long-context LLM serving, and production systems increasingly back the per-engine cache with a remote tier shared by every engine. We study such a tier in a disaggregated deployment of GLM-5.3, an FP8 mixture-of-experts model with multi-head latent attention (MLA), on 8xB300 nodes running prefill context parallelism (PCP8). Enabling the remote tier (LMCache with a Valkey store) left median time-to-first-token unchanged but raised the 16k-token p99 from 3.96 s to 17.3 s. Replaying a production request stream on an isolated engine, we find that a remote hit took 0.88 s against 0.31 s to recompute the prompt, and that synchronous loading turned a hit-heavy stream into an unstable queue: p99 83.32 s with the GPUs 7% busy. A two-term cost model explains both: a hit pays off only if the tier delivers more than B* = sR (2.53 GB/s for this model and GPU), and a fixed per-hit engine cost (T0 ~ 0.33 s) means that hits on prompts shorter than about 17k tokens cannot beat recompute at any bandwidth. Guided by the model, we (i) shard the MLA KV store across PCP ranks, with a proof that the existing minimum-over-ranks lookup returns the longest cached prefix and a load protocol that can never desynchronize collectives; (ii) partition the remote tier by rank, one server instance per rank with no coordination, which raises GET bandwidth 6.3x to 10.76 GB/s; (iii) add asynchronous loading to the sharded store; and (iv) fix three client bugs that caused unbounded stalls. On the hit-heavy stream, with 98.5% of prompt tokens served from the remote tier, p99 falls from 83.32 s to 0.67 s. The sharded store raises prefill throughput by 14%, and by 34% together with an upstream kernel fix. All changes are submitted upstream to LMCache.

title: Where, How, and When: Query-Guided Grounding for Video Understanding
summary: Understanding video content requires reasoning at multiple levels of granularity, from identifying objects to interpreting their interactions and localizing when specific actions occur. This thesis studies three query-guided grounding tasks that answer where key objects are (object-level grounding), how they interact (relationship-level grounding), and when specific moments occur (moment-level grounding). For object-level grounding, we present QDETRv, a query-guided extension of the Detection Transformer for one-shot localization of unseen objects in videos, which combines query-context fusion, a memory module for temporal consistency, and unsupervised pretraining on synthetic object trajectories. We further propose the Temporal Object-Aware Vision Transformer (TOViT) for few-shot video object detection, which builds on a language-aligned open-set vision encoder and propagates high-confidence object features across frames. For relationship-level grounding, we introduce few-shot referring relationships in videos: given a (subject, predicate, object) query and a few support videos sharing the predicate, the entities are localized by optimizing a T-partite random field using a meta-learned relation network with query-conditioned translational embeddings, Global Semantic Aggregation, Local Localization Aggregation, and belief-propagation-based message passing. For moment-level grounding, we propose the Moment Alignment Transformer (MATR) for video-to-video moment retrieval, which uses dual-stage Dynamic Time Warping for pre- and post-fusion alignment, learnable queries for boundary prediction, and self-supervised pretraining with temporal augmentations; MATR also extends to text-to-video moment retrieval with performance comparable to, or better than, the state of the art. These contributions advance query-guided video understanding across spatial, relational, and temporal grounding.

title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
summary: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

title: Who May Release an Agent's Promise? Standing over Commitments in Multi-Party Chat
summary: When an assistant serving a team makes a promise to Alice, who may cancel it? We call this standing: only the creditor (the person owed) or someone the creditor or operator policy authorizes may release a commitment, regardless of rank. In a controlled chat environment we vary who cancels and separate two errors: unauthorized release (obeying someone without standing) and override (executing a released promise). Across six models, smaller open ones override the creditor (Qwen3.5-9B: 69%); larger ones drop promises on a peer's direct word (Qwen3.8-27B: 89%; gpt-6.1-sol: 83%); nearly all act on a bystander's "go ahead after all". Oracles dissociate the errors: stating the rule or the creditor curbs unauthorized release but not override, which the latter even raises in three of four models; among them, only knowing whether the promise is still owed cuts override. Enabling thinking moves smaller models the way scale does. A self-kept commitment ledger stops override in four of five models; with a one-paragraph release policy it matches or beats the best oracle store, raising gpt-6-luna's strict accuracy from 49% (policy alone) to 83%. Code, prompts, outputs and labels are released.

title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
summary: Neural networks often learn low-frequency components before high-frequency ones --- a phenomenon called spectral bias or termed F-principle. Many numerical studies have demonstrated this phenomenon, and theoretical studies have sought to explain it. However, several goals remain insufficiently addressed: (1) explaining spectral bias asymptotically, including its origin and why the preferred components are generally sinusoidal; (2) extending the explanation to general activation functions, such as sigmoid and ReLU; (3) making weak assumptions about the data distribution; (4) avoiding aliasing effects, such as those arising in finite-domain Fourier analysis; and (5) developing a theoretical framework applicable to arbitrary networks. We address these goals theoretically by analyzing the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of the dynamics matrix H, which arises when we expand the network output as a general Fourier series (GFS) in an orthogonal polynomial basis and express the gradient-descent dynamics of the GFS coefficients as ordinary differential equations. The graded structure of H enables an intuitive explanation of spectral bias, while orthogonal polynomial theory helps us analyze how learning bias depends on the activation function and, potentially, the network architecture.

title: Wolof-Adapted Industry-Ready Open-Weight Language Models
summary: Wolof is spoken by 23M people, mostly in Senegal, but remains weakly supported by open-weight language models, while API models raise cost, governance, and sovereignty constraints for local deployments. In this paper, we present 0.6B-14B open-weight models adapted to Wolof through instruction tuning, preference alignment, and model merging. After presenting the pipeline and data, extensive experiments on 63~public and in-house tasks show good performance on Wolof understanding and generation while remaining effective on other languages and cross-lingual skills, with the 8B and 14B models being particularly competitive with substantially larger commercial systems. The models are currently being evaluated in internal customer-care pilots and are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Orange/wolof-lm .

title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
summary: Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Such a task requires models to possess entangled understanding and generation capabilities, as well as extensive world knowledge to translate human action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract visual reasoning into coherent visual outputs. We introduce WorldCast, a benchmark comprising 320 manually designed cases across eight categories, and evaluate 12 representative models. The conducted experiments yield three key insights: (a) advances in frontier models are rapidly pushing the boundaries of intelligent world modeling, with the GPT-Image-2.5 System scoring 72.8 and demonstrating early-stage visual state prediction capabilities on real-world tasks; (b) WorldCast reveals substantial gaps between models: even Nano Banana Pro reaches only 42.8 and the best open-source model scores 20.1, with deficits in handling complex context, entangled references, and reasoning-heavy tasks; (c) strong generative models effectively draw on the capabilities of their underlying language models. These findings highlight the need for multimodal generative models that are capable of dynamic planning and reasoning while also being deeply unified to faithfully simulate real-world states.

title: Wrong Votes, Right Gradients: Why Majority-Vote Rewards Track Verifiable RL
summary: Reinforcement learning with self-generated labels, such as majority vote over a model's own samples, often recovers most of the gain of training with verifiable rewards. This is puzzling from the usual prompt-level view, in which majority vote only returns a model's modal answer and cannot add information about correctness. We argue that the relevant unit is the batch-level update. Because parameters are shared, a prompt's own gradient accounts for less than 1\% of the change in that prompt's output at practical batch sizes, so a wrong label matters only to the extent that label errors share a direction across prompts. We decompose the majority-vote update into shrinkage and misdirection relative to the gold update, and show that misdirection vanishes with batch size whenever errors are incoherent across prompts, however often the labels are wrong. Measuring per-response gradients on five models, we find that majority-vote errors are as incoherent as a random-reward null, that the majority-vote update agrees with the gold update as closely as two independent gold updates agree with each other, and that its noise-corrected cosine with the gold update is 1 within error. Randomly flipping up to 30\% of gold labels leaves the update direction intact, while the same fraction flipped by a shared rule destroys it, and rewards that favor a kind of response on every prompt, such as a learned reward model, fall measurably short. The equivalence holds at every checkpoint we examine but is local: gold-reward training still ends ahead on held-out majority accuracy. Error coherence, not error rate, determines when self-generated labels can stand in for verification.

title: X-RIC: An Agentic RAN-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for Enhancing Reinforcement Learning
summary: The O-RAN ALLIANCE introduces architectural flexibility through disaggregation and AI-driven control. While the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) enables centralized optimization, current AI approaches lack reasoning capabilities and explainability. We propose eXplainable RIC (X-RIC), a novel framework integrating agentic AI into O-RAN architectures. X-RIC combines reactive Reinforcement Learning (RL) with strategic agentic reasoning through: (i) automated Behavioral Cloning (BC) using domain heuristics for sample-efficient training, (ii) a Telecom Language Model (TLM), a transformer-based reasoning module providing contextual abstraction and interpretability, and (iii) closed-loop co-adaptation within the Near-RT RIC control loop enabling continuous policy refinement. To ensure deployment readiness, we introduce BARX (Benchmarking Agentic Reasoning for RAN), a domain-specific evaluation framework assessing agentic control across latency, compliance, and determinism metrics. We validate X-RIC on SLA-aware network slicing in simulation and O-RAN-compliant testbed deployments. X-RIC achieves 89% operational cost reduction while maintaining SLA compliance, converging 75% faster with 50% fewer training steps and 46% lower variance.

title: ZoomCap: Evidence-Routed Visual Zooming for Recoverable Visual Information Transfer
summary: Detailed captions transfer visual information into vision-language model supervision, but quality is easily conflated with length: long single-pass outputs still miss small objects, text, and spatial relations or promote uncertain observations into confident claims. We formulate fine-grained captioning as recoverable visual information transfer, in which a teacher acquires missing evidence under a finite observation budget and converts it into reusable supervision. ZoomCap uses a draft caption to route conditional knowledge retrieval, OCR-sensitive reading, coverage-gap recovery, and adaptive visual zooming, allocating deeper crops only to the most complex eligible region, deriving spatial relations from grounded geometry, and fusing non-duplicate evidence. We also introduce FactCycle, which scores caption-derived atomic claims on two blind anchors--source image (truthfulness) and reconstruction (realizability)--separating fabrication from generator loss claim by claim; human and multi-judge comparisons complement this fact-level view. Against Qwen3.5-397B-A17B captions, ZoomCap achieves an 81.9% human tie-adjusted preference score with a teacher over 10x smaller, and FactCycle counts 52.4 transferred claims per image vs. 31.5 for ScaleCap. The evidence also transfers: in continual pre-training, ZoomCap-450K improves the 11-benchmark average by 1.31-2.38 points over the strongest competing corpus and Ling-Tiny-VL-v3 gains 1.4 points on a production document/OCR monitor suite (1.5 on perception) at 60B tokens; in medical pre-training, 2.64M ZoomCap-captioned images improve five VQA benchmarks by 3.04 points (vs. 1.76 for same-image Gemini-3.1-Pro captions).

title: AeroDASH: Asynchronous Vision-Language-Action Control for Continuous UAV Flight
summary: Onboard inference latency creates a mismatch between the trajectories predicted by vision-language-action (VLA) policies and the ongoing motion of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). We present AeroDASH, an asynchronous VLA framework for continuous language-conditioned flight. A B-spline policy is initialized through supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations, providing continuous trajectory references in position and yaw. During execution, trajectory fusion removes the expired prediction prefix and connects the remaining segment to the active reference with derivative continuity while limiting trajectory deformation. To account for deviations induced by asynchronous execution, execution-aware group relative policy optimization (GRPO) further adapts the policy using trajectory-level rewards. On the UAV-Flow test set, AeroDASH achieves a success rate of 76.56%, exceeding OpenVLA-UAV and AeroDASH w/o GRPO by 38.1 and 20.1 percentage points, respectively. Execution experiments show that AeroDASH sustains motion during inference and reduces acceleration, jerk, and speed fluctuations relative to asynchronous tracking of waypoint sequences. We further demonstrate language-conditioned flight with onboard inference and asynchronous trajectory execution. The code will be released upon acceptance.
summary_zh: 机载推理延迟会导致视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略预测的轨迹与无人航空器（UAV）的持续运动之间产生不匹配。我们提出了AeroDASH，一种用于连续语言条件飞行的异步VLA框架。通过专家示范上的监督微调初始化B样条策略，在位置和偏航方向上提供连续的轨迹参考。在执行过程中，轨迹融合去除已过期的预测前缀，并将剩余段与活动参考以导数连续性连接，同时限制轨迹变形。为考虑异步执行引起的偏差，执行感知的组相对策略优化（GRPO）进一步利用轨迹级奖励对策略进行适配。在UAV-Flow测试集上，AeroDASH达到了76.56%的成功率，分别超过OpenVLA-UAV和AeroDASH w/o GRPO 38.1和20.1个百分点。执行实验表明，AeroDASH在推理期间维持运动，并相对于航点序列的异步跟踪减少了加速度、加加速度和速度波动。我们进一步展示了带机载推理和异步轨迹执行的语言条件飞行。代码将在录用后发布。
tldr: AeroDASH introduces an asynchronous VLA framework for UAV flight, using B-spline trajectory fusion and execution-aware GRPO to handle inference latency, achieving significantly higher success rates in language-conditioned flight tasks.
tldr_zh: AeroDASH提出了一种用于无人机飞行的异步视觉-语言-动作框架，通过B样条轨迹融合和执行感知的GRPO来处理推理延迟，在语言条件飞行任务中显著提高了成功率。

title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models
summary: Large-scale action pretraining equips Embodied Foundation Models (EFMs) with strong manipulation capabilities, with particular strengths in generalization and closed-loop robustness, but reproducing such pretraining requires substantial robot data and computation. To transfer these capabilities from pretrained EFMs to policies without action pretraining, we introduce TILDE (Teacher-In-the-Loop Distillation from EFMs), which synergizes on-policy distillation at student-induced states with learning from teacher-executed recovery trajectories. We further propose AutoDAgger, an autonomous data aggregation pipeline in which a robotic reward model is utilized to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, thereby collecting recovery experience without human monitoring or manual control. AutoDAgger accelerates recovery-trajectory collection by more than $2\times$ compared with the human-in-the-loop method. By unifying learning from demonstrations, on-policy teacher supervision, and teacher's corrective behavior, TILDE improves task performance by up to $4.1\times$ over behavior cloning across three real-world tasks and supports effective cross-architecture distillation.
summary_zh: 大规模动作预训练赋予具身基础模型（EFMs）强大的操作能力，尤其在泛化性和闭环鲁棒性方面表现突出，但复现此类预训练需要大量的机器人数据和计算资源。为了将这些能力从预训练的EFMs迁移至未经动作预训练的策略，我们提出了TILDE（具身基础模型的教师介入式蒸馏），该方法将在学生诱导状态下进行的在线策略蒸馏与利用教师执行的恢复轨迹进行学习相结合。我们进一步提出了AutoDAgger，一种自主数据聚合流程，其中利用机器人奖励模型监控任务进展并触发教师干预，从而无需人工监控或手动控制即可收集恢复经验。与人工介入方法相比，AutoDAgger将恢复轨迹的收集速度提升了2倍以上。通过统一学习示范、在线教师监督以及教师的纠正行为，TILDE在三个真实世界任务中将任务性能较行为克隆提升了最高4.1倍，并支持有效的跨架构蒸馏。
tldr: TILDE introduces a teacher-in-the-loop distillation framework that combines on-policy distillation with autonomous recovery trajectory collection via a learned reward model, significantly improving policy performance over behavior cloning across real-world manipulation tasks.
tldr_zh: TILDE提出了一种教师参与循环的蒸馏框架，结合了在策略蒸馏和基于奖励模型自主收集恢复轨迹，在真实世界操作任务上显著提升了策略性能。

title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
summary: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. Under this receding-horizon paradigm, the unexecuted remainder---the action tail---is discarded, and the next chunk is regenerated from fresh noise. We show that this discarded tail retains transferable denoising progress: action-tail initialization can match or outperform a native 10-step Gaussian baseline using fewer denoising steps. However, the optimal denoising budget varies substantially across samples, indicating that tail reuse should be adapted to the updated environment. Based on this observation, we introduce VLA-Rolling, a lightweight inference framework that reuses action tails through three stages: action-tail inheritance, per-action confidence estimation, and confidence-guided refinement through renoising and denoising budget allocation, while the underlying VLA remains frozen. Across $π_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, X-VLA, and MolmoAct2 on LIBERO, MetaWorld, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0, VLA-Rolling reduces action-chunk inference cost in all 16 model--benchmark pairs, achieving up to a $1.48\times$ speedup, while improving success rate in 14 pairs by up to $15.08$ percentage points. These results show that action tails are not merely discarded predictions, but reusable intermediate states that enable more efficient and accurate VLA inference. These results demonstrate that the action tail can support the generation of better actions with fewer denoising steps. Our project is available at https://chenbao123ww.github.io/VLA-Rolling/.
summary_zh: 流程匹配视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型通过迭代去噪高斯噪声来生成动作块，但通常只执行一个短前缀，然后在更新观测后重新规划。在这种滚动时域范式下，未执行的部分——即动作尾部——被丢弃，下一块则从新的噪声中重新生成。我们发现，这个被丢弃的尾部保留了可迁移的去噪进展：使用动作尾部初始化可以在更少的去噪步数下达到或超越原生10步高斯基线。然而，最优去噪预算在不同样本之间差异显著，这表明尾部复用应适应更新后的环境。基于这一观察，我们提出了VLA-Rolling，一种轻量级推理框架，通过三个阶段复用动作尾部：动作尾部继承、逐动作置信度估计，以及通过重新加噪和去噪预算分配进行置信度引导的精细化处理，而底层VLA保持冻结。在LIBERO、MetaWorld、LIBERO-Plus和RoboTwin 2.0上对$π_{0.5}$、SmolVLA、X-VLA和MolmoAct2的实验中，VLA-Rolling在所有16个模型-基准组合中降低了动作块推理成本，最高实现$1.48\times$加速，同时在14个组合中提升了成功率，最高提升$15.08$个百分点。这些结果表明，动作尾部不仅仅是丢弃的预测，而是可复用的中间状态，能够实现更高效、更准确的VLA推理。这些结果也证明，动作尾部能够以更少的去噪步数支持生成更好的动作。我们的项目可在https://chenbao123ww.github.io/VLA-Rolling/获取。
tldr: This paper introduces VLA-Rolling, an inference-time framework that reuses the unexecuted action tail from flow-matching VLA models as initialization for the next denoising step, adaptively allocating denoising budgets to reduce inference cost while improving success rates across multiple VLA models and benchmarks.
tldr_zh: 本文提出VLA-Rolling，一种推理时框架，通过复用流匹配VLA模型中未执行的action tail作为下一步去噪的初始化，并自适应分配去噪预算，在多个VLA模型和基准上降低了推理成本并提升了成功率。

title: DiPLO: Self-distilled Diffusion Planning for Loco-manipulation
summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation is particularly challenging because it requires coordinating locomotion, balance, and object interaction, making it difficult to learn from limited demonstrations or from scratch through Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce DiPLO (self-distilled Diffusion Planning for Loco-manipulation), a framework that combines a self-distilled diffusion planner with a low-level whole-body tracking policy. Our planner is pretrained via supervised learning on motions derived from human-to-humanoid retargeting, while the tracker is trained via RL to execute them. DiPLO centers around two complementary post-training stages. First, we introduce Self-Distillation Diffusion Policy Optimisation (SD:DPO) to remove the planner's dependence on strong task conditioning, which we identify as a crucial ingredient for effective pretraining, as downstream fine-tuning does not recover comparable performance when it is omitted.. We then fine-tune this distilled model with Diffusion-Augmented Proximal Policy Optimization (DA:PPO), a maximum-entropy RL method for diffusion models, to improve task success and align generated plans with the frozen tracker's execution capabilities. Together, these stages enable motion generation through state-history and goal conditioning alone, enabling 99% task success in pick-carry-place tasks, compared to just 45% for the pretrained model. The resulting planner also generates motions for unseen object goals, with further evaluations on kicking and pushing/pulling tasks. Finally, we deploy our pipeline on the hardware, using our DA:PPO planner-tracker on a Unitree G1, achieving repeated successful executions without any real-world fine-tuning.
summary_zh: 类人形机器人操作与移动相结合的任务（loco-manipulation）极具挑战性，因为它需要协调运动、平衡与物体交互，这使得仅依靠有限示范或从零开始的强化学习（RL）变得困难。我们提出了DiPLO（面向操作与移动的自蒸馏扩散规划框架），该框架结合了自蒸馏扩散规划器与底层全身跟踪策略。我们的规划器通过对来自人体到人形机器人重定向的运动数据进行监督学习进行预训练，而跟踪器则通过强化学习训练以执行这些运动。DiPLO围绕两个互补的后训练阶段展开。首先，我们引入了自蒸馏扩散策略优化（SD:DPO），以消除规划器对强任务条件的依赖——我们将其识别为有效预训练的关键因素，因为若省略该步骤，下游微调无法恢复相当的性能。随后，我们使用扩散增强近端策略优化（DA:PPO）对该蒸馏模型进行微调，这是一种针对扩散模型的最大熵强化学习方法，旨在提高任务成功率并使生成的规划与冻结跟踪器的执行能力对齐。这两个阶段共同使得仅通过状态历史和目标条件即可实现运动生成，在抓取-携带-放置任务中达到99%的任务成功率，而预训练模型仅为45%。由此产生的规划器还能为未见过的物体目标生成运动，并进一步在踢球和推拉任务中进行了评估。最后，我们将该流程部署到真实硬件上，使用DA:PPO规划器-跟踪器在Unitree G1机器人上实现了无需任何真实世界微调的重复成功执行。
tldr: DiPLO introduces a self-distilled diffusion planner combined with a whole-body tracking policy for humanoid loco-manipulation, improving task success via self-distillation and RL fine-tuning, with successful real-world deployment on a Unitree G1 robot.
tldr_zh: DiPLO 提出了一种自蒸馏扩散规划器与全身跟踪策略相结合的人形机器人移动操作框架，通过自蒸馏和强化学习微调提高了任务成功率，并在 Unitree G1 机器人上实现了真实世界部署。

title: Learning When to Adapt: Reactivity-Conditioned Residual Adaptation under Human-Robot Distribution Shift
summary: Pedestrians differ in whether they respond to a robot, yet many RL policies assume all are non-reactive to prioritize safety. Policies trained without conditioning on local pedestrians' reactivity may therefore be unnecessarily conservative or rely on cooperation that does not occur. We propose RCRA, an online adaptation framework that modulates a learned residual around a frozen conservative navigation policy according to estimated pedestrian reactivity. A Transformer-based estimator infers latent pedestrian reactivity from motion histories and robot context, providing a more accurate signal for navigation adaptation and improving scenario-averaged simulation accuracy by $12.62$ percentage points over the Bayesian baseline, which assumes known pedestrian goals. These estimates are spatially aggregated into an adaptation scale that gates LoRA modules, enabling cooperative behavior near reactive pedestrians and conservative behavior near non-reactive pedestrians. Among baselines achieving SR above $90\%$ in every scenario, RCRA reduces scenario-averaged path length by $16.7\%$ relative to the conservative backbone and by $7.3\%$ relative to randomized-training baselines. It improves mean SR by $14.88$ percentage points over the reactive-trained policy.
summary_zh: 行人对于机器人的响应与否存在差异，然而许多强化学习策略假设所有行人都是非响应性的，以优先确保安全。因此，若策略的训练未以局部行人的响应性为条件，则可能过于保守，或依赖于实际中不会发生的协作行为。我们提出了RCRA，一种在线自适应框架，该框架根据估计的行人响应性，对冻结的保守导航策略周围的已学习残差进行调节。基于Transformer的估计器从运动历史和机器人上下文中推断潜在的行人响应性，为导航自适应提供更精确的信号，并在场景平均仿真精度上较贝叶斯基线提升12.62个百分点，其中贝叶斯基线假设行人目标已知。这些估计在空间上聚合为一个自适应尺度，用于门控LoRA模块，从而在响应性行人附近产生协作行为，在非响应性行人附近保持保守行为。在各类场景中成功率（SR）均高于90%的基线中，RCRA相比保守骨干网络将场景平均路径长度缩短16.7%，相比随机训练基线缩短7.3%。相较于响应性训练策略，其平均成功率提升14.88个百分点。
tldr: RCRA is an online adaptation framework that modulates a frozen conservative navigation policy via LoRA residuals based on estimated pedestrian reactivity, improving navigation efficiency and safety under human-robot distribution shift.
tldr_zh: RCRA 是一种在线自适应框架，根据估计的行人反应性，通过 LoRA 残差调制冻结的保守导航策略，在人类-机器人分布偏移下提高导航效率和安全性。

title: T(R,O) Grasp++: Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping in Cluttered Environments at Scale
summary: Dexterous grasping in cluttered scenes remains a central challenge in robotic manipulation, as it requires high-dimensional hand coordination under complex object-environment constraints. To address this problem, we introduce one of the largest simulation benchmarks to date, comprising around 0.5B grasp annotations across eight dexterous hands and approximately 50K objects. Furthermore, we propose T(R,O) Grasp++, a scalable diffusion-based framework for cross-embodiment dexterous grasp synthesis in cluttered environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving an average success rate of 88% across eight dexterous embodiments. Meanwhile, our pipeline achieves only 0.3s inference latency while improving inference sample efficiency by over 10 times.
summary_zh: 灵巧抓取在杂乱场景中仍是机器人操作领域的一大核心挑战，因为其要求在复杂的物体-环境约束下实现高维手部协调。为解决这一问题，我们构建了迄今规模最大的仿真基准之一，涵盖约50万条抓取标注，覆盖八种灵巧手和约5万个物体。此外，我们提出了T(R,O) Grasp++，一个基于扩散模型的可扩展框架，用于在杂乱环境中实现跨形态的灵巧抓取合成。大量实验表明，我们的模型显著优于现有基线方法，在八种灵巧形态上的平均成功率达到88%。同时，我们的流程仅需0.3秒的推理延迟，并将推理采样效率提升了10倍以上。
tldr: This paper introduces a large-scale simulation benchmark with 0.5B grasp annotations across eight dexterous hands and a diffusion-based framework for cross-embodiment dexterous grasp synthesis in cluttered environments, achieving 88% success rate and low latency.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一个包含8只灵巧手和约5000万个抓取标注的大规模仿真基准，以及一种可扩展的基于扩散的跨本体灵巧抓取合成框架，在杂乱环境中实现了88%的成功率和低延迟。

title: Energy-Score Stabilized Attentive Mixture-Density Policy: A Lightweight Approach to Multimodal Robot Motion
summary: For practical motion generation, it is essential to handle multimodality (multiple actions can be correct for the same observation) while maintaining low inference cost and strong generalization from limited demonstrations. We introduce an attentive mixture-density policy trained with the Energy Score that represents future visuomotor trajectories as explicit probability distributions with a single forward pass. Concretely, we output Gaussian mixture parameters for joint commands (and optionally attention points) and optimize them with the Energy Score (computed as a sum of 1D CRPS under a diagonal covariance assumption) instead of the negative log-likelihood (NLL) to avoid MDN singularities and gradient-scale instabilities. Our architecture couples explicit spatial attention with mixture-density outputs, enabling robust multimodal behavior selection under visual noise and small-data regimes. On an 8-DOF manipulator, the method generates distinct avoidance trajectories and stabilizes learning in obstacle avoidance. Moreover, in a randomized moving-object grasping task, where spatiotemporal multimodality and fast timing decisions are required, the proposed model outperforms Diffusion Policy by 15-25% under several unseen conditions, demonstrating superior generalization and real-time feasibility.
summary_zh: 在实际运动生成过程中，关键在于处理多模态问题（即同一观测可能对应多个正确动作），同时保持较低的推理成本以及在有限示范数据下的强泛化能力。我们提出了一种基于能量分数训练的注意力混合密度策略，该策略通过单次前向传播将未来的视觉-运动轨迹表示为显式的概率分布。具体而言，我们为关节指令（以及可选的注意力点）输出高斯混合模型参数，并使用能量分数（在对角协方差假设下，以一维CRPS之和的形式计算）对其进行优化，而非采用负对数似然（NLL），以避免混合密度网络（MDN）的奇异性问题及梯度尺度不稳定性。我们的架构将显式空间注意力与混合密度输出相结合，从而在视觉噪声和小样本数据条件下实现稳健的多模态行为选择。在8自由度机械臂上，该方法能够生成不同的避障轨迹，并在避障任务中稳定学习过程。此外，在随机移动物体抓取任务中，由于该任务要求处理时空多模态性和快速时序决策，所提出的模型在多种未见条件下比扩散策略（Diffusion Policy）性能提升15%–25%，展现出更强的泛化能力和实时可行性。
tldr: This paper proposes a lightweight attentive mixture-density policy trained with the Energy Score for multimodal robot motion generation, achieving robust performance and real-time feasibility in grasping tasks, outperforming Diffusion Policy.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种基于能量分数训练的轻量级注意力混合密度策略，用于多模态机器人运动生成，在抓取任务中展现出鲁棒性和实时性，优于扩散策略。

title: Vision as Proprioception: Estimating Humanoid Robot Pose from Video
summary: Estimating a humanoid robot's internal state from video has a wide range of real-world applications but remains unexplored. During interactions with a robot, its onboard state information may be unavailable due to privacy, ownership, or communication constraints. Meanwhile, online and AI-generated robot videos provide rich sources of data but typically lack corresponding joint configurations, limiting their direct use in robot learning. To address these issues, we present HumanoidPose, a new framework that treats vision as proprioception to recover full-body joint configurations in world space from video alone. Specifically, we combine pretrained human-pose features with robot kinematics in a unified model that predicts each embodiment's joint configurations. We retarget human motions to sixteen different humanoid embodiments, enabling scalable learning entirely from synthetic data. To improve real-world generalization, we further leverage unlabeled online videos through self-training to develop a 2D robot-pose detector. In our evaluation, HumanoidPose improves joint-angle and joint-position accuracy over the evaluated baselines and reduces joint-angle error by 18-32% relative to the best-performing baseline on each of the three real humanoid platforms. We further show improved global localization and generalization to unseen embodiments. HumanoidPose enables visual understanding of other robots during interaction and extraction of robot motion from online and generated videos.
summary_zh: 摘要：从视频中估计人形机器人的内部状态具有广泛的现实应用，但这一领域尚未得到充分探索。在与机器人交互过程中，由于隐私、所有权或通信限制，其机载状态信息可能无法获取。与此同时，在线视频和AI生成的机器人视频提供了丰富的数据来源，但通常缺乏相应的关节配置信息，限制了它们在机器人学习中的直接应用。为解决这些问题，我们提出了HumanoidPose，一种新框架，将视觉视为本体感觉，仅凭视频即可恢复世界坐标系下的全身关节配置。具体而言，我们将预训练的人体姿态特征与机器人运动学结合在一个统一模型中，以预测各具体形态的关节配置。我们将人体动作重定向到十六种不同的人形机器人形态，从而实现完全基于合成数据的可扩展学习。为提高现实世界的泛化能力，我们进一步利用未标注的在线视频，通过自训练开发了一个二维机器人姿态检测器。在评估中，HumanoidPose在关节角度和关节位置精度上均优于所评估的基线方法，并且在三个真实人形机器人平台上，相对于各平台表现最佳的基线方法，关节角度误差降低了18-32%。我们进一步展示了改进的全局定位能力以及对未见形态的泛化能力。HumanoidPose使得在交互过程中能够从视觉上理解其他机器人，并能从在线视频和生成视频中提取机器人运动信息。
tldr: HumanoidPose estimates full-body humanoid robot joint configurations from video alone by combining pretrained human-pose features with robot kinematics, trained on synthetic data with self-training on unlabeled online videos, improving pose accuracy on three real humanoid platforms.
tldr_zh: HumanoidPose 通过结合预训练的人体姿态特征与机器人运动学，仅从视频中估计人形机器人的全身关节配置，利用合成数据训练并在无标注网络视频上自训练，在三个真实人形平台上提升了姿态精度。

title: The Bitter Lesson Comes to Robotics
summary: General purpose multimodal language models (LMs) are increasingly capable of directly controlling robotic arms (e.g., by commanding end effector poses) to manipulate their environment. Tracking the development of these capabilities is important for understanding their potential benefits, such as improving industrial automation, and risks, such as enabling malicious users to produce dangerous chemical or biological agents. To this end, we investigate the ability of frontier multimodal LMs to directly control physical robotic arms. We evaluate seven models at multiple reasoning-effort settings on six manipulation tasks taken from the RoboDojo benchmark. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic comparison of a broad range of frontier LMs across a common suite of manipulation tasks on physical hardware. We find that current frontier models can directly control real robotic arms to perform a variety of manipulation tasks but are not yet precise or efficient enough to complete them within a practical action budget. However, these capabilities are improving rapidly: performance increases on our benchmark between July and September 2026 (inclusive) correspond to a performance doubling time of 44.5 days, while the best recorded execution rate increased by a factor of 4.4 and the lowest recorded execution cost fell by a factor of 6.2. These trends raise the possibility that the Bitter Lesson is coming to robotics; the capabilities of embodied general purpose LMs may one day be comparable to those of more specialized models.
summary_zh: 通用多模态语言模型（LM）在直接控制机械臂（例如，通过指令末端执行器姿态）以操控其环境方面的能力日益增强。追踪这些能力的发展，对于理解其潜在益处（如提升工业自动化水平）与风险（如助长恶意用户制造危险化学或生物制剂）具有重要意义。为此，我们研究了前沿多模态语言模型直接控制物理机械臂的能力。我们在取自RoboDojo基准测试的六项操控任务上，以多种推理努力设置评估了七个模型。据我们所知，这是首次在物理硬件上对广泛前沿语言模型在统一操控任务套件上进行系统性比较。我们发现，当前前沿模型能够直接控制真实机械臂执行多种操控任务，但其精确度和效率尚不足以在实际动作预算内完成任务。然而，这些能力正在迅速提升：从2026年7月至9月（含）期间，我们的基准测试性能提升对应的性能倍增时间为44.5天，而最佳记录执行速率提升了4.4倍，最低记录执行成本下降了6.2倍。这些趋势预示着“苦涩教训”可能正来临于机器人领域；具身通用语言模型的能力未来或可与更专门的模型相媲美。
tldr: This paper evaluates seven frontier multimodal language models on six physical manipulation tasks from the RoboDojo benchmark, finding that while current models can directly control real robotic arms, they are not yet efficient enough for practical action budgets. However, capabilities are improving rapidly, with a performance doubling time of 44.5 days, suggesting the 'bitter lesson' may soon extend to robotics.
tldr_zh: 本文评估了七个前沿多模态语言模型在RoboDojo基准测试中的六项实体操控任务上的表现，发现当前模型虽能直接控制真实机械臂，但效率和精度尚不足以在实际动作预算内完成任务。然而，能力提升迅速（性能翻倍时间约44.5天），暗示‘苦涩教训’可能即将适用于机器人领域。

title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds
summary: Embodied AI lacks the data-rich pretraining that gave language models their agents and skills, so new manipulation capability costs demonstrations per task or a frontier model in every episode. We study a third route: a strong general model acts only as an offline author that writes, runs, diagnoses and repairs a manipulation skill in simulation until it passes an exam on layouts drawn after freezing; the frozen skill then runs as code alone or under a cheap caller that reads only its description. We call this skill-level recursive self-improvement Skill-RSI and specify a compile protocol (isolated, audited author; hidden validation layouts; no-feedback and inherit-only controls; tamper-evident ledger) and a reuse protocol that runs the identical files with executors from another model family. On 7 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with cluttered tables, Claude Code compiled 4 tasks into 7 frozen skills, 5 from a first draft needing only qualification, at USD 4.29-8.22 of author cost each (USD 55 per skill counting the 13 failed campaigns). The other three tasks did not compile in 18 campaigns, including five with GPT-6 and a pre-registered 150-layout run: on the hardest task every campaign scored 78-95 of 100 but had 3-16 safety aborts, failing the gate of 95% success with zero aborts; a 100-episode exam bounds an abort rate only to 3.6%. On hidden layouts, repair that inherits the previous version beat from-scratch rewriting in 8 of 8 controlled campaigns (sign test p = 0.004); an inherit-only lineage attributes most of the gap to inheritance, with development feedback adding a little (3 of 3, p = 0.125). Write-once campaigns found no detectable first-draft effect of practice (minimum detectable effect 14 points). The frozen skills kept 148/150 successes on new layouts with no model and 147/150 with a DeepSeek-flash caller at USD 0.00028-0.00054 per episode; no direct-control baseline was run.
summary_zh: 具身智能缺乏大规模数据预训练，而正是这种预训练赋予了语言模型其智能体能力和操作技能。因此，每新增一项操作能力，要么需要为每个任务收集演示数据，要么需要在每个回合中调用前沿模型。我们探索了第三条路径：一个强大的通用模型仅作为离线作者，在仿真环境中编写、运行、诊断并修复一项操作技能，直至其通过基于冻结后布局的考试；随后，该冻结技能仅以代码形式运行，或由一个仅读取其描述的廉价调用器驱动。我们将这一方法称为技能级递归自我改进（Skill-RSI），并制定了编译协议（隔离且可审计的作者、隐藏的验证布局、无反馈与仅继承的控制组、防篡改账本）以及复用协议，即使用来自另一模型族的执行器运行完全相同的文件。在RoboTwin 2.0的7个杂乱桌面任务中，Claude Code将4个任务编译为7个冻结技能，其中5个仅需一次初稿即可通过资格验证，每个技能的作者成本为4.29至8.22美元（若计入13次失败的尝试，则每技能成本为55美元）。其余3个任务在18次尝试中未能编译成功，其中包括使用GPT-6进行的5次尝试，以及一次预注册的150布局运行：在最困难的任务中，每次尝试的得分为78至95分（满分100分），但均出现3至16次安全中止，未能通过95%成功率且零中止的考核门槛；一次100回合的考试仅能将中止率约束在3.6%以内。在隐藏布局上，继承前一版本的修复在8次受控尝试中全部优于从头重写（符号检验p = 0.004）；仅继承的血统分析表明，大部分性能差距来自继承机制，而开发反馈仅带来少量提升（3次尝试中3次成功，p = 0.125）。一次性编写尝试未发现练习带来的可检测初稿效应（最小可检测效应为14分）。冻结技能在新布局上无模型调用时保持了148/150次成功，使用DeepSeek-flash调用器时保持147/150次成功，每回合成本为0.00028至0.00054美元；未运行直接控制基线。
tldr: This paper introduces Skill-RSI, a protocol where a strong general model compiles manipulation skills offline in simulation into frozen, portable code that runs cheaply without a frontier model. Results on RoboTwin 2.0 tasks show cost-effective skill compilation, with recursive self-improvement through inheritance outperforming from-scratch rewriting on hidden layouts.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了Skill-RSI协议，通过强通用模型在仿真中离线编译操作技能，生成可冻结、可移植的代码，无需前沿模型即可廉价运行。在RoboTwin 2.0任务上验证了成本效益，并发现继承式递归自我改进优于从零重写。

title: Dream What I Can: Sparse Visual Planning for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
summary: Video models provide rich priors for generalizable robotic manipulation, but plausible visual futures are not always executable. We introduce DreamCan, a hierarchical policy that grounds video models through sparse visual planning: a high-level planner adapted from a pre-trained video model and a low-level visuomotor policy. Rather than predicting dense trajectories, the high-level planner generates sparse visual subgoals that balance reachability and task utility. From offline, action-free robot videos, we estimate these quantities and use dynamic programming to select subgoal sequences without manual annotations. The resulting subgoals are more reliably attained than uniformly spaced alternatives, and the full system outperforms language, dense-video, and uniform-subgoal planners, reaching high planning success rates on Language-Table tasks and 91.2% success on LIBERO-Long with a 0.1B-parameter low-level policy. Additional suboptimal videos and test-time compute further improve success. The system also performs challenging real-world bimanual tasks, including box folding and packing with unseen object combinations. More results are available at https://dreamcan.github.io/.
summary_zh: 视频模型为可泛化的机器人操作提供了丰富的先验知识，但看似合理的视觉未来并不总是可执行的。我们提出了DreamCan，一种通过稀疏视觉规划来锚定视频模型的层次化策略：其高层规划器由预训练的视频模型改编而来，低层则采用视觉运动策略。高层规划器并非预测密集轨迹，而是生成稀疏的视觉子目标，以平衡可达性与任务效用。我们从离线的、无动作的机器人视频中估计这些量，并利用动态规划在无需人工标注的情况下选择子目标序列。与均匀间隔的替代方案相比，所生成的子目标更易于实现，且整个系统优于基于语言、密集视频和均匀子目标的规划器，在Language-Table任务中取得了较高的规划成功率，并在LIBERO-Long上以0.1B参数的低层策略达到了91.2%的成功率。额外的次优视频和测试时计算进一步提升了成功率。该系统还能执行具有挑战性的真实世界双臂任务，包括折叠纸箱和包装未见组合的物体。更多结果请访问 https://dreamcan.github.io/。
tldr: DreamCan introduces a hierarchical robot manipulation policy that uses a pre-trained video model for sparse visual subgoal planning, improving long-horizon task success in simulation and real-world bimanual tasks.
tldr_zh: DreamCan 提出了一种层级机器人操作策略，利用预训练视频模型进行稀疏视觉子目标规划，在仿真和真实世界双臂任务中提高了长时程任务的成功率。

title: SARAM: Sparse Adapter Allocation with Reuse and Merging for Lifelong Robot Learning
summary: Lifelong robot learning requires acquiring new tasks sequentially without forgetting earlier ones. With large pre-trained vision-language-action (VLA) backbones, adapter-based methods effectively mitigate this challenge. However, their task-specific adapters and selection modules accumulate with the task stream, creating a scalability challenge in on-disk storage and deployment cost under fixed onboard resource budgets. We propose SARAM, a lifelong learning framework that limits storage growth while keeping GPU memory and per-step inference cost independent of the task stream length. For each new task, SARAM reuses frozen adapters from previous tasks and introduces new adapters only at sparsely selected layers, with a duplication penalty encouraging them to capture information not already represented by the adapter library. At deployment, a compact signature derived from backbone activation statistics identifies the task once per episode, and the corresponding task update is merged into the backbone, leaving only the backbone in the control loop. Across four LIBERO suites, SARAM matches or exceeds adapter-based baselines while adding up to 4.5x less on-disk state per task. GPU memory usage and control frequency remain comparable to those of the backbone as the task stream grows. Experiments on a real UR5 arm with a different backbone further demonstrate retention throughout a sequential task stream.
summary_zh: 终身机器人学习要求在不遗忘先前任务的情况下顺序获取新任务。借助大规模预训练的视觉-语言-行动（VLA）骨干网络，基于适配器的方法能够有效缓解这一挑战。然而，其任务专用适配器和选择模块会随任务流不断累积，在机载资源预算固定的条件下，给磁盘存储和部署成本带来了可扩展性难题。我们提出SARAM，一种终身学习框架，它在限制存储增长的同时，保持GPU内存和每步推理成本不依赖于任务流长度。对于每个新任务，SARAM复用先前任务的冻结适配器，并仅在稀疏选定的层引入新适配器，同时通过重复惩罚机制鼓励新适配器捕获适配器库中尚未表示的信息。在部署时，由骨干网络激活统计量生成的紧凑签名在每个回合中识别一次任务，相应的任务更新被合并到骨干网络中，从而仅保留骨干网络在控制回路中。在四个LIBERO套件中，SARAM达到或超越基于适配器的基线方法，同时每个任务最多减少4.5倍的磁盘状态存储。随着任务流的增长，GPU内存使用和控制频率保持与骨干网络相当。在真实UR5机械臂上使用不同骨干网络的实验进一步证明，SARAM能够在连续任务流中保持任务记忆。
tldr: SARAM presents a lifelong learning framework for VLA backbones that limits storage growth by reusing and merging task-specific adapters, keeping GPU memory and inference cost constant as task streams lengthen, with real-robot validation on a UR5 arm.
tldr_zh: SARAM 提出一种针对 VLA 基座的终身学习框架，通过复用和合并任务适配器限制存储增长，使 GPU 内存和推理成本不随任务流变长而增加，并在 UR5 机械臂上进行了真实机器人验证。

title: When Better Policies Leave Harder Failures: Coverage Shift in VLM Success Monitoring
summary: Can a better robot policy become harder to monitor? We study a fixed vision-language model (VLM) that judges success while a policy improves. In a controlled 20-seed tray-placement experiment, training selects only simulator-verified successes. Success rises from 66.8% to 97.0%, and accepted hover failures fall from 5.0% to 0.9% of executions. Yet the judge accepts 50.0% of remaining hovers, versus 31.1% under untrained sampling. These residual failures more often lie below the tray rim, which can conceal the gap beneath a grasped cube. A separate boundary probe accepts 148/160 below-rim hovers and 0/160 above-rim hovers. We call this change in conditional monitoring sensitivity coverage shift: learning changes which failures reach a fixed judge. A broader diagnosis covers nine judges and 1,392 stimuli. Judge-filtered experiments across eight settings further show heterogeneous effects of state-dependent acceptance. The results distinguish task improvement from failure detectability and motivate reporting absolute misses, conditional misses, and audit coverage together.
summary_zh: 更好的机器人策略是否可能变得更难监控？我们研究了一个固定的视觉-语言模型（VLM）来判断任务成功，同时策略在持续改进。在受控的20孔托盘放置实验中，训练仅选择经模拟器验证的成功样本。成功率从66.8%提升至97.0%，被接受的悬停失败在执行中的占比从5.0%降至0.9%。然而，判断器对剩余悬停案例的接受率为50.0%，而在未训练采样条件下这一比例为31.1%。这些残余失败更常见于托盘边缘下方，这可能掩盖被抓取立方体下方的间隙。一项独立的边界探针接受了148/160个边缘下方悬停案例，而边缘上方悬停案例则为0/160。我们将这种条件监控敏感度的变化称为覆盖偏移：学习改变了哪些失败会到达固定判断器。一项更广泛的诊断覆盖了九个判断器和1,392个刺激样本。跨八种设置的判断器过滤实验进一步显示了状态依赖接受的异质性效应。研究结果区分了任务改进与失败可检测性，并促使同时报告绝对遗漏、条件遗漏及审计覆盖率。
tldr: This paper investigates how improving a robot policy can reduce a VLM-based success monitor's coverage of residual failures, coining 'coverage shift' and showing that conditional acceptance rates worsen for the harder, remaining failure modes.
tldr_zh: 该论文探讨了机器人策略改进如何降低基于VLM的成功监测器对剩余失败的覆盖范围，提出“覆盖偏移”概念，并表明对更难的剩余失败模式的条件接受率会恶化。
