We propose utility-verified abstraction (UVA), which teaches the agent to describe private entities by their role and type while retaining the technical details an expert needs. From solved repair trajectories, we rewrite each question into this form and keep the rewrite only if it discloses fewer private entities and the repair, replayed from the same execution state with the repair trajectories. Across two benchmarks, the trained agent consults more often than before training. On repository-level issue repair, it solves 37.6% of issues, against 25.3% for the same model working alone, a gain from the training as a whole rather than from consultation alone. Its questions disclose 3.7-fold fewer private entities and 1.4-fold less verbatim code than the untrained agent's questions to the same expert.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
summary: Empirical studies of electricity prices routinely state that their models use only information available at the time of the trading decision. For weather-driven forecasts drawn from commercial archives, this condition is harder to meet than it appears, and whether it holds can change over time. We identify three timing pitfalls. A forecast run is labelled by the issue time of its weather model, but becomes available hours later and keeps changing after publication. Auction gates follow local clock time, while archives use UTC. Outturn series are revised after publication without earlier values being kept. Using the timestamps of 128,656 forecast runs from ten weather-model configurations, matched to the day-ahead and first intraday auction gates in Great Britain over 2022-2026, we find that selecting "the latest run issued before the gate" picks a run not yet published at the gate on more than 99% of delivery days for six of the ten configurations at one of the two gates. For GFS at the day-ahead gate, the share is 0.6% in winter and 99.8% in summer. The exposure also shifts as publication delays drift, and an action margin of a few minutes can cost a full six-hour forecast cycle. The wrongly selected inputs differ materially from those available at the gate, but their apparent accuracy gain ranges from -9% to +24% across variables, models, gates and seasons, so its effect cannot be assumed and must be measured. We argue that point-in-time correctness is a dynamic property of the data pipeline, and propose a protocol that audits it from timestamps before any model is fitted.

title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
summary: Jailbreak papers report an attack success rate, the share of responses that deliver the harmful request, and read it as a property of the target model. We hold the target model, the prompts and the responses fixed and change only the grader. Three dense graders of 8B and 9B parameters, from three model families, move compliant responses to the neighbouring class, evasion, instead of scattering them across classes. One of them assigns the compliance label zero times in 900 responses. This class collapse also appears on new harmful requests, on a target model from a third family, and in a held-out 7B grader from a fourth family. Per-class label counts expose it at no cost and without human labels. The collapse decides how the rate behaves under a change of grader. On two corpora of 900 responses and eight graders, the compliance rate differs by a factor of 22 to 25, while the non-refusal rate differs by 18 to 23 percentage points. Without the three collapsing graders, compliance differs by a factor of 1.7 to 2.8 on all four corpora, and non-refusal still differs by 10 to 22 points. These results do not change when every grader is called once. We propose a reporting minimum that keeps the compliance rate and adds its per-class label counts and the named grader. Beside it goes the non-refusal rate, whose disagreement across graders is additive.

title: The One-Pixel of Reasoning: One Truthful Relation Is Enough to Mislead LLM Agents
summary: Can one sentence manipulate an agent's belief by targeting a single implicit warrant linking evidence to a conclusion? In this paper, we introduce the one-relation attack (ORA), a novel cognitive attack on this inferential relation. ORA localizes a critical implicit warrant and performs a one-relation intervention using a single source-grounded sentence that qualifies this warrant and steers the agent toward an incorrect belief. Across eighteen models on biomedical inference and vulnerability detection, best-of-$10 attacks overturn initially correct answers at mean rates of 54.9% for proprietary and 80.0% for open-weight models. Attacks also transfer without victim feedback, and paired controls support the roles of targeting and qualification. Moreover, successful sentences can pass source-support checks and evade identification, and multi-agent debate raises team error from 50.0% to 59.5% in our balanced stress test. These findings establish implicit warrants as a cognitive attack surface for manipulating agents' beliefs.

title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Pointwise Replicable Agnostic Learning
summary: Pointwise replicability asks that two independently trained predictors, using the same random seed, agree at each fixed query with high probability. We determine its optimal agnostic sample complexity on finite and countable domains. For every nonempty binary class of finite VC dimension $d\ge1$, the required number of independent examples is $Θ\!\left(\frac{d}{ρ^2α^2}+\frac{\log(1/β)}{α^2}\right)$, uniformly over independent accuracy, failure, and disagreement parameters $α,β,ρ\in(0,1/10)$. The learner returns one binary function, may be improper, and uses unrestricted shared randomness. Its sample budget is fixed before observing data, and the replicability guarantee includes queries of zero marginal mass. The main construction combines an ensemble of empirical-risk minimizers with a smooth, signal-dependent risk decomposition. A single shared phase selects the final binary predictor. Record times certify its weak-signal risk, while a uniform bound protects the strong-signal risk at that same selected time. A phase-comparison theorem controls the actual shared-seed execution under simultaneous changes in the marginals and risk coefficients. A rare repair step then makes the confidence cost additive. Together with matching lower bounds, this removes the remaining logarithmic overhead and parameter restrictions in the general countable-domain sample-complexity problem. This extended version also retains the earlier explicit constructions and their proofs, including proper learning for VC-one classes, the full finite-atom class, a faster realizable bound, and counterexamples that separate restrictions of particular algorithms from restrictions of the learning problem.

title: Think Visually Across Space and Time: Grounded Reasoning for Video Segmentation
summary: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) requires a model to identify an implicitly described target and predict its pixel-level mask trajectory, while resolving the spatial relations and temporal events that determine the answer. Text-only Chain-of-Thought (CoT) can explain a target choice without making the underlying visual references explicit, leaving a \emph{video reference gap} between linguistic inference and the evidence distributed across frames. We introduce \textbf{Temporal Chain of Video Primitives (TCoVP)}, a spatiotemporally grounded form of Video CoT that organizes query-relevant observations into a chronological reasoning chain. Each primitive associates an entity reference with temporal support and timestamped spatial evidence, and the chain interleaves these references with language to guide reasoning about which entity is relevant, when the queried event holds, and where its evidence appears. The selected target primitives then provide box prompts and temporal support for video mask prediction. We construct TCoVP-SFT-15k and TCoVP-RL-13k to learn this representation through supervised fine-tuning and chain-aligned reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments across five VRS benchmarks and three model backbones demonstrate the strong performance of TCoVP, highlighting the effectiveness of organizing spatial and temporal evidence within the reasoning process. All models and code will be publicly released. Project page: \url{https://victor-wjw.github.io/TCoVP/}

title: Tilted Mondrian: Triage and Mitigation of Fine-grained Disparities in Conformal Prediction
summary: Fairness in conformal prediction is often pursued through Mondrian calibration, which provides finite-sample coverage guarantees separately across groups. These guarantees, however, are coarse: substantial disparities can remain within finer strata. This coarse-to-fine fairness issue raises two questions: how severe can such disparities be, and how can they be mitigated? Aggregate disparities can depend on how groups are distributed across strata. For severity assessment, we introduce propensity standardization to examine the effect of population composition, and show how group composition can induce disagreement between aggregate and finer-stratum comparisons. For mitigation, we develop Tilted Mondrian to improve fairness compared to group-Mondrian at a finer level without additional model training. Tilted Mondrian retains groupwise coverage guarantees and mitigates coverage and prediction set size disparities within finer strata. Finally, we derive a method-agnostic bound that quantifies how much reduction in finer-stratum coverage disparity can be achieved.

title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
summary: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, source-routed plan chaining, and diagnostic plan revision. RetailRAG consistently outperforms existing agentic RAG baselines across all evaluation axes, serving as a strong reference system for assessing LLM agents on retail workflows. On RetailBridge, evaluating ten LLM backbones with RetailRAG reveals multi-source chaining as the dominant bottleneck across providers and model scales, suggesting that reliable retail agents require explicit cross-source orchestration rather than scaling alone. Code and data are publicly available at \url{https://github.com/DISL-Lab/RetailBridge}.

title: Towards Human-AI Complementarity for AI Safety
summary: Safely overseeing AI is increasingly challenging for the humans doing it, as they must evaluate longer and more complex outputs with every new model generation. To mitigate this challenge, we could leverage complementarity: where humans and models make different mistakes, combining their judgements could yield an oversight signal stronger than either produces alone. We study this opportunity in realistic, safety-relevant settings, contributing the largest known suite of such tasks (3,957 instances across 8 datasets and 6 domains) as well as a platform and data pipeline for measuring human, AI, and human-AI performance on matched items. We collected 35,613 judgements from 416 human raters, finding a considerable opportunity for a complementarity effect. We also found that with the assistance methods we tested, human raters corrected the AI's errors less often, even when overall human accuracy rose, and the hybridisation methods we tested added little over the better single source on average. While complementarity is an important and feasible engineering target for safe oversight, achieving it remains an open challenge for future work.

title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks. Despite this progress, individual skills may follow distinct trajectories as the policy evolves, with some becoming redundant after the model internalizes their capabilities, others remaining valuable as external scaffolding, and still others turning harmful. However, existing skill library systems fail to identify each skill's true contribution due to free-riding among co-retrieved skills, difficulty confounding across tasks, and the absence of skill-specific counterfactual evidence, which prevents reliable skill lifecycle management. We propose TrackRL, an agentic RL framework where skill tracking drives skill library full lifecycle management. Specifically, within each GRPO group, we turn grouped sampling into online randomized controlled experiments. Independent random injection and within-group contrasts on the same task isolate each skill's true contribution, and reliability-weighted aggregation accumulates evidence across groups. As evidence accumulates, we continuously track skill utility, which measures the skill's causal contribution as external scaffolding, and model mastery, which reflects how far the corresponding capability has been internalized. Along this line, we formulate skill lifecycle management as an evidence-gated state-transition process that governs each skill from generation and admission through protected incubation to retention, retirement, or removal, while a soft capacity bound controls library growth. Experiments show that TrackRL outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation, with further analyses revealing how skill value shifts during policy learning and how evidence-driven state transitions shape skill library evolution. Our code is available at https://github.com/xizhu1022/TrackRL.

title: TrustAgent-RFF: Agentic Diagnostic Planning for Reliable RF Fingerprinting under Domain Shift
summary: Radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) models can achieve accuracy under source domain conditions but become unreliable when the receiver, distance, collection day, or environment changes. Incorrect predictions in unseen domains may receive high softmax confidence, making confidence thresholding insufficient for trustworthy deployment. We propose TrustAgent-RFF, a prediction level reliability framework for RFF that operates with a frozen in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) classifier without target domain labels. For each device prediction, the framework acquires radio frequency evidence: counterfactual stability, prototype consistency, acquisition domain similarity, and signal quality. A source calibrated trust estimator combines these diagnostics with classifier confidence, prediction margin, and evidence availability indicators. Source derived lower tail penalties and cross module interactions reduce trust when diagnostic signals indicate weak support. A large language model (LLM) based planner adaptively selects the next diagnostic action based on evidence, trust state, action costs, and remaining budget. A deterministic source calibrated decision layer updates the prediction state as Accept, Reject, or Defer. Experiments across five RFF datasets and classifier backbones reveal an average source to target accuracy drop of 38.7% and show that many incorrect target domain predictions remain highly confident.

title: UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop
summary: Looped large language models trade parameter storage for recurrent computation, but most are trained from scratch. In practice, pretraining with looped depth is expensive, making post-training upcycling of a pretrained non-looped LLM an attractive alternative. We introduce \textbf{UpLoop}, a post-training recipe based on \emph{layer-wise} recurrence. Instead of looping a whole model or a middle block, UpLoop loops each selected layer locally, preserving the pretrained depth hierarchy and avoiding feature-space mismatch. To make loop execution useful, we add hidden-wise gates on the attention and MLP residual branches, so later loops act as progressive refinements rather than redundant rewrites. Empirically, UpLoop breaks the commonly observed saturation at two loops ($R=2$) in prior looped models. Starting from Qwen3-4B Base and applying SFT, UpLoop improves the average accuracy across 20 benchmarks by 6.17\% at $R=3$. We use $R=3$ as the main setting for the best accuracy--cost trade-off, while both native and extrapolated $R=4$ yield further gains.

title: UtoMe: Observation-Uncertainty-Guided Token Merging for Weather Foundation Models
summary: Weather transformers process dense reanalysis fields whose reliability varies across variables, locations, and weather regimes. Token merging can reduce computation, but feature similarity alone does not account for this heterogeneous input uncertainty. We introduce UtoMe, an observation-uncertainty-guided token merging framework that combines dynamics saliency with ensemble data assimilation spread as a relative input-reliability proxy. The resulting importance score protects selected tokens as anchors and calibrates bipartite matching between the remaining tokens. Three variants use external uncertainty at both training and inference, during training only, or neither stage. In ERA5 72-hour forecasting at two spatial resolutions, UtoMe improves Overall error over train-time ToMe at matched token budgets. At $1.40625^\circ$ and 50% token reduction, UtoMe-E lowers Overall error from 67.32 to 53.00 at the same 0.55x encoder FLOPs. Small reductions remain close to the full-token baseline; larger reductions incur measurable accuracy losses. Component ablations and spatial uncertainty controls support combining dynamics with aligned uncertainty when allocating a weather transformer's token budget.

title: VTF900: A 900-Subject Visible-Thermal Face Recognition Dataset and Benchmark
summary: Despite advancements in visible-thermal face recognition, where thermal probe (query) face images are matched against visible enrollment templates, existing benchmarks are currently limited by small gallery sizes (N $\approx$ 100 subjects). This limitation inhibits the ability to accurately evaluate visible-thermal facial recognition at scale and to report significant recognition performance metrics, which have better operational relevance. Therefore, we introduce VTF900, a large-scale visible-thermal face recognition benchmark with 900 subjects and paired imagery that includes expression, pose, and occlusion variations. VTF900 is designed to support large-scale (i.e., large gallery) evaluations across verification (1:1 matching) and closed-set identification (1:N matching) for visible-thermal face recognition. Furthermore, VTF900 specifically addresses the challenging combination of cross-spectral and cross-dataset analysis. In this paper, after training models on the ARL-VTF dataset, we provide benchmark analyses across convolutional (baseline), vision transformers, and domain-adaptive neural network architectures to assess how these methods scale. At full gallery scale (N = 900), transformer models achieve strong discriminative performance under frontal conditions (e.g., ViT-B: 97.68% AUC, 51.10% TAR@1%FAR), while domain-adaptive methods such as DPIT-ResNet50 demonstrate greater robustness under off-pose conditions (94.68%AUC, 36.08% TAR@1%FAR). Our results show that high AUC at small scale does not translate to reliable performance at deployment scale, and that pose variation significantly amplifies performance degradation. VTF900 exposes these limitations, enabling more rigorous evaluation of cross-spectral face recognition systems.

title: ViCoR: Estimating Visual Necessity via Counterfactual Residuals for Multimodal Medical Data Selection
summary: Medical vision-language models often exhibit hidden stratification, where high overall performance masks failures on subtle visual findings and overlapping clinical conditions. We trace this failure mode to modality imbalance during fine-tuning, where strong linguistic priors can suppress visually grounded learning and induce plausible but weakly grounded rationales. Existing data selection methods usually score image-text pairs as holistic units, without separating visually necessary samples from shortcut-solvable ones. To address this problem, we propose ViCoR, a counterfactual-residual-based data selection method for Med-VLM fine-tuning. ViCoR estimates visual necessity through image-dependent optimization residuals, calibrates the resulting scores with medical supervision compatibility, and constructs a diversity-aware fine-tuning subset. Across two backbones, four external generalization benchmarks, and one multi-disease robustness benchmark, ViCoR-selected 20\% subsets achieve the strongest average performance compared with full-data fine-tuning and selection baselines. Gradient-level analysis and perturbation audits further show that ViCoR enriches image-dependent training signals and strengthens image-level and evidence-region dependence. The code will be available at https://github.com/htgan-ai/ViCoR.

title: Visual Scaffolding: Toward Native Multimodal Reasoning
summary: The success of chain-of-thought (CoT) in complex reasoning can be attributed to a textual scaffolding effect: explicit intermediate results can be examined, reused, and composed to support subsequent reasoning, much as scaffolding supports a building under construction. However, mainstream multimodal LLMs lack an equivalent scaffold for visual distinctions that are difficult to express in concise verbal descriptions. We therefore ask: Can native visual representations become first-class citizens alongside language, providing a visual scaffold for reasoning? We define native multimodal reasoning as reasoning in which native visual representations and language jointly carry reusable intermediate states. As a concrete implementation, the visual scaffolding mechanism we proposed lets the MLLM autonomously initiate a retrieval action at any reasoning step. A lightweight retriever selects native visual features, which are then incorporated directly into the evolving CoT and remain available to subsequent steps. To evaluate this mechanism under controlled visual demands, we introduce NMR-Bench, comprising Burden Counting and Path Tracing. With 88M added parameters (approximately 2%) on Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking, our model achieves 66.43% and 72.50% accuracy, respectively, surpassing the evaluated GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro baselines. Controlled interventions show that changing selected visual content affects task accuracy and can redirect subsequent visual selection even when intervening text is held fixed. These findings show that native visual states can function as intermediate reasoning material and point toward reusable scaffolds for additional modalities.

title: Visual Sufficiency Landscapes: Understanding Query-Conditioned Reliability in Visual Token Pruning
summary: Different visual token pruning strategies retain different subsets while maintaining similar task performance. This motivates a combinatorial question: how many visual subsets can preserve model behavior, and how does their abundance depend on the query? We introduce visual sufficiency landscapes to characterize this abundance. At a fixed layer and budget, visual sufficiency probability is the fraction of uniformly sampled subsets that jointly preserve the dense model's answer, reference-answer likelihood, and output distribution. Independent sampling replicates separate input variation from estimation noise. Across Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL2-8B, and LLaVA-v1.5-7B, differences between inputs on GQA and TextVQA exceed replication error, and different questions about the same GQA image produce distinct landscapes. Sufficiency probability also improves failure prediction for full pruning methods. On LLaVA, adding this probability increases AUC by 0.1151 for FastV, 0.0683 for VisionZip, and 0.1401 for SparseVLM, while reducing log loss and Brier score. Several architecture-adapted configurations on the other two models reproduce these gains. Under controlled selection rules, predictors trained on the original images reduce log loss on new images by 9.0%, 13.0%, and 14.1%, respectively. These results establish successful-subset abundance as a measurable dimension of local prunability and connect it to the identification of high-risk pruning conditions.

title: What Can't Jev Decide? Probing the Limits of One-Pass Decision Models
summary: Jev and its open replicas choose among the options a caller supplies with a single forward pass, fast enough to decide inside an agent loop. We ask what such a model cannot decide, and find a simple limit: Jev cannot make a decision that an LLM makes only by writing out intermediate steps. On a benchmark that varies one factor at a time, Jev finds and selects records without error up to 20k tokens and 64 options, but once the answer depends on two or more updates of one user, accuracy falls, to 53-80% at sixteen updates, because similar records interfere. Given a stale summary of the state, Jev follows it. On real decision items graded by how many thinking tokens a reference LLM needs, Jev answers 97.5% of the items that one forward pass of that LLM solves, but only 74% of the others. Jev also does not know its limit: its confidence flags the errors it makes itself but not those it inherits from a stale input, and neither an explicit nor a trained hand-off option catches the latter. The open models we evaluate share these limits. Checking the state such models rely on requires a model that reasons.

title: When Form Changes but Logic Doesn't: Building Logic-invariant LLMs through Logical Structure
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance across diverse reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether this performance reflects an understanding of underlying logical structure or a reliance on shallow semantic cues. A key indicator of such understanding is whether models treat logically equivalent inputs consistently, producing the same predictions despite differences in expression. Through systematic evaluation on curated data, we show that even strong LLMs often fail this test: they do not consistently preserve predictions across logically equivalent inputs and generalize poorly to unseen logical forms. To address this limitation, we propose LoGIcal STructure-guided reasoning (LoGIST), a framework that guides LLM reasoning with explicit logical structure. LoGIST maps each input instance to a decision diagram, a directed acyclic graph that captures the underlying logical structure, and encodes this graph into a logical embedding that conditions the LLM's reasoning process. Across multiple training settings, LoGIST reduces inconsistency under logical equivalence and improves generalization to unseen logical forms, suggesting that logical invariance is a useful target for building more robust and generalizable logical reasoning in LLMs.

title: Where Groups Split: A Probe Prior for Nonzero Within-Group Variance in RL Post-Training
summary: Group relative policy optimization learns from a prompt only when the rewards in the sampled group disagree. With a binary verifier, a group that is entirely correct or entirely incorrect has within-group variance zero and a zero advantage. Uniform sampling continues to spend rollouts on prompts that are unanimous now and stay unanimous as training goes on. Pass rate is a weak forecast of that future. Two prompts at the same pass rate can move apart: one into the range where a finite group splits, and one toward a ceiling where the group becomes unanimous again. Aperture estimates the later pass rate from a short probe. A small subset of the pool is trained with the same recipe, every prompt is scored on the base model and on the probe model, and the two pass rates are plugged into the probability that a group of the training size is all wrong or split. The resulting weight is a static prior. It can be used alone or multiplied by an online scheduler, and the GRPO update is left as it is. On mathematical and logical reasoning with 1.7B and 4B models, the prior improves greedy accuracy over uniform GRPO and raises the fraction of groups with a nonzero advantage. The same prior still helps when it is combined with dynamic sampling or with selective rollouts.

title: Where and Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail When Reasoning over Rapidly Evolving Knowledge
summary: As the world changes, new information is published while older records remain online. This complicates reasoning for large language models (LLMs), which must retrieve evidence and resolve conflicts to determine which information remains valid. Existing evaluations treat information seeking as a black box, revealing little about where and why LLMs fail. To address this gap, we introduce TREK, a suite of three components: TREKTRACE is a plug-and-play framework that attributes failures to specific stages of retrieval and reasoning. We apply it to TREKBENCH-WILD, a meta-benchmark of real-world questions that require complex reasoning over rapidly evolving knowledge. Surprisingly, the main bottleneck is post-retrieval reasoning rather than retrieval: frontier models are often misled by conflicting evidence even after retrieving all the information needed to answer. To study this bottleneck, we build TREKBENCH-CTRL, a controlled benchmark with distractors spanning temporality, relevance, and trustworthiness, and show that benchmarks dominated by outdated distractors substantially underestimate task difficulty. Together, TREK provides a testbed for diagnosing and improving reasoning over rapidly evolving knowledge.

title: Whistle and Wrong Lyrics: Synthetic Queries Are Not Enough for Real-World Query-by-Melody
summary: People look up a song by humming it, but also by whistling it or singing it with the wrong words. Published query-by-humming systems and benchmarks focus on hums and sung queries, and no public dataset pairs whistles or wrong-lyrics singing with song recordings. We study both query types with a melody-only retrieval system: a key-normalized pitch track embedded by a 5.2M-parameter contour encoder, with a spectral-peak tracker for whistles. First, a physics-grounded generator renders synthetic whistles and nonsense-syllable singing from the vocal melodies of 11,083 songs. Training on them raises top-1 retrieval of held-out synthetic queries against an 11,050-song gallery from 0.180 to 0.251 for whistles and from 0.193 to 0.264 for wrong-lyrics singing, but the gain does not transfer: on the MLEnd test performers the best synthetic-only model gets 210 of 339 real whistles right at top-1, against 214 for the baseline. Second, a closed-set fine-tune on real MLEnd whistles with performer-disjoint splits raises whistle-to-hum top-1 from 0.631 (95% CI 0.581-0.681) to 0.673 (0.622-0.723), on known songs only. Third, two further generations of synthetic queries also fail to transfer: melody-conditioned whistles and la-la singing from a commercial neural music model leave real-whistle top-1 at 0.631, and an open-source pipeline (YingMusic-Singer-Plus singing with partly wrong, mumbled or nonsense lyrics, a DDSP whistle synthesizer, and a melody-error model fitted on real performers) gives at best 0.619 (paired difference -0.012, 95% CI -0.038 to +0.015). Across physics-based, commercial neural and open-source neural synthetic data, nothing transferred to real whistles, which points to collecting real queries as the missing step. Code is public; models and data will be released.

title: Who Gets Unmasked? Sampler-Induced Bias in Diffusion Language Models
summary: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate by gradually unmasking a canvas, so their samplers decide not only which token to write but also when to commit it. We show that this second decision changes who appears in generated text, a sampler-induced bias on top of the model's own. Common commit rules, including LLaDA's default, commit the positions whose sampled tokens are most probable; this peeking favors majority options. To separate the sampler from the model, we read the model's belief about a fork, such as a protagonist's gender, in one forward pass, and show that this belief matches exact sampling from the model. Measured against it, peeking samplers on LLaDA and Dream amplify occupational gender stereotypes and collapse opinion distributions, and confidence-based ordering shifts gender-balanced occupations toward men, more so under faster parallel decoding. We propose Fork-First Sampling, which decides the fork before anything else is written: it follows the belief or any target distribution, improves fluency, and avoids the stories that remark on the protagonist's gender, which prompt-based fixes produce, at the cost of one forward pass. Fairness evaluations of dLLMs should report the commit rule.

title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
summary: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.
summary_zh: 世界模型使具身智能体能够预判行为后果，然而，由于异构动作空间和多模态监督数据的稀缺，跨不同具身形态联合建模移动与操控仍具挑战。我们提出了Ropedia W0，这是首个覆盖人类及多种具身形态机器人的以自我为中心的移动-操控世界基础模型。我们构建了Xp-Data数据集，包含10,000小时以自我为中心的人类数据和3,000小时机器人数据，具备统一的多模态标注和系统性质量控制。一种统一的运动学表示通过相机位姿编码移动行为，通过投影骨架编码操控行为，其中机器人骨架将具身特定的正向运动学与大规模人工关键点标注及修正相结合。我们还引入了Xp-Teleop，一个基于高质量灵巧人形遥操作数据的长时程移动-操控基准。评估结果表明，在五个跨具身形态基准（DreamDojo、$Ψ_0$、$ω$-HOME、Xp-Teleop和AgiBot）以及留出的人类自我中心视频上，从零样本推理到少样本和全数据后训练，均取得了最先进的性能。扩展人类预训练数据可同时提升人类和机器人评估的性能。经过蒸馏后，我们的模型支持实时的、分钟级的长时程生成，实现实时VR交互。在策略评估、基于模型的规划以及世界-动作建模中的应用进一步展示了该模型在具身决策中的实用价值。
tldr: Ropedia W0 introduces the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model trained on 10k hours of human and 3k hours of robot data, unifying locomotion and manipulation across embodiments via a shared kinematic representation, and achieving SOTA on multiple benchmarks with real-time distilled rollouts.
tldr_zh: Ropedia W0 提出了首个以自我为中心的运动-操作世界基础模型，利用 1 万小时人类数据和 3 千小时机器人数据进行训练，通过统一运动学表示跨实体建模运动与操作，在多个基准上达到 SOTA，并支持实时 VR 交互。

title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control
summary: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. We propose HAF-VLA, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control. Built upon a pretrained flow-matching VLA, HAF-VLA inherits the vision-language prefix encoder and action expert weights, and adapts them to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with learnable stage embeddings and cross-stage KV-cache conditioning. Instead of generating the full action chunk in a single pass, HAF-VLA progressively denoises a shared whole-body action space: first locomotion and head commands, then waist refinement, and finally full-body manipulation. To preserve structural dependencies across stages, we introduce a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism, enabling subsequent action generation stages to refine and augment their outputs based on the action representations from preceding stages. Experimental results across six real-world tasks demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, demonstrating an effective pathway for adapting strong mobile-manipulation VLAs to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.
summary_zh: 人形机器人在以人为中心的环境中作为通用智能体展现出巨大潜力，然而将通用视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略适配到真实世界的人形移动操作任务仍然面临挑战。与固定基座或轮式机械臂不同，人形机器人需要在高维全身动作空间中协调运动、姿态、视线和双臂操作，其中不精确的基座或腰部运动极易引发不稳定且激烈的手臂补偿行为。我们提出HAF-VLA，一种面向人形机器人VLA控制的分层动作流框架。基于预训练的流匹配VLA，HAF-VLA继承了视觉-语言前缀编码器和动作专家权重，并通过可学习的阶段嵌入和跨阶段KV缓存条件机制将其适配到人形全身移动操作任务。HAF-VLA并非一次性生成完整动作块，而是逐步去噪共享的全身动作空间：首先生成运动与头部指令，然后是腰部细化，最后生成全身操作动作。为保持各阶段之间的结构依赖关系，我们引入跨阶段KV缓存条件机制，使后续动作生成阶段能够基于前序阶段的动作表示对其输出进行细化和增强。跨六个真实世界任务的实验结果表明，我们的框架显著提升了现有模型在人形移动操作任务中的性能，为将强大的移动操作VLA适配到人形全身移动操作提供了一条有效路径。
tldr: HAF-VLA introduces a hierarchical action-flow framework that adapts pretrained VLA models to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation via stage embeddings, cross-stage KV-cache conditioning, and progressive denoising, improving real-world tasks.
tldr_zh: HAF-VLA 提出了一种分层动作流框架，通过阶段嵌入、跨阶段KV缓存条件和渐进去噪，将预训练VLA模型适配到人形机器人全身移动操作，并在真实世界任务中提升了性能。

title: FR-VLA: Implicit Force Reasoning VLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: Integrating force awareness into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models involves not merely encoding wrench measurements as an additional modality, but determining when and how strongly physical interaction should influence robot action generation. Existing VLAs that use force typically inject it through a fixed pathway, without explicitly determining when it is relevant to the current action. This calls for an intermediate force relevance mechanism inside the VLA, in which visual-language context estimates the relevance of physical feedback to the current task before force enters the action pathway. FR-VLA addresses this gap with a Vision-Language Force-Reasoning Model that uses learnable force query tokens to derive a force admission signal grounded in visual-language context, and uses this signal to modulate an external tokenized force pathway for action generation. In real-world experiments on five contact-rich tasks across two robotic platforms, FR-VLA achieves the highest mean success rate over six evaluated stages, and trajectory visualizations show that its force admission varies with the interaction phase.
summary_zh: 将力觉感知融入视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型，不仅涉及将力/力矩测量作为额外模态进行编码，更关键的是确定物理交互应在何时以及以何种强度影响机器人动作生成。现有使用力信息的VLA模型通常通过固定路径注入力数据，并未显式判断该信息与当前动作的相关性。这要求在VLA内部建立一种中间力相关性机制，使视觉-语言上下文在力信息进入动作路径之前，先评估物理反馈与当前任务的相关性。FR-VLA通过引入视觉-语言力推理模型解决了这一空白，该模型利用可学习的力查询令牌，基于视觉-语言上下文推导出力接纳信号，并以此信号调制外部令牌化力路径，用于动作生成。在两个机器人平台的五项接触密集任务真实世界实验中，FR-VLA在六个评估阶段中取得了最高平均成功率，轨迹可视化结果表明其力接纳程度随交互阶段动态变化。
tldr: FR-VLA introduces a Vision-Language Force-Reasoning Model that learns a force admission signal from visual-language context to modulate force input in VLA action generation, improving contact-rich manipulation on real robots.
tldr_zh: FR-VLA提出了一种视觉-语言力推理模型，通过从视觉-语言上下文学习力准入信号来调节VLA动作生成中的力输入，从而提升真实机器人上的接触丰富操作性能。

title: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
summary: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. We propose CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding. Given a sequence of cached per-frame features from the VLM backbone, CondenseVLA distills observation history into a fixed set of slot tokens using learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention. Simple auxiliary regularization penalizes overlap among slot attention maps and decorrelates slot embeddings, encouraging complementary attention and reducing slot redundancy. Across the evaluated tasks, CondenseVLA improves Simpler-WidowX success from 58.7% to 69.8% (+11.1 percentage points), achieves 97.2% on LIBERO, and reaches 52.8% on real-world tasks. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA
summary_zh: 机器人操控往往依赖于短期线索——例如短暂的接触、暂时的遮挡以及中间物体状态——这些线索在单帧中具有模糊性，唯有通过跨时间的观测整合才能加以解析。然而，仅通过扩大历史窗口来注入历史信息，计算成本高昂，且由于观测存在大量冗余以及任务无关、不灵活的采样方式，其增益往往十分有限。我们提出CondenseVLA，一种多帧VLA策略，配备可学习的解码端历史信息压缩模块，用于在动作解码中利用短期视觉上下文。给定来自VLM骨干网络的缓存逐帧特征序列，CondenseVLA通过可学习查询和多头交叉注意力，将观测历史蒸馏为一组固定数量的槽位令牌。简单的辅助正则化方法对槽位注意力图之间的重叠施加惩罚，并对槽位嵌入进行去相关，从而促进互补性注意力并减少槽位冗余。在评估的所有任务中，CondenseVLA将Simpler-WidowX的成功率从58.7%提升至69.8%（提升11.1个百分点），在LIBERO上达到97.2%，在真实世界任务中达到52.8%。在依赖记忆的RMBench任务上，其成功率达到21.6%。这些结果支持对有限的近期视觉证据进行选择性压缩以用于动作解码，同时，更难的多观测任务也揭示了有限历史窗口的局限性。项目页面：https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA
tldr: CondenseVLA introduces a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for multi-frame Vision-Language-Action models, distilling cached visual features into a fixed set of slot tokens via cross-attention and auxiliary regularization, improving memory-dependent manipulation success on Simpler-WidowX, LIBERO, real-world, and RMBench benchmarks.
tldr_zh: CondenseVLA 提出了一种可学习的解码端历史浓缩模块，通过交叉注意力和辅助正则化将缓存的视觉特征蒸馏为固定数量的槽令牌，从而提升记忆依赖的机器人操作成功率（Simpler-WidowX、LIBERO、真实世界和RMBench）。

title: Long-Horizon Multi-Object Rearrangement via Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions
summary: Despite recent advances in policy learning, long-horizon manipulation remains difficult because learned policies must avoid compounding errors while preserving future feasibility. While search-based planning can explicitly reason over such future consequences, it quickly becomes expensive in high-dimensional continuous action spaces. This raises a central question: how can long-horizon reasoning from search be transferred into policies in continuous action spaces? To this end, we propose DISCO: Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions. DISCO uses progressive-widening MCTS in physics simulation to generate long-horizon plans. During search, a learned policy proposes continuous actions, while a learned value function scores actions by their expected progress toward task completion. Using GPU-parallelized simulation, DISCO periodically distills MCTS-generated plans into the policy-value model, improving the action proposals and value estimates used in subsequent searches. Finally, the learned policy-value model can be directly deployed without the need for simulator-based search at test time. Across simulated and real-world rearrangement tasks, DISCO outperforms behavior cloning, reinforcement learning, and search-based baselines.
summary_zh: 尽管策略学习近期取得了进展，但长程操作仍然困难重重，因为学习到的策略必须避免累积误差，同时保持未来可行性。虽然基于搜索的规划能够显式推理此类未来后果，但在高维连续动作空间中，其计算代价迅速变得高昂。这引出了一个核心问题：如何将搜索中的长程推理迁移到连续动作空间中的策略中？为此，我们提出了DISCO：连续动作上的蒸馏树搜索。DISCO利用物理仿真中的渐进加宽蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）生成长程规划。在搜索过程中，学习到的策略提出连续动作，而学习到的价值函数则根据动作对任务完成预期进展的贡献对其进行评分。借助GPU并行仿真，DISCO定期将MCTS生成的规划蒸馏到策略-价值模型中，从而改进后续搜索中使用的动作提议和价值估计。最终，学习到的策略-价值模型可直接部署，无需在测试时依赖基于仿真的搜索。在模拟和真实世界的重排任务中，DISCO均优于行为克隆、强化学习以及基于搜索的基线方法。
tldr: DISCO combines progressive-widening MCTS with learned policy and value networks in physics simulation, distilling search-derived plans into a policy-value model for long-horizon multi-object rearrangement, achieving superior performance over baselines in simulated and real-world tasks.
tldr_zh: DISCO将渐进式扩展的蒙特卡洛树搜索与学习到的策略和价值网络结合，在物理仿真中生成长期规划，并将搜索产生的计划蒸馏到策略-价值模型中，在仿真和真实世界的多目标重排任务上优于基线方法。

title: SWAP: Test-Time Steerable Humanoid Whole-Body Collision Avoidance
summary:
Humanoid robots operating in human-centric environments must coordinate the entire body to traverse tight, cluttered spaces while maintaining balance. Existing methods often struggle to jointly consider dynamic stability and collision avoidance from high-dimensional perceptual inputs. Moreover, for humanoids, safe behavior is inherently multimodal: the same obstacle may admit multiple valid traversals, which is difficult to represent with a single deterministic policy. To address these challenges, we propose SWAP (Steerable Whole-body Avoidance Policy), a hierarchical framework that separates collision-aware decision making from stabilization. A high-level, perception-conditioned diffusion policy generates multimodal, collision-aware motion proposals, while a low-level whole-body RL controller tracks these proposals and maintains dynamic balance. To efficiently train the high-level policy, we obtain scalable supervision via hindsight labeling: we roll out the low-level policy under randomized commands, place obstacles only in the space that each executed motion did not sweep, so the motion is collision-free by construction, and re-render the perception the robot would have seen. At deployment, Monte Carlo sampling with simple cost signals steers the diffusion model toward safe, task-aligned behaviors without heavy reward tuning.
  Experiments in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid show reliable avoidance with static and dynamic obstacles. Test-time steering further enables customization, improving targeted rewards (e.g., speed, orientation, or posture) by 34% on average while maintaining a high collision avoidance rate. Together, these results support a practical solution to humanoid whole-body collision avoidance with test-time steerability. Project website: https://iscoyizj.github.io/SWAP-steerable-humanoid-oa-website/
summary_zh:
摘要：
在以人为本的环境中操作的人形机器人必须协调全身动作，以在狭窄、杂乱的空间中穿行并保持平衡。现有方法通常难以从高维感知输入中联合考虑动态稳定性与碰撞避免。此外，对于人形机器人而言，安全行为本质上是多模态的：同一障碍物可能存在多种有效的通行方式，而单一确定性策略难以表征这种多样性。为解决上述挑战，我们提出了SWAP（可操控全身避碰策略），一种将碰撞感知决策与稳定控制分离的层级框架。高层策略采用基于感知条件的扩散策略，生成多模态、碰撞感知的运动提案；低层策略则通过全身强化学习控制器跟踪这些提案并维持动态平衡。为高效训练高层策略，我们通过事后标注获得可扩展的监督信号：在随机指令下 rollout 低层策略，仅在执行运动未扫掠的空间中放置障碍物，从而使该运动在构造上保证无碰撞，并重新渲染机器人本应看到的感知信息。在部署阶段，通过蒙特卡洛采样结合简单代价信号，引导扩散模型朝向安全且符合任务目标的行为，而无需繁重的奖励调参。在仿真和真实 Unitree G1 人形机器人上的实验表明，该方法能够可靠地避开静态与动态障碍物。测试时引导进一步支持行为定制，在保持高避碰率的同时，目标奖励（如速度、朝向或姿态）平均提升34%。上述结果共同支撑了一种兼具测试时可操控性的实用化人形机器人全身避碰解决方案。项目网站：https://iscoyizj.github.io/SWAP-steerable-humanoid-oa-website/
tldr: SWAP introduces a hierarchical framework for humanoid whole-body collision avoidance, combining a high-level diffusion policy for multimodal motion generation with a low-level RL controller for stabilization, and enables test-time steering via cost-guided sampling in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 robot.
tldr_zh: SWAP提出了一个用于人形机器人全身避碰的分层框架，结合高层扩散策略生成多模态运动与低层强化学习控制器维持稳定，并在仿真和真实Unitree G1机器人上实现测试时引导以定制行为。

title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
summary: Multimodal reasoning provides robotic foundation models with predictive context needed for reliable action generation. However, language-based reasoning captures task semantics but struggles to express fine-grained physical dynamics, while latent reasoning models future state evolution but offers limited structure for organizing these dynamics into reusable reasoning primitives. To bridge this gap, we introduce PhysWord, a reasoning-before-acting foundation model built on Physical Words, which use atomic action verbs as shared semantic anchors for continuous representations of physical dynamics. Specifically, PhysWord predicts upcoming atomic action words and directly aligns their contextual hidden states with latent targets derived from the corresponding future observations. Building on these primitives, we construct a temporally structured PhysWord space with visual and optional tactile variants of each action word. Autoregressively predicting Physical Words across future timesteps captures transitions between execution stages, providing structured multimodal context for action generation. PhysWord achieves state-of-the-art success rates of 90.3\% on visuotactile UniVTAC and 99.6\% on vision-based LIBERO-Long, and outperforms competing methods on real-world tasks using bimanual grippers and dexterous hands. Further evaluations demonstrate that our structured latent reasoning framework generalizes to unseen scenarios and enables long-horizon manipulation.
summary_zh: 多模态推理为机器人基础模型提供了生成可靠动作所需的预测性上下文。然而，基于语言的推理虽能捕捉任务语义，却难以表达细粒度的物理动力学；而潜在推理虽可预测未来状态演化，但缺乏足够的结构来将这些动力学组织为可复用的推理原语。为弥合这一鸿沟，我们提出了PhysWord——一种基于“物理词汇”（Physical Words）构建的“先推理后行动”基础模型。物理词汇以原子动作动词作为连续物理动力学表征的共享语义锚点。具体而言，PhysWord预测即将发生的原子动作词，并将其上下文隐藏状态直接与由对应未来观测导出的潜在目标对齐。基于这些原语，我们构建了一个具有时间结构的PhysWord空间，其中每个动作词均包含视觉及可选触觉变体。跨未来时间步自回归地预测物理词汇，可捕捉执行阶段之间的转换，从而为动作生成提供结构化的多模态上下文。PhysWord在视觉触觉数据集UniVTAC上达到了90.3%的最新成功率，在基于视觉的LIBERO-Long上达到99.6%，并在使用双手夹爪和灵巧手的真实世界任务中优于现有方法。进一步评估表明，我们的结构化潜在推理框架能够泛化至未见场景，并支持长时程操作任务。
tldr: PhysWord introduces Physical Words, atomic action verbs serving as semantic anchors for latent reasoning in robot manipulation, achieving state-of-the-art success on UniVTAC, LIBERO-Long, and real-world bimanual/dexterous tasks.
tldr_zh: PhysWord 提出了物理词汇，以原子动作动词作为潜在推理的语义锚点，在 UniVTAC、LIBERO-Long 以及真实双臂/灵巧手任务上取得了最先进成果。

title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
summary: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. Leveraging cooperation effectively for both prediction and navigation remains a major challenge. We propose CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making. CoopUQ predicts future occupancy grid maps through cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion and further leverages forecasts and their uncertainty to guide policy via constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the cost penalizes navigation through regions predicted to be occupied or highly uncertain. This design enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts. Experimental results across multiple Unity3D-based simulation environments with both in-distribution and OOD settings, including diverse layouts, pedestrian densities, and rushing behavior, demonstrate improved prediction performance and safety over representative baselines. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate its robustness across various scenes. Our code and videos are available at https://coopuq.github.io/.
summary_zh: 强化学习使移动机器人在受限的人机共享环境中能够做出快速且可扩展的导航决策。然而，将单机器人方法直接扩展到多机器人场景往往无法确保安全性和效率，尤其是在遮挡和分布外（OOD）情境下，此时单个机器人可能会忽视潜在风险或做出不准确的预测。如何有效利用协作来同时改善预测和导航仍然是一个重大挑战。我们提出了CoopUQ，一个多机器人社交导航框架，该框架将不确定性感知的协同占用预测与稳健决策制定相结合。CoopUQ通过跨机器人的时空特征融合预测未来占用栅格图，并进一步利用预测结果及其不确定性，通过带约束的多智能体强化学习来引导策略，其中代价函数对穿越预测为占用或高度不确定区域的导航行为进行惩罚。这一设计使策略能够在分布偏移下调整其风险敏感度。在多个基于Unity3D的仿真环境中进行的实验，涵盖了分布内和分布外设置，包括多样化的布局、行人密度和急行行为，结果表明，与代表性基线方法相比，所提出的方法在预测性能和安全性能上均有提升。真实机器人实验进一步验证了其在不同场景下的稳健性。我们的代码和视频可在https://coopuq.github.io/获取。
tldr: CoopUQ introduces a multi-robot social navigation framework that fuses uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasts to guide a constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning policy, improving safety in occluded and out-of-distribution scenarios.
tldr_zh: CoopUQ 提出了一种多机器人社交导航框架，通过跨机器人不确定性感知的占用预测来引导约束多智能体强化学习策略，在遮挡和分布外场景下提升了安全性。

title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
summary: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. We introduce PhysRSI-eval to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure. Different VLMs are evaluated on 18 manipulation tasks under a fixed interaction budget. The analysis of experimental results motivates the Physical Barrel Hypothesis: different capabilities may constrain different parts of improvement. The five-axis metrics also distinguish systems with close public benchmark averages and show that high scores need not come with early or efficient gains. We study observational scaling from two perspectives: predicting the relative performance of VLM agents from their public capabilities, and forecasting later progress from early physical feedback. Together, these analyses ask how quickly and how far an agent can improve. Moreover, we conduct workspace interventions and then analyze what improvement leaves behind. Removing history reduces late-round success, frozen workspaces remain useful on unseen layouts, and three cross-task cases achieve success earlier. The results suggest that scene-specific adaptation and reusable experience can coexist.
summary_zh: 在本文中，我们系统性地探讨了物理递归自我改进的机制、缩放行为及其泛化能力。我们引入了PhysRSI-eval，通过五轴指标体系来量化物理RSI：首次尝试表现、效率、成功率、预算及失败中获得的改进。在固定的交互预算下，我们针对18项操作任务评估了不同的视觉语言模型（VLM）。对实验结果的分析引出了“物理桶假说”：不同的能力或许会限制改进过程中的不同环节。五轴指标也能区分那些在公开基准上平均分接近的系统，并表明高分未必伴随着早期或高效的增益。我们从两个角度研究观测缩放：一是根据VLM代理的公开能力预测其相对表现，二是从早期的物理反馈中预测后续进展。这些分析共同探讨了代理能够以多快的速度以及多远程度实现改进。此外，我们进行了工作区干预，并分析了改进后留下的痕迹。移除历史记录会降低后几轮的成功率，冻结的工作区在未见过的布局上依然有效，且三个跨任务案例更早达到了成功。这些结果表明，针对特定场景的适应与可复用的经验能够共存。
tldr: The paper introduces PhysRSI-eval, a five-axis benchmark for physical recursive self-improvement in VLM-based robotic manipulation, and proposes the Physical Barrel Hypothesis. It analyzes scaling laws predicting agent improvement from public capabilities and early feedback, and studies workspace interventions.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了用于评估VLM机器人操作中物理递归自我改进能力的五轴基准PhysRSI-eval，并提出了物理桶假说。通过观测缩放定律分析从公开能力和早期反馈预测智能体改进，并研究了工作区干预的影响。

title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: Recent advances in multimodal models have enabled GPT-6 Astra to perform robotic manipulation through in-context learning. Yet contact-rich control and tactile perception are often regarded as strengths of specialist policies, leaving open whether Astra can directly understand and use tactile observations. We provide, to our knowledge, the first demonstration that Astra directly interprets vision-based tactile images and uses their contact cues for manipulation. Tactile RGB images enter through its existing visual interface, enabling few-shot closed-loop control on nineteen simulated UniVTAC and OpenViTac tasks with 210 sampled scene seeds per setting. With visuo-tactile input, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% and 81.8%, exceeding the strongest reported specialist baselines in our comparison by 22.9 and 13.1 percentage points, respectively. Vision-only performance also leads these baselines, reaching 76.3% and 80.6%. Trajectory analysis reveals active probing, cautious grasping, contact-guided alignment, and recovery, alongside difficulties with tangential loading and corrective execution. Our findings challenge the exclusivity of specialist policies in contact-rich manipulation and show that fine-grained vision can partially compensate for missing touch. They also identify vision-based tactile sensing as an interface for scaling contact understanding with foundation models and reveal signs of benchmark saturation. These results motivate joint visual-tactile pretraining, harder contact-rich evaluations, and physical-robot validation.
summary_zh: 近期多模态模型的进展使得GPT-6 Astra能够通过上下文学习执行机器人操作任务。然而，富含接触的控制与触觉感知通常被视为专家策略系统的优势所在，因此尚不明确Astra是否能够直接理解并利用触觉观测信息。我们首次证明了Astra能够直接解读基于视觉的触觉图像，并利用其中的接触线索进行操控。触觉RGB图像通过其现有的视觉接口输入，从而在19个模拟UniViTAC和OpenViTac任务上实现了少样本闭环控制，每个设置采样210个场景种子。在视觉-触觉联合输入下，Astra的平均成功率达到93.8%和81.8%，分别比我们对比中最强的已报道专家基线高出22.9和13.1个百分点。仅依赖视觉输入的性能也同样优于这些基线，分别达到76.3%和80.6%。轨迹分析揭示了主动探测、谨慎抓取、接触引导的对准以及恢复行为，同时暴露出其在切向载荷和纠错执行方面的困难。我们的研究结果挑战了专家策略在富含接触操作任务中的独占性，并表明细粒度视觉在一定程度上可以弥补触觉信息的缺失。此外，研究还识别出基于视觉的触觉感知可作为扩展基础模型接触理解能力的一种接口，并揭示了基准测试趋于饱和的迹象。这些发现为视觉-触觉联合预训练、更具挑战性的接触丰富评估以及物理机器人验证提供了有力的动机。
tldr: This paper demonstrates that GPT-6 Astra, a multimodal model, can directly interpret vision-based tactile images for contact-rich manipulation, achieving higher success rates than specialist baselines on simulated UniVTac and OpenViTac tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文证明多模态模型 GPT-6 Astra 可以直接解读基于视觉的触觉图像并进行接触丰富的操作，在 UniVTac 和 OpenViTac 模拟任务上成功率超过专家基线。

title: PICA-WAM: Visual Perturbation Invariance via Cross-Appearance Self-Alignment in World Action Models
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future video and generate actions, yet remain sensitive to task-irrelevant visual perturbations, i.e., changes in visual appearance that should not affect robot behavior. We identify a gap in conventional WAM training: video prediction encourages representations to preserve appearance information, while action generation does not explicitly enforce invariance to task-irrelevant appearance. Data augmentation exposes WAMs to such perturbations but does not require perturbed and nominal observations to produce consistent action representations, and alignment with external pretrained features does not guarantee the desired invariance. To address this gap, we propose PICA-WAM, a self-supervised training framework that casts perturbation invariance as an auxiliary cross-appearance self-alignment task for WAMs. An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher processes the nominal observation to provide a deeper-layer target, while the online WAM processes a perturbed observation and aligns its shallower-layer action representation to this target through a lightweight projection head. Across four strong WAMs evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO-Plus, EBench, and a real robot, PICA-WAM consistently improves robustness under visual perturbations, preserves nominal performance in simulation, and raises the real robot success rate. PICA-WAM further reduces the sensitivity of video features to task-irrelevant appearance and its propagation into actions, as shown by paired layer-wise diagnostics. Code: https://github.com/YudeZou/PICA-WAM-release
summary_zh: 世界动作模型（WAMs）联合预测未来视频并生成动作，但对任务无关的视觉扰动（即不应影响机器人行为的视觉外观变化）仍较为敏感。我们发现了传统WAM训练中的一个不足：视频预测促使表征保留外观信息，而动作生成并未明确强制对任务无关外观的不变性。数据增强使WAMs暴露于此类扰动，但并未要求扰动观测与标称观测产生一致的动作表征，且与外部预训练特征的对齐也无法保证所期望的不变性。为解决这一问题，我们提出了PICA-WAM，一种自监督训练框架，将扰动不变性作为WAMs的辅助跨外观自对齐任务。指数移动平均（EMA）教师网络处理标称观测以提供深层目标，而在线WAM处理扰动观测，并通过轻量级投影头将其浅层动作表征与该目标对齐。在RoboTwin 2.0、LIBERO-Plus、EBench及真实机器人上评估的四种强WAMs中，PICA-WAM持续提升了视觉扰动下的鲁棒性，保持了仿真中的标称性能，并提高了真实机器人的成功率。成对逐层诊断进一步表明，PICA-WAM降低了视频特征对任务无关外观的敏感性及其向动作的传播。代码：https://github.com/YudeZou/PICA-WAM-release
tldr: PICA-WAM introduces a self-supervised cross-appearance self-alignment training framework that improves the robustness of World Action Models to task-irrelevant visual perturbations by aligning action representations from perturbed observations to nominal ones via an EMA teacher, showing consistent gains in simulation and on a real robot.
tldr_zh: PICA-WAM提出了一种基于交叉外观自对齐的自监督训练框架，通过EMA教师网络将扰动观测的动作表示与名义观测对齐，从而提升世界动作模型对任务无关视觉扰动的鲁棒性，并在仿真和真实机器人上取得一致提升。

title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
summary: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. Across diffusion, vision-language-action, world-action, and prompted VLM-based methods, the best trained multi-task policy achieves 29.1% Core-50 success. Without benchmark finetuning, GPT-6 using move_eef for palm-and-finger control achieves 5.2% on Core-50 and 1.9% on Transfer-16 over 660 trials. Trained-policy stage diagnostics expose failures in contact establishment, action coordination, and maintaining achieved goals, with additional sequencing errors in composed tasks. HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction.
summary_zh: 通用操作要求在具身、物体和任务需求之间保持可靠的行为表现。我们提出了HandsOn，一个用于跨具身灵巧操作的可组合仿真平台与基准。该平台支持五种机械臂、六种灵巧手，以及在随机化场景中约200种刚性、铰接和可变形资产。该基准将18,000个精心整理的人类演示与66个人工验证任务配对：Core-50支持基于演示的学习和执行测试，而Transfer-16评估资产与关系迁移、技能组合以及无目标任务训练演示的可变形操作。定性真实机器人 rollout 展示了仿真到真实的迁移效果。在扩散模型、视觉-语言-动作模型、世界-动作模型和基于提示的VLM方法中，最佳训练的多任务策略在Core-50上达到29.1%的成功率。在不进行基准微调的情况下，使用move_eef进行手掌-手指控制的GPT-6在660次试验中于Core-50上达到5.2%，在Transfer-16上达到1.9%。训练策略的阶段诊断揭示了接触建立、动作协调和已达成目标维持方面的失败，并在组合任务中出现额外的序列错误。HandsOn为研究操作泛化及可靠物理交互的极限提供了共享基础。
tldr: This paper introduces HandsOn, a large-scale simulation benchmark for generalizable dexterous manipulation, featuring 66 tasks, 18,000 human demonstrations, and evaluations of various policy learning methods including VLA and world-action models, with only 5.2% success for a prompted VLM. The benchmark enables the study of cross-embodiment, object, and task generalization in dexterous manipulation, including transfer and skill composition without target task demonstrations.
tldr_zh: 本文介绍了一个大规模仿真基准 HandsOn，用于可泛化的灵巧操作，包含66个任务、18,000个人类演示，并评估了包括VLA和世界动作模型在内的多种策略学习方法，其中提示VLM的成功率仅为5.2%。该基准支持跨本体、物体和任务泛化的研究，包括无需目标任务演示的迁移和技能组合。

title: DexOAK: Object-Aware Kinematic Retargeting
summary: We introduce DexOAK, a learning-based object-aware kinematic retargeting framework for generating contact-consistent robot hand references from human motion-capture data. DexOAK first minimizes an interaction-graph Laplacian objective over a joint hand-object graph, so the robot reproduces the demonstrated object-relative interaction geometry rather than the human hand pose alone. These per-frame solutions form seed retargeted references, from which a feed-forward network conditioned on human keypoints and object point clouds learns the retargeting function. Object-aware finetuning then refines the network under contact, non-penetration, and self-collision losses that position the fingers on the demonstrated contacts and reduce artifacts destabilizing physics-based refinement. Once trained, the network transfers to unseen data by inference alone, without per-frame optimization. DexOAK references improve dynamic retargeting over the state-of-the-art across bimanual tasks with rigid and articulated objects. On the Inspire hand, success rises from 39.5% to 48.4% on OakInk-v2, and ADD-AUC rises from 62.7% to 77.9% on ARCTIC. Ablations trace the gains to object-aware kinematic retargeting and the amortized network refined with contact losses. Trained on OakInk-v2, it transfers to ARCTIC zero-shot and nears in-domain performance after fine-tuning. On hardware, 46/56 open-loop replays succeed across five tasks, enabling dexterous robot data generation from human data. Visualizations and interactive results are at: https://fspinola.github.io/dexoak/.
summary_zh: 我们提出了DexOAK，一种基于学习的对象感知运动学重定向框架，用于从人体运动捕捉数据生成接触一致的机器人手部参考。DexOAK首先在联合的手-物图上最小化交互图拉普拉斯目标函数，从而使机器人复现所演示的相对于物体的交互几何结构，而不仅仅是人类手部姿态。这些逐帧解构成种子重定向参考，随后一个以人类关键点和物体点云为条件的前馈网络学习重定向函数。对象感知微调阶段在接触、非穿透和自碰撞损失下优化网络，从而将手指定位于演示接触点上，并减少会破坏基于物理的细化过程稳定性的人为伪影。训练完成后，该网络仅通过推理即可迁移至未见数据，无需逐帧优化。在涉及刚性和关节化物体的双手任务中，DexOAK参考相较现有最优方法显著提升了动态重定向性能。在Inspire手上，OakInk-v2数据集成功率从39.5%提升至48.4%，ARCTIC数据集ADD-AUC从62.7%提升至77.9%。消融实验将上述提升归因于对象感知运动学重定向以及经接触损失优化的分摊网络。该网络在OakInk-v2上训练后，可零样本迁移至ARCTIC，经微调后接近领域内性能。在硬件实验中，五个任务中46/56次开环重放取得成功，实现了从人类数据生成灵巧机器人数据。可视化结果及交互演示详见：https://fspinola.github.io/dexoak/。
tldr: DexOAK introduces an object-aware kinematic retargeting framework that generates contact-consistent robot hand references from human motion capture, improving dynamic retargeting and enabling hardware data generation.
tldr_zh: DexOAK提出了一种对象感知的运动学重定向框架，能够从人体运动捕捉生成接触一致的机器人手部参考，改善动态重定向并支持硬件数据生成。

title: Tactile In-Hand Object Rotation: A Comparative Study of Hand Morphology in Simulation and Hardware
summary: Continuous in-hand rotation requires coordinated contact maintenance and renewal, linking manipulation performance to both hand geometry and tactile feedback. We investigate these relationships through rotational progress, finger participation, and fingertip loading on two versions of the low-cost LEAP Hand with anthropomorphic and symmetric finger arrangements. Both hands are integrated with TacTip vision-based tactile sensors and use a shared reinforcement learning framework. Simulation evaluates full tactile, binary touch, and proprioception-only observations on 12 unseen objects; hardware experiments evaluate full tactile policies on ten objects under multiple hand orientations. In simulation, full tactile observations increase mean normalized rotation per episode over proprioception alone by 94.8% for the anthropomorphic hand and 66.9% for the symmetric hand, with longer mean episode durations and lower mean total fingertip loads. Hardware contact measurements reveal more differentiated finger participation in the anthropomorphic hand, while cumulative loading is more evenly distributed across the symmetric hand's fingers. Overall, the symmetric hand achieves a 32.0% higher mean rotation count and a 25.8% higher aggregate rotation rate, together with longer manipulation duration. Additional hardware force recordings show a 19.9% lower mean total fingertip load for this layout. These findings relate finger arrangement to contact organization and load sharing, and show that richer tactile information supports greater task progress at lower mean loading in both simulated embodiments.
summary_zh: 连续手内旋转需要协调的接触维持与更新，将操作性能与手部几何结构和触觉反馈紧密关联。我们通过旋转进度、手指参与度以及指尖载荷，在低成本LEAP Hand的两种版本上——即拟人化和对称手指布局——研究这些关系。两只手均集成TacTip视觉触觉传感器，并采用共享的强化学习框架。仿真实验评估了12个未见物体上的全触觉、二值触觉及仅本体感觉观测；硬件实验则在多种手部姿态下对十个物体评估全触觉策略。在仿真中，与仅依赖本体感觉相比，全触觉观测使拟人化手的每回合平均归一化旋转量提高94.8%，对称手提高66.9%，同时具有更长的平均回合持续时间和更低的平均总指尖载荷。硬件接触测量显示，拟人化手中手指参与度更具差异性，而对称手各手指间的累积载荷分布更为均匀。总体而言，对称手实现了32.0%更高的平均旋转次数和25.8%更高的总旋转速率，同时操作持续时间更长。额外的硬件力记录显示，该布局的平均总指尖载荷降低了19.9%。这些发现将手指布局与接触组织和载荷分配相关联，并表明在两种仿真具身中，更丰富的触觉信息能够在较低平均载荷下支持更大的任务进展。
tldr: This paper compares two LEAP Hand morphologies with tactile sensing for in-hand object rotation, showing that full tactile feedback and hand geometry significantly improve rotation performance and load distribution in both simulation and hardware.
tldr_zh: 本文比较了两种带有触觉传感的LEAP手形态在手中物体旋转任务中的表现，表明完整的触觉反馈和手部几何结构在仿真和硬件中均显著提高了旋转性能和负载分布。

title: Robot Learning with Vision-Language-Action Models for Agricultural Manipulation
summary: Robotic manipulation in agricultural environments remains challenging due to variations in plant geometry, occlusion, and camera viewpoints. Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) and generalist robot policies offer a promising approach to addressing these challenges by learning manipulation behaviors from multimodal observations and language instructions. However, adapting these policies to agricultural tasks requires domain-specific demonstrations, which are costly and time-consuming to collect on physical robots. In this work, we develop a simulation-to-real robot-learning framework for agricultural reaching and grasping that integrates task-specific demonstration collection and pretrained policy adaptation. A MuJoCo-based agricultural environment is developed with diverse tomato plant structures to support demonstration collection and controlled evaluation. Expert demonstrations are collected through joystick teleoperation, with a low-level controller used to execute robot actions. Two pretrained generalist robot policies, Octo and $π_{0.5}$, are adapted using simulated demonstrations, followed by further fine-tuning on a physical Franka Research 3 manipulator using real-robot demonstrations. The adapted policies are evaluated under in-distribution, viewpoint/spatial-shift, and out-of-distribution conditions in simulation, followed by physical-robot experiments. The influence of proprioceptive information on policy performance is also investigated. Results show that $π_{0.5}$ achieves higher task-performance scores than Octo and exhibits less degradation under distribution shifts. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating pretrained generalist policies with task-specific demonstration learning for agricultural manipulation.
summary_zh: 农业环境中的机器人操作因植物几何形态差异、遮挡以及相机视角变化而依然面临挑战。预训练视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型及通用机器人策略通过从多模态观测和语言指令中学习操作行为，为应对这些挑战提供了一种有前景的途径。然而，将这些策略适配到农业任务中需要领域特定的示范数据，而在实体机器人上采集此类数据成本高昂且耗时。在本研究中，我们开发了一个面向农业抓取与操作任务的仿真到现实机器人学习框架，整合了任务特定示范采集与预训练策略适配。我们基于MuJoCo构建了一个包含多样化番茄植株结构的农业仿真环境，以支持示范采集和受控评估。专家示范通过摇杆遥操作采集，并使用底层控制器执行机器人动作。两种预训练通用机器人策略Octo和$π_{0.5}$利用仿真示范进行适配，随后在物理Franka Research 3机械臂上结合真实机器人示范进行进一步微调。适配后的策略在仿真环境中分别于分布内、视角/空间偏移及分布外条件下进行评估，随后开展实体机器人实验。此外，还研究了本体感知信息对策略性能的影响。结果表明，$π_{0.5}$在任务性能得分上优于Octo，并且在分布偏移下表现出更小的性能退化。这些发现证明了将预训练通用策略与任务特定示范学习相结合用于农业操作的潜力。
tldr: This paper presents a simulation-to-real framework for adapting pretrained VLA policies (Octo and π0.5) to agricultural reaching and grasping, demonstrating that π0.5 outperforms Octo under distribution shifts in both simulated and physical robot experiments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于农业抓取任务的仿真到现实的机器人学习框架，通过微调预训练VLA策略（Octo和π0.5），证明π0.5在分布偏移下比Octo更鲁棒。

title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
summary: Robotic value models assess task execution from visual observations and instructions, providing feedback for policy learning and execution monitoring. However, existing evaluations cover only selected aspects of execution understanding, leaving the reliability of value feedback insufficiently tested. We introduce RoboValue, a fine-grained sim-and-real benchmark for unified evaluation of robotic value models. Its framework evaluates four complementary capability dimensions through shared interfaces: task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure and recovery reasoning, and value consistency. Diagnostic trajectories and instruction variations test whether value judgments accurately reflect task requirements and changes throughout execution. RoboValue-Dataset covers 15 simulation and 20 real-world manipulation tasks, providing expert demonstrations for training and annotated trajectories for fine-grained evaluation. We evaluate representative robotic value models in zero-shot and one-shot settings under standard conditions and separate shifts in robot embodiment and environment. Our results reveal errors in fine-grained instruction grounding, history-dependent progress tracking, and recovery assessment, even in models with strong outcome and forward-progress scores. The same semantic subtask can also receive substantially different value gains across valid execution orders. These findings identify concrete targets for value supervision, while the dataset and public leaderboard support continued assessment of feedback reliability. The website is available at https://robovalue-benchmark.github.io/.
summary_zh: 机器人价值模型通过视觉观察和指令评估任务执行情况，为策略学习和执行监控提供反馈。然而，现有评估仅覆盖执行理解的若干特定方面，导致价值反馈的可靠性尚未得到充分检验。我们提出RoboValue，一个用于机器人价值模型统一评估的细粒度仿真与真实世界基准测试。其框架通过共享接口评估四个互补的能力维度：任务状态理解、时间进度监控、失败与恢复推理，以及价值一致性。诊断性轨迹和指令变体用于测试价值判断是否准确反映任务要求及执行过程中的变化。RoboValue数据集涵盖15个仿真任务和20个真实世界操作任务，提供专家示范用于训练，并提供带标注的轨迹用于细粒度评估。我们在标准条件下以及机器人具身和环境分别发生偏移的情况下，对代表性机器人价值模型进行了零样本和单样本设置下的评估。结果表明，即使在具有较强结果预测和前向进度评分的模型中，仍存在细粒度指令接地、历史依赖进度跟踪和恢复评估方面的错误。同一语义子任务在不同有效执行顺序下也可能获得显著不同的价值增益。这些发现为价值监督提供了具体目标，同时数据集和公开排行榜支持对反馈可靠性的持续评估。网站地址：https://robovalue-benchmark.github.io/。
tldr: RoboValue is a new benchmark for evaluating robotic value models, covering task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure/recovery reasoning, and value consistency across simulated and real manipulation tasks. The benchmark reveals significant shortcomings in current models, such as weak instruction grounding and history-dependent progress tracking.
tldr_zh: RoboValue 是一个用于评估机器人价值模型的新基准，涵盖任务状态理解、时间进度监控、故障与恢复推理以及价值一致性，跨越仿真和真实操作任务。该基准揭示了当前模型在细粒度指令理解和历史依赖进度跟踪等方面的明显不足。

title: Learning Wheel Motion Uncertainty for Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry on Quadrupedal Wheel-Legged Robots
summary: Wheel kinematics can support odometry for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots when LiDAR geometry provides weak motion constraints. However, slip and contact loss make rolling predictions unreliable, and contact state alone cannot determine their reliability across motion directions. We propose a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework that retains analytical rolling predictions and learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history. The estimator maintains moving wheel-center states, allowing the learned uncertainty to regulate the influence of rolling predictions through forward-kinematic corrections. Degeneracy-aware projection (DAP) complements this mechanism by suppressing LiDAR constraints along geometrically weak directions. The learned covariance network (CovNet) is trained through a differentiable filter using simulated velocity supervision and deployed on the real robot without fine-tuning. On the six room sequences with the highest degeneracy ratios in our indoor dataset, the method reduces mean per-sequence position root mean square error (RMSE) by 66.2% relative to FAST-LIO2 and by 31.0% relative to a fixed-covariance variant. In a severely degenerate corridor run, it achieves an endpoint position error of 0.198 m, compared with 7.531 m for FAST-LIO2. These results demonstrate robust odometry under challenging geometric and wheel-motion conditions. We plan to publicly release our code and multimodal dataset. Project website: https://weihairuo.github.io/wheel-motion-uncertainty/
summary_zh: 轮式运动学可在激光雷达几何结构提供较弱运动约束时，为四足轮腿机器人的里程计提供支撑。然而，打滑和接触丢失会使滚动预测不可靠，且仅凭接触状态无法判断其在各运动方向上的可信度。我们提出一种紧耦合的激光雷达-惯性-运动学里程计框架，该框架保留了解析滚动预测，并从本体感觉历史中学习每个轮子、方向相关的过程协方差。该估计器维护移动轮心状态，使学习得到的不确定性能够通过正向运动学修正调节滚动预测的影响。退化感知投影（DAP）通过沿几何弱约束方向抑制激光雷达约束，对该机制形成补充。学习得到的协方差网络（CovNet）通过可微分滤波器在仿真速度监督下训练，并无需微调即可部署于真实机器人。在我们室内数据集中退化率最高的六个房间序列上，该方法相比FAST-LIO2将每序列平均位置均方根误差（RMSE）降低了66.2%，相比固定协方差变体降低了31.0%。在一次严重退化的走廊运行中，该方法实现终点位置误差为0.198 m，而FAST-LIO2为7.531 m。这些结果证明了该方法在具有挑战性的几何与轮式运动条件下的鲁棒里程计性能。我们计划公开代码和多模态数据集。项目网站：https://weihairuo.github.io/wheel-motion-uncertainty/
tldr: This paper proposes a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots that learns per-wheel, direction-dependent covariance from proprioceptive history to handle wheel slip and contact loss, combined with degeneracy-aware projection to suppress unreliable LiDAR constraints, achieving significant position error reduction in degenerate environments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种四足轮腿机器人的紧耦合LiDAR-惯性-运动学里程计框架，通过从本体感觉历史中学习每轮方向相关协方差来处理打滑和接触丢失，并结合退化感知投影抑制不可靠的LiDAR约束，在退化环境中显著降低位置误差。

title: ReInsVLN: Revisiting Historical Evidence for Training-Free Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) relies on retaining and using relevant observations. Yet growing histories introduce redundancy, and retained information may remain underused. We introduce ReInsBench, a diagnostic benchmark that examines history utilization through controlled continuation trials. Its results show that history-review reinstruction can recover navigation failures using the existing task context. Motivated by this finding, we propose ReInsVLN, a training-free framework supporting memory construction and utilization in frozen navigators. Coverage- and Instruction-Aware Compression constructs compact visual context through temporal redundancy reduction, coverage-aware protection, and instruction-guided token selection. Forgetting-Inspired History Reminders guide navigators to revisit retained observations according to a predefined schedule, without additional model calls. On R2R Val-Unseen, ReInsVLN improves success rates by 8.48 and 3.37 percentage points over the native StreamVLN and InternVLA-N1, reaching 64.27% and 64.44%, respectively. Visual compression largely preserves navigation performance while reducing prefill latency and KV cache memory by up to 21.77% and 32.25%, respectively, on matched observation workloads. Real-world trials on humanoid and quadruped robots further support the applicability of ReInsVLN to sequential instruction following and ordinal navigation.
summary_zh: 视觉与语言导航（VLN）依赖于对相关观察信息的保留与使用。然而，不断增长的历史数据引入了冗余，且已保留的信息可能未被充分利用。我们提出了ReInsBench，一个通过受控延续试验来检验历史利用情况的诊断基准。其结果表明，基于历史回顾的重新指令可以利用现有任务上下文修复导航失败。受此发现启发，我们提出了ReInsVLN，一个无需训练、支持在冻结导航器中构建和利用记忆的框架。覆盖与指令感知压缩通过时间冗余削减、覆盖感知保护和指令引导的令牌选择构建紧凑的视觉上下文。基于遗忘机制的历史提醒按照预定计划引导导航器重新审视已保留的观察信息，而无需额外的模型调用。在R2R Val-Unseen上，ReInsVLN相较于原生StreamVLN和InternVLA-N1，成功率分别提升了8.48和3.37个百分点，达到64.27%和64.44%。在匹配的观察负载下，视觉压缩在基本保持导航性能的同时，分别将预填充延迟和KV缓存内存降低了最高21.77%和32.25%。在仿人机器人和四足机器人上的真实世界试验进一步支持了ReInsVLN在顺序指令跟随和序列导航中的适用性。
tldr: ReInsVLN is a training-free framework that improves vision-and-language navigation by compressing visual history and scheduling memory revisits, showing gains on R2R and real-robot trials.
tldr_zh: ReInsVLN 是一个无需训练的框架，通过压缩视觉历史和安排记忆重访来提升视觉语言导航性能，在 R2R 和真实机器人实验中均取得改进。

title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
summary: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%.
